title: Biodiversity and the Conferences of the Parties
abstract: In a year containing summits from the three United Nations environmental frameworks, we consider how cooperation across the Conferences of the Parties (COPs) can facilitate implementation and impact. Co-timed with the start of the biodiversity COP, we highlight the reciprocal relationship between climate change and biodiversity.

title: Political affiliation impacts climate attention and choice beyond extreme weather exposure
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Political polarization and increasing exposure to extreme weather can shape public engagement with climate change, yet the underlying psychological mechanisms remain unclear. In this Registered Report, we examine how political affiliation, extreme weather exposure and subjective attribution influence climate-relevant information search and decision-making in a US sample (
                    N
                     = 1,451). We combined a process-tracing paradigm within an incentivized decision task involving real carbon emissions with objective data on extreme weather exposure. Democrats attended more to carbon emission information and made more pro-climate choices than Republicans, with no evidence of moderation by objective extreme weather exposure. The subjective attribution of extreme weather to climate change was associated with greater attention to carbon information, more pro-climate choices and moderated the effects of exposure on both outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of political affiliation in climate-relevant decision-making and suggest that extreme weather effects depend less on exposure itself than on how these experiences are interpreted.

title: Climate choices and attention are shaped more by politics than weather
abstract: Climate change will further increase the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events. Subjective experience and attribution of extreme weather events to climate change, rather than objective exposure alone, are associated with greater climate-relevant attention and choices. Political affiliation influences attention and behaviour irrespective of subjective attribution and objective exposure.

title: Astrid Schomaker on biodiversity in a triple COP year

title: Graphite from Mars
Millisecond phonon lifetimes in piezoelectric nanomechanical resonators
abstract: Piezoelectric nanomechanical resonators operating at gigahertz frequencies are a promising platform for quantum information processing and precision sensing, but phonon lifetimes have been limited to the microsecond range, widely attributed to the higher intrinsic loss of piezoelectric materials. Here we show that this limitation is not fundamental. Using a fabrication process informed by recent studies of defect-mediated loss in lithium niobate, we combine the chemical restoration of ion-milled surfaces with a shadow-mask metallization process to produce lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators with inferred internal phonon lifetimes of up to 21 ms at 3.6 GHz, corresponding to quality factors exceeding 4 × 108 (f × Qi > 1018) at millikelvin temperatures. By systematically varying the electrode-to-resonator spacing, we demonstrate that the measured lifetime is set by external coupling between the device and measurement circuit rather than material loss. This establishes that lithium niobate, once fabrication-induced surface damage is removed, achieves an intrinsic quality comparable with the best mechanical materials while remaining an intrinsically piezoelectric platform with strong electromechanical coupling.

title: Unidirectional rotation in a molecular motor driven by angular-momentum transfer via helical orbitals
abstract: The generation of unidirectional motion has been a long-standing challenge in the engineering of molecular motors and, more generally, machines. A molecular motor is characterized by a set of low-energy states that differ in their configuration, that is, position or rotation. In biology and Feringa-type motors, unidirectional motion is driven by excitation of the molecule into a high-energy transitional state followed by a directional relaxation back to a low-energy state. Directionality is created by a steric hindrance to movement along one of the directions on the path from the excited state back to a low-energy state. Here we showcase a principal mechanism for the generation of unidirectional rotation of a molecule without the need for steric hindrance and transitional excited states. The chemical design of the molecule-consisting of a platform, an upright axle and a chiral rotor moiety-enables a rotation mechanism that relies on the transfer of orbital angular momentum from the driving current to the rotor. The transfer is mediated via orbital currents that are carried by helical orbitals in the axle.

title: Stereochemical preorganization directs triple-helical assembly of Au4 nanoclusters
abstract: Programming hierarchical helicity from molecular stereochemistry remains a major challenge in synthetic materials. Collagen achieves this through conformational preorganization that translates local stereochemical information into homochiral triple helices, a level of hierarchical control rarely realized in artificial systems. Here we show that atomically precise Au4 nanoclusters encode local stereochemical information into a homochiral triple helix through a collagen-inspired assembly mechanism. A configuration-dependent endo-exo puckering of thiazolidine-2-thione ligands acts as a stereochemical switch, controlling metal-site exposure and biasing Au···Au metallophilic interactions. This intrachain preorganization fixes the torsional geometry of single helices, which then cooperatively braid into left-handed and right-handed triple helices, respectively. Systematic steric modulation redirects the assembly into alternative architectures, demonstrating programmable control over helicity. The triple-helical superstructures exhibit amplified chiroptical responses. These results establish a transferable molecular grammar for hierarchical helicity in metal nanoclusters and identify metallophilicity as a design principle for biomimetic materials.

title: Elevating CO2 electrolyzer temperature accelerates the viability of chemical electrification
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Climate change mitigation has spurred interest in producing chemicals from CO
                    2
                    . CO
                    2
                    reduction by electrochemistry can be driven directly by green electricity, yielding even multi-carbon (C2+) products. However, the resulting processes still suffer from high electrolyzer losses and substantial energy demands. This study evaluates the environmental and economic benefits of integrating optimized electrolyzers into complete processes. For CO
                    2
                    electroreduction to ethylene and dimerization to 1-butene, elevated-temperature electrolysis effectively utilizes waste heat. Challenging the ambient-temperature paradigm, this strategy achieves system-wide savings in energy (10%), climate impacts (9%) and overall cost (11%). Generalizing these findings across various CO
                    2
                    electroreduction pathways identifies energy savings of up to 25% and the heating system as a key design variable affecting electrolyzer design targets. Our study demonstrates how process integration can guide CO
                    2
                    electrolyzer development toward sustainable processes.

title: Bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnets enable untethered organ monitoring
abstract: Metal-free molecular magnets differ from conventional magnetic devices that predominantly rely on metallic magnets as these metal-free materials may offer biocompatibility and bioresorbability. However, existing molecular materials lack the ferromagnetic strength required for high-fidelity sensing at clinically relevant tissue depths. Here we introduce a bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnet derived from graphitic carbon nitride, combining metallic-level ferromagnetism with full bioresorbability. De-nitrogenation creates spin centres coupled through a reconstructed π-σ conjugated framework, conferring robust spontaneous magnetization that remains stable under physiological conditions. Integrated with poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) and silk fibroin, the material forms catheter-deliverable epicardial patches for cardiac tracking and can also be dispersed in injectable hydrogels for organ-scale sensing, including the three-dimensional reconstruction of localized hepatic pathologies. Coupled with a skin-interfaced Hall array, this magnetic sensing architecture provides the continuous, untethered monitoring of multi-organ dynamics, robust against motion artifacts and tissue impedance. In porcine models, it facilitates the continuous assessment of ejection fraction over 4 weeks, followed by benign bioresorption. Benchmarked against standard-of-care echocardiography, this approach delivers clinical-grade trajectories, supporting longitudinal, infrastructure-independent physiological monitoring.

title: Supramolecular chemical ligation of helical polymers
abstract: Chemical ligation of polymer segments is an essential approach to extend the length of synthetic polymers. Ligating individual polymer chains at the molecular level remains a formidable challenge owing to the entropically disfavoured collision probability between reactive end groups, and the need to overcome the activation barrier. Here we report a pathway to chemical ligation of synthetic polymers via folding-driven supramolecular polymerization followed by dynamic covalent polycondensation. Our strategy, which does not require thermal activation, uses hydrogen bonds that induce conformational folding to rigidify the polymer backbone while providing sticky ends for supramolecular pre-organization. This promotes base-catalysed covalent exchange between terminal groups (in our case, thiolate-disulfide groups). We obtain mechanistic insight in the ligation process by engineering side-chain units that determine conformational foldability and intermolecular H-bonding pre-organization. The resulting extended helical polymers fold into hierarchical globular architectures in solution and exhibit thermo-responsive macromolecular entanglements in bulk films. The combination of noncovalent assembly and dynamic covalent polymerization offers a supramolecular pathway for non-thermal and controllable polycondensation of dynamic polymers with secondary structures.

title: Stacking-specific two-dimensional In2Se3 for ferroelectric homojunctions
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectric semiconductors offer unique opportunities for ultrathin non-volatile memory and neuromorphic devices, yet the role of stacking order in intrinsic ferroelectric systems remains largely unexplored. Here we report the stacking-controlled growth of large-area 2D β'- and α-In2Se3 with distinct 2H and 3R configurations through chemical vapour deposition by regulating selenium kinetics and strain relaxation. By combining atomic-resolution microscopy, non-linear optical characterization and first-principles calculations, we uncover a strong correlation between stacking order and ferroelectric behaviour: β'-In2Se3 undergoes an antiferroelectric-to-paraelectric transition when switching from 2H to 3R stacking, whereas in α-In2Se3, in-plane ferroelectric polarization vanishes during the 3R-to-2H transition. We further achieve the controlled synthesis of 2H/3R ferroelectric homojunctions and directly visualize polarization-dependent interfacial potential barriers using differential phase-contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy. The engineered homojunctions exhibit switchable band alignment and tunable carrier transport, yielding memristors with significantly reduced switching voltages and an on/off ratio of ∼2.6 × 104, approximately one order of magnitude higher than devices based on single-stacking α-In2Se3. These findings establish stacking order as a powerful structural parameter for tailoring ferroelectricity in 2D materials and introduce stacking-engineered polymorphic heterogeneity as a versatile platform for high-performance ferroelectric electronics and memory technologies.

title: Directed assembly of cathode interlayers enables efficient binary organic solar cells
abstract:
Abstract
                  Cathode interlayers create interfacial dipoles in organic solar cells to maximize device efficiency. However, the dipoles are highly dependent on the molecular orientation of the interlayers, which remain challenging to be controlled. Here, based on the amphiphilic nature of the interlayers, we show a stepwise film deposition approach using a polar solvent for active layer pretreatment and a bipolar solvent for subsequent interlayer self assembly. Sum-frequency generation vibrational spectroscopy reveals a preferred perpendicular orientation of the interlayer molecules, thereby enhancing the surface potential and reducing the charge transport resistance. As a result, we achieve a certified efficiency of 20.65% and fill factor of 82.7% in binary organic solar cells. This method is universally applicable to different cathode interlayers and active layers. Our work highlights the importance of controlling interlayer molecular orientation for unlocking significant performance gains, paving the way for further advancements in device optimization.

title: Interhalogen of Iodine Chloride Accelerates Charge Transfer for Efficient Li2O2 Oxidation in Lithium–Oxygen Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Li–O2 batteries suffer from sluggish Li2O2 oxidation kinetics at electrode/electrolyte interfaces, leading to large charge polarization and low energy efficiency. Soluble redox mediators (RMs) provide a solution-mediated pathway for Li2O2 decomposition and reduce the charge overpotential. However, the chemical oxidation of Li2O2 by oxidized RMs remains kinetically sluggish, resulting in persistent charge polarization. Herein, iodine monochloride (ICl), an interhalogen compound, is electrochemically generated in situ during the charge process to promote the oxidation of Li2O2. The large electronegativity difference between I and Cl promotes intramolecular charge transfer from I to Cl, creating an electrophilic iodine center (Iδ+) that increases the I–Cl bond polarity and strengthens the interaction with Li2O2. This lowers the decomposition barrier of Li2O2 from 2.39 to 0.77 eV, thereby facilitating its chemical oxidation. The Li–O2 battery delivers a low discharge/charge polarization of 0.52 V, effectively mitigating parasitic reactions at high voltages and enabling an extended cycling lifespan exceeding 800 h. This work provides a valuable design principle for developing redox mediators for efficient Li2O2 oxidation.

title: Fluorine-Mediated Molten-Salt Crystallization Regulates Phase Evolution and Structural Stability in Sodium Layered Oxides
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ni- and Co-free P2-type Fe–Mn layered oxides with high Na concentrations are promising cathodes for sodium-ion batteries, but their practical use is limited by phase instability during Na-excess synthesis and structural degradation during cycling and storage. Although large single-crystal-like architectures could improve stability, controlled phase-selective crystallization in these cathode systems remains challenging. Here, we show that fluorine-assisted molten-salt synthesis enables controlled formation of large-particle Fe–Mn–Ti P2 cathodes with enhanced phase selectivity and structural coherence. Compared with Na-excess processing alone, NaF-assisted flux growth expands the P2 phase stability window and promotes large particles with uniform morphologies while preserving local layered ordering. Multiscale characterization further reveals more-reversible structural evolution and more homogeneous Mn redox behavior in the NaF-assisted material, together with a gradient-like fluorine distribution involving surface-enriched NaF-like species and lower level interior fluorine environments. These coupled structural, morphological, and chemical features collectively mitigate crack formation and deliver good cycling stability. In summary, NaF-assisted molten-salt synthesis shows promise in addressing key limitations of Ni- and Co-free P2-type Fe–Mn layered cathodes.

title: A Microporous Zr-Tetraphosphonate MOF with Permanent Porosity, Robustness, and Thermochemical Heat Storage Capability
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Combining high-valent metal cations with phosphonate linkers represents a promising strategy to address the limited stability of MOFs, yet permanently porous phosphonate MOFs (P-MOFs) remain rare due to the strong coordination propensity of phosphonate groups. Herein, we report IEF-10, a new microporous zirconium tetraphosphonate framework constructed from ZrO5F octahedral secondary building units and a pyrene tetraphosphonate linker. The material combines three features that are seldom achieved simultaneously in P-MOFs: permanent accessible microporosity (equivalent BET surface area ∼430 m2·g–1), accessible phosphonic acid functionalities (-PO3H), and exceptional thermal (up to 450 °C), mechanical (>3 tons), and chemical stability (pH 1–12, organic solvents). The structure exhibits reversible water adsorption with moderate uptake and experimentally determined capacities of heat storage of ∼400–500 J·g–1, reflecting a favorable balance between host–guest interactions and regeneration requirements. As a proof of concept, IEF-10 was evaluated for thermochemical heat storage under dynamic moist-gas flow conditions. Calorimetric measurements revealed fast heat-release kinetics (3–4 h), and excellent cyclability in terms of heat release (at least 10 cycles, total test duration of 5 weeks). The hydrophobic surface character is an advantage for long-term storage uses as the adsorbent can remain in a dry state between the charging and discharging stages even at low relative humidity levels in the reactor. These results demonstrate how the combination of permanent porosity, accessible phosphonic acid groups, and exceptional framework robustness can enable functional adsorption-driven energy storage while providing new opportunities for the development of porous zirconium P-MOFs.

title: Energy Deposition Timescale Controls Chemistry in Pulsed Methane Plasmas
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nonoxidative methane conversion offers a promising route for the coproduction of hydrogen and value-added hydrocarbons without CO2 emissions. Among emerging approaches, pulsed plasmas can provide potential advantages by enabling high energy deposition, rapid quenching, and generation of active nonthermal species. This work systematically investigates how pulsed energy deposition from nanosecond-to-millisecond time scales (10 to 50 mJ/pulse) influences methane plasma characteristics (electron density and gas temperature), reaction mechanisms, conversion, and energy efficiency. Nanosecond discharges produced the highest overall C2 selectivity (>70%), with up to 20% for C2H4; in this regime, methane dissociation proceeded through both electron-impact and thermal dissociation, whereas longer pulses were predominantly thermal. Pulsed plasma conversion was similar to thermal arcs (∼377 kJ/mol CH4) and specific energy requirements to produce C2H2 and H2 were 15 kWh/kg and 40 kWh/kg, respectively, in 100 μs long discharges. The product distribution was largely determined by thermal processes involving dehydrogenation reactions (Kassel’s reaction scheme). High gas temperatures preferentially favored C2H2 formation over C2H4, and C2H4 selectivity decreased with increasing pulse width. Overall, these results demonstrate that pulse width and energy can be used to tailor hydrocarbon selectivity and can help design pulsed plasma systems for efficient production of value-added hydrocarbons and hydrogen.

title: Energy shocks, firm resilience, and policy responses: Evidence from the 2022 crisis*
abstract: The 2022 energy price shock, triggered by geopolitical disruptions, prompted governments to implement widespread policy interventions to support firms and accelerate the energy transition. Using nationally representative firm surveys from the United States and Germany, this paper examines how firms adjusted to the shock and their reported responses to fiscal incentives. We document that firms were generally resilient, relying on a combination of price pass-through, margin adjustment, and energy-saving investments. Responses differed across countries: firms in Germany – facing a larger and more persistent shock – were more likely to invest in energy efficiency and reduce energy consumption, while firms in the United States primarily absorbed costs through lower profits. Evidence from input-output simulations suggests that, absent policy intervention, energy-intensive sectors would have faced substantially larger price pressures. We also find that firms with pre-existing plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions were more likely to report intending to utilize fiscal incentive programs, suggesting that policy targeting and credibility may play an important role in supporting the green transition. Overall, our findings provide descriptive evidence on firms’ responses to energy price shocks and announced policy measures, offering insights for the design of targeted and predictable energy and climate policies in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical environment.

title: A Pseudo-Icosahedral RhH2Au10 Superatom: Two Hydrogen Atoms Acting as Gold-Atom Equivalents and Modifiers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract A hydrogen atom is known to act as a gold-atom-equivalent dopant in gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) by contributing to the valence electron count. To gain insights into the interaction of multiple H atoms with AuNCs, we herein synthesized a di-H-atom-doped NC, [RhH2Au10(dppp)5]3+ (RhH2Au10; dppp = 1,3-bis(diphenylphosphino)propane), by exposing [RhAu10(dppp)5]3+ (RhAu10) to H2 gas; RhAu10 was generated in situ via hydride (H–) abstraction from [RhHAu10(dppp)5]2+. Comprehensive characterization of RhH2Au10 by X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations revealed that the two H atoms occupy the two “missing” Au sites in the arachno-type RhAu10 core via dissociative adsorption of H2, forming a pseudo-icosahedral RhH2Au10 core. This core structure contrasts sharply with the previously reported di-H-atom-doped silver- or copper-based superatoms, in which the H atoms form an MH2 (M = Os, Ru, Rh) unit completely encapsulated within an icosahedral Ag12 or Cu12 shell. The RhH2Au10 core possesses an 8-electron closed-shell electronic configuration of (1S)2(1P)6, which is isoelectronic to the icosahedral RhAu12 superatom, thereby demonstrating the Au-atom equivalence of H atoms. Nevertheless, the two H atoms in the RhH2Au10 superatomic core act as structural modifiers compared to the RhAu12 superatom: (1) the degeneracy of the 1P orbitals is lifted by lowering the geometric symmetry, and (2) the HOMO–LUMO energy gap is expanded due to the reduced electronic confinement volume. This study demonstrates that multiple H atoms in a gold-based superatomic core not only behave as Au-atom equivalents but also serve as key components for modulating their fundamental properties.

title: Layer-Distortion Engineering of Acridinium-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks Enables Efficient Photoredox Transformations of Alcohols
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Planar two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) often suffer from severe interlayer π–π stacking, which promotes excitonic recombination, restricts access to active sites, and compromises photocatalytic efficiency. Here we report a layer-distortion engineering strategy to construct wavy acridinium-based COFs, Mes-Acr-TAPB and Mes-Acr-TAPP, by introducing structural distortion into otherwise planar layered frameworks. The resulting wavy framework efficiently suppresses interlayer π–π stacking, enlarges interlayer spacing, modulates molecular packing, pore environment, and improves accessibility to photoactive acridinium sites. Compared with the planar analog Dur-Acr-TAPB, Mes-Acr-TAPB exhibits enhanced exciton dissociation along with substrate absorption, more efficient charge separation, and superior photocatalytic activity. As a heterogeneous photoredox catalyst, Mes-Acr-TAPB enables diverse alcohol transformations under mild conditions, including β-scission radical functionalization, ring contraction/expansion, and skeletal transposition. Mes-Acr-TAPB shows broad functional-group tolerance and supports late-stage structural modification of complex natural products, highlighting its synthetic utility. This work establishes layer-distortion as an effective design principle for mitigating interlayer stacking in 2D COFs and advancing high-performance COF photocatalysts for sustainable organic synthesis.

title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Slaked Lime Utilizing a Diaphragm Flow Cell
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Slaked lime (Ca(OH)2) is one of the most widely utilized chemicals, with applications in diverse industries including construction, mining, water treatment, and chemical manufacturing. Currently, Ca(OH)2 is synthesized by coal-fired calcination of CaCO3 to make CaO, followed by exothermic hydration. Converting CaCO3 into Ca(OH)2 using electrochemically generated acid and base has attracted great interest because it could be powered by renewable electricity and would generate the CO2 byproduct in a pure form. Previous electrochemical Ca(OH)2 syntheses have incorporated the processing of calcium salts within the electrochemical cell to avoid acid–base recombination losses, but these cells have poor stability and high energy demand. Herein, we show that production of high-salinity acid and base solutions using a diaphragm flow cell (DFC) coupled with ex situ processing of CaCO3 substantially improves the efficiency of electrochemical Ca(OH)2 production. Using a closed loop with a simple KCl salt solution, we demonstrate the synthesis of >99% pure Ca(OH)2 for 0.088 to 0.10 kWh per mole at productive current densities of 158 to 334 mA cm–2.

title: Efficient Chemical Synthesis and Enzymatic Replication of 3′-Deoxyapionucleic Acid (ApioNA): An RNA-Selective XNA with Conformational Flexibility
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Xeno-nucleic acids (XNAs) have emerged as versatile platforms due to their sugar scaffolds that enable precise chemical tuning, leading to distinct classes ranging from fully compatible systems to orthogonal systems. However, sugar-modified XNAs capable of discriminating between RNA and DNA have remained elusive. In this work, we establish 3′-deoxyapionucleic acid (ApioNA) as a structurally flexible XNA with inherent RNA-selective hybridization properties. We achieved efficient production of ApioNA oligonucleotides through an efficient asymmetric synthesis of their building blocks and systematically characterized their properties. Thermal melting analyses demonstrate that ApioNA forms moderately stable duplexes with RNA while exhibiting weak pairing with DNA and negligible self-association. Quantum mechanical calculations reveal that the apiofuranose ring populates two low-energy puckering states, and the addition of an extra methylene group enhances backbone flexibility, thereby favoring A-form geometry for RNA pairing while requiring a higher-energy state to accommodate B-form DNA. Despite its weak affinity for DNA, ApioNA supports a complete enzymatic replication cycle using commercial Therminator and Bst 3.0 polymerases with approximately 98% fidelity and is processed by native E. coli machinery in vivo. This work fills the RNA-selective niche in the XNA functional landscape and establishes sugar puckering dynamics and backbone flexibility as key design principles for programming nucleic acid pairing specificity.

title: Monolayer photonic-crystal manganese halide gel scintillator for full-vision imaging
abstract: A monolayer photonic crystal integrated with a transparent manganese halide gel scintillator enhances the extraction of X-ray-excited light while preserving high spatial resolution. By combining X-ray computed tomography with structured-light scanning, the system enables a unified, spatially registered three-dimensional visualization of internal structures and external geometry.

title: A region-aware field reliability prediction method for power batteries under heterogeneous conditions using improved deep clustering
abstract: Power batteries, as core components of new energy systems, exhibit significant regional variability in field reliability under heterogeneous operating conditions. However, accurate prediction of region-specific reliability remains challenging due to the scarcity of comprehensive field failure data across diverse regions and the homogeneity assumptions commonly adopted in existing regional reliability modeling. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel region-aware field reliability prediction method for power batteries under heterogeneous conditions, leveraging an improved deep clustering algorithm. First, environmental factors and a macro-level socioeconomic covariate associated with regional field reliability are systematically analyzed and identified, and a dynamic panel dataset is constructed. Mutual information is employed to quantify their statistical associations with regional field reliability. Second, an improved Transformer-based multi-kernel ensemble spectral clustering (TMESC) algorithm is developed to enable intelligent regional classification driven by heterogeneity in observed regional characteristics. Third, based on the derived regional clusters and available failure data from observed regions, a nonlinear mapping model is developed to quantitatively link field reliability with regional characteristics, facilitating accurate prediction of field reliability in unobserved regions. Experimental results show that, guided by TMESC clustering, the proposed method estimates power battery failure rates and has accurate predictive ability at the regional aggregate scale, improving regional reliability assessment and providing support for data-driven warranty and maintenance strategies.

title: Online probabilistic early warning for power system dynamic congestion events with enhanced trustworthiness
abstract: The development of renewables and electricity demand induces the growth of inter-area power transfer of power systems, potentially causing dynamic congestion events (DCEs) of transmission interfaces that threaten system stability and adequacy. The lack of procedures for perceiving real-time DCEs often leads to inadequate time for decision-making and resource mobilization. In this paper, a trustworthiness-enhanced learning approach is proposed for online probabilistic early warning (PEW) of DCEs, promoting the system proactivity in resisting risks. An explainable PEW network is first built utilizing tensorized neural blocks and tandem attention, enabling more explicit variable-wise information encoding. Next, an interface for static covariates is designed to fuse heterogeneous data and improve prediction performance. Then, an ensemble confidence calibrator is developed to modify the mapping between logits and congestion posterior probabilities via negative log-likelihood minimization, outputting more credible multi-class probability estimates. Test results verify the efficacy of the proposed trustworthiness-enhanced PEW method. By combining class predictions with calibrated probability estimations, more comprehensive decisions can be made.

title: Human-in-the-loop preference calibration for home energy management via LLM-enabled contract-constrained language interfaces
abstract: As residential energy systems become increasingly electrified and coordination-intensive, home energy management systems (HEMS) must operate economically while remaining aligned with evolving user-authorized comfort and service boundaries. Existing personalization approaches rely on questionnaire initialization, fixed preference parameters, or indirect behavioral corrections, limiting alignment under changing needs and the use of runtime natural-language feedback for long-horizon calibration. This paper proposes a large language model (LLM)-enabled human-in-the-loop framework that converts user utterances into authorization-aware, contract-constrained, machine-checkable events for downstream control and preference updating. The LLM is a contract-constrained semantic interface, not a direct controller. Explicit intents support bounded execution and direct profile correction, whereas vague feedback requires option negotiation and user confirmation before bounded updating. A Contract-Informed Preference Update (CIPU) mechanism combines structured interaction evidence with projection and trust-region stabilization, while model predictive control remains the safety-constrained execution layer. In simulations, the proposed method reduces normalized preference distance by 22.50% and complaints by 74.46% relative to Survey MPC across three role-conditioned profiles. On a controlled 188-utterance language-interface benchmark, the proposed interface achieves 100% structured-event exact match and a 0% parser-level false direct-execution rate. Closed-loop ablations show 59.40% fewer complaints than the explicit-only variant, while event-log auditing of the no-contract-gate variant yields a 36.90% event-interface mismatch rate after gate removal. Under mid-horizon preference drift, final preference mismatch is reduced by 44.09% on average and up to 71.43% relative to Survey MPC.

title: Sugar-Based 1-Dimensional Metal–Organic Chalcogenolates with Hydration-Tunable Chiroptical Emission
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chiral topology in semiconductors introduces a structural degree of freedom for tuning the chiroptical, excitonic, and spintronic behavior. In metal–organic chalcogenolates (MOChas) semiconductors, how ligand stereochemistry and supramolecular organization influence chiral topology, and thus optical and excitonic responses, remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate intrinsic circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) in sugar-based 1-dimensional MOChas, with structures solved via small-molecule serial femtosecond crystallography. These materials exhibit blue and green CPLs, arising from the chiral inorganic core. Despite the close chemical similarity between the glucose- and galactose-derived ligands, we observed dramatic differences in their inorganic structure. Silver glucosethiolate shows reversible hydration-driven photoluminescence switching with a hydration-linked emission energy. Labile water molecules in the glucose-based system correlate with a blueshift in excitonic emission. Our results suggest a new direction in the search for chirophotonic hybrid semiconductors, exploiting intrinsically chiral topologies and excitonic optical frequencies, which are sensitively modulated by ligand identity and supramolecular interactions.

title: Synthetic W/Cu Mimics of the Mo/Cu Active Site in Aerobic CODH: Nonclassical Isocyanide Coordination and the Role of the Bridging Sulfide
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aerobic carbon monoxide dehydrogenase (CODH) uses an unsupported Mo–S–Cu heterobimetallic active site to catalyze CO oxidation, but the mechanistic role of the bridging sulfide remains to be fully resolved. We report a series of W/Cu complexes designed to test whether steric shielding from a bidentate tBuxantphos ligand can suppress unwanted Cu···Sdithiolate and Cu···O═M interactions that plagued the reactivity of a previously reported NHC-ligated model system. Addition of [Cu(tBuxantphos)]+ to [(bdt)WVI(O)(OSiiPr3)(X)]− (bdt = 1,2-benzenedithiolate; X = O, S, Se) unexpectedly favors Cu coordination at the W═O rather than the W═X unit, giving X═W–O–Cu cores as the thermodynamically preferred isomers, opposite to the connectivity predicted by hard–soft acid–base theory and found in CODH itself. The resulting complexes bind isocyanides at CuI with nonclassical (blue-shifted) C≡N stretching frequencies. In contrast, no reactivity is observed toward CO gas, consistent with DFT predictions that CO coordination is endergonic. However, the calculations reveal that the CO adduct of the hypothetical O═W–S–Cu–CO isomer is more stabilized than its S═W–O–Cu–CO counterpart, an effect traced by molecular orbital analysis to delocalization of electron density from the redox-active dithiolate through the bridging sulfide into the Cu–CO π-backbonding manifold. These results provide an electronic rather than purely structural rationale for why the CODH active site retains a bridging sulfide despite an apparent thermodynamic preference for a bridging oxo in the synthetic analogues investigated here.

title: Crossover from Asymmetric to Symmetric Electrowetting Linked to Double-Layer Restructuring
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Voltage-controlled wetting at solid–liquid interfaces is central to the performance of a range of electrochemical and microfluidic technologies, yet the molecular basis of polarity-dependent electrowetting remains unresolved. Classical electrocapillarity predicts a symmetric dependence of contact angle on applied potential, but experiments and simulations frequently exhibit pronounced asymmetry. Here, combining electrowetting measurements with atomistic simulations, we show that asymmetric wetting at aqueous carbon interfaces arises from the structure of the electrical double layer. By investigating aqueous KF and LiCl electrolytes at graphitic interfaces across lower concentration and water-in-salt regimes, we identify a crossover from strongly asymmetric electrowetting at lower concentration to a symmetric response at high concentration for KF, while LiCl retains a pronounced asymmetry. This transition is accompanied by corresponding changes in the solid–liquid interfacial tension, demonstrating that polarity-dependent wetting can arise from voltage-dependent molecular restructuring of the interfacial liquid, which modifies the interfacial thermodynamics, without invoking faradaic processes. We introduce interfacial connectivity, defined by the network of intermolecular interactions within the first adsorption layer, as a molecular descriptor linking double-layer structure to macroscopic wetting behavior. These results demonstrate that electrolyte-controlled electrowetting can recover the symmetric electrocapillary limit under appropriate conditions and establish a unified framework connecting double-layer structure, interfacial free energy, and voltage-dependent wetting.

title: Sky-Blue Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence from a Zirconium(IV) Complex
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Earth-abundant early transition-metal complexes with luminescent ligand-to-metal charge-transfer (LMCT) excited states remain an attractive yet underexplored alternative to widely used precious-metal emitters. A fundamental understanding of the molecular design principles governing the photophysical properties of LMCT emitters is critical to further developing cost-effective and sustainable photochemical applications using this compound class. Here, we report the synthesis of a novel bis(4,5-ditolylamido-9,9-dimethylxanthene)zirconium complex, Zr(TolXDA)2, that shows efficient photoluminescence due to thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) at room temperature. Steady-state and time-resolved spectroscopic studies at room temperature reveal highly efficient and long-lived emission in the sky-blue and green wavelength range for solid samples (λPL = 480 nm, ΦPL = 0.60, τPL = 4–14 μs) and THF solutions (λPL = 548 nm, ΦPL = 0.30, τPL = 8 μs) of Zr(TolXDA)2, respectively. Despite the relatively large singlet–triplet energy gap (ΔEST ≥ 0.26 eV), TADF emission in Zr(TolXDA)2 is unambiguously confirmed by temperature-dependent emission studies. This is likely facilitated by the high LMCT character of the S1 and T1 states, a consequence of strategic ligand design, which allows for rapid forward and reverse intersystem crossing. This hypothesis is supported by femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, which confirms facile forward and reverse intersystem crossing in Zr(TolXDA)2 (τISC = 15 ± 5 ps, τrISC = 0.48 ± 0.39 μs), and TD-DFT calculations, which establish significant negative charge transfer to zirconium in the lowest energy excited states.

title: Decoupling Dissolution from Water Oxidation at Single-Faceted High-Entropy Perovskite Electrodes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract High-entropy oxides (HEOs) are promising anode materials for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) due to their wide compositional space and electronic flexibility. However, their electrochemical dissolution and OER remain concurrent, preventing decoupled analysis of dissolution kinetics and stability. Here, we present a combined atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) strategy to decouple lattice dissolution from water oxidation under well-defined reaction conditions. Structurally analogous, atomically flat, single-faceted (001) ABO3 perovskite electrodes, La1–xSrx(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2)O3 with x = 0 and 0.3, serve as model systems to probe dissolution and OER kinetics in acid. Pipet-probed localized cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry reveal that the measured current contains contributions from both OER and lattice dissolution, the latter producing nanoscale dissolution pits beneath the SECCM droplet. By correlating pit-growth kinetics with total OER charge as a function of pulse duration (τ), overpotential (η), and pH, we quantitatively separate dissolution from OER. The proportional scaling between dissolution charge and total charge indicates that OER and dissolution proceed within a common kinetic regime, sharing a common intermediate. A rate-law-based analysis yields the standard dissolution rate constant (kd0 cm/s), transfer coefficient (α), and proton reaction order (b) for the dissolution of the 001 facet of both HEO-P. Our results unravel how aliovalent A-site substitution (30% Sr2+) alters dissolution kinetics, charge partitioning between dissolution and OER, and thickness-dependent stability, thereby enabling quantitative disentangling of the intrinsic activity and stability of HEO electrodes.

title: Intricate Proteoform Heterogeneity in the Tailpiece of IgA within and across Its Circulatory and Secretory Configurations
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Human immunoglobulin A (IgA) naturally occurs in multiple molecular forms─monomers, dimers, and even higher-order polymers─that are differentially distributed across serum, breast milk, and mucosal surfaces. The C-terminal tailpiece of IgA is essential to its polymerization mediated by the joining chain (J-chain) and thus also an important determinant of its extensive structural heterogeneity, yet its features remain somewhat poorly defined. Here, we used HILIC-LC-MS/MS-based glycopeptide analysis to characterize the N-glycan structures, disulfide linkages, and C-terminal amino acid sequence variants within the IgA tailpiece across the different molecular configurations of endogenous IgA. We find extensive correlation between these post-translational modifications; i.e., variations in tailpiece Asn459 N-glycosylation, redox status and disulfide connectivity of Cys471, and the presence or absence of C-terminal Tyr472 are intrinsically interconnected. When Cys471 was disulfide-bound to the J-chain, Asn459 glycans showed broader structural heterogeneity and retained more high-mannose structures, whereas free Cys471 tailpieces mainly carried mature, sialylated complex-type glycans. Serum IgA and milk SIgA displayed distinct tailpiece signatures, including differences in N-glycan maturation and processing of the ultimate C-terminal Tyr472 residue. Together, these findings define biofluid-specific molecular forms of IgA and highlight the remarkable structural diversity of the human IgA tailpiece. Overall, our results advance the understanding of the IgA structure and could offer a much-needed molecular basis to assist future bioengineering of IgA-based therapeutics.

title: Core–Shell Structures Govern Through-Space Interactions in Triblock Copolymers toward Deep-Red Clusteroluminescence
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Green fluorescent protein (GFP) and its derivatives have transformed biological imaging, yet fluorophores that simultaneously combine biocompatibility, structural programmability, and intrinsic long-wavelength luminescence remain scarce. Here, we develop a controllable one-pot polymerization strategy to construct nonconjugated triblock copolymers that can self-assemble into core–shell clusters. By modulating the hydrophilic–hydrophobic balance of copolymer chains, the core-to-shell ratio, chain packing, and electronic through-space interactions within the clusters can be precisely regulated, enabling tunable clusteroluminescence (CL) that extends to the deep-red and near-infrared emission region. Ultrafast spectroscopy further uncovers the excited-state dynamics of these core–shell clusters and reveals how the coupled evolution of electronic states and structures governs CL generation. Moreover, the core–shell clusters enable in vivo angiography under two-photon excitation, highlighting their potential as biocompatible nanofluorophores. These findings establish core–shell engineering as a general design principle for efficient clusteroluminogens, deepen the mechanistic understanding of CL, and pave the way for next-generation nanofluorescence technologies.

title: Modifier-Driven Proton Conductivity in Hybrid Glasses above 200 °C
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Compositional tuning is a cornerstone of inorganic glass science, yet analogous strategies remain underdeveloped for emerging metal–organic hybrid glasses. We introduce phosphate modification of zinc imidazolate glass as a route to hybrid glasses with tunable network connectivity and proton-conductive functionality. Melt-quenching of ZIF-zni with benzimidazolium dihydrogen phosphate (BP) affords a series of cm-scale, transparent bulk glasses across a wide compositional range. Systematic characterization reveals that modification proceeds through ligand exchange at zinc centers, increasing the average coordination number from 4 to above 5 and progressively depolymerizing the imidazolate network. Despite macroscopic homogeneity, X-ray total scattering identifies a quasi-periodic ordering at ∼11 Å, and 1H NMR spin relaxation establishes nanoscale phase segregation between ZIF-derived and BP-rich domains of 2–70 nm. This heterogeneity underpins proton transport under anhydrous conditions; conductivities of 10–5–10–3 S cm–1 at 240 °C follow Vogel–Tammann–Fulcher dynamics, confirming that segmental motion couples to ion mobility. Infiltrating the glass into a porous PTFE scaffold yields a composite membrane that achieves 8.4 × 10–5 S cm–1 at 170 °C under humidification and sustains steam electrolysis with near-unity Faradaic efficiency. These results establish network-modified hybrid glasses as a scalable and designable platform for intermediate-temperature solid electrolytes.

title: G-Quadruplex-Interacting Photooxidative Platinum(IV) Prodrug for Inhibiting Oncogene Transcription and Amplifying Antitumor Immunity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional platinum (Pt)-based chemotherapeutics elicit cancer cell death primarily through DNA binding, but this approach is inherently limited by poor site specificity and a lack of spatiotemporal control, which compromises therapeutic precision and safety. To overcome these limitations, we report DNATplatin, an in situ activatable and photooxidative Pt(IV) prodrug designed to combine precise recognition of DNA secondary structures with targeted genetic intervention through DNA photooxidation. By incorporating a bis-N-methylpyridinium moiety to selectively recognize DNA, DNATplatin shows a 10-fold increase in the levels in genomic DNA relative to oxaliplatin and a 2.5-fold emission turn-on selectivity for G-quadruplexes (G4s) over typical duplex DNA. Following precise nuclear localization, photoactivated DNATplatin acts as a potent photooxidant that oxidizes G4, dismantles G4 scaffolds, and abrogates circular dichroism signatures. These orchestrated lesions generate localized oxidative stress and selectively silence major G4-driven oncogenes, thereby effectively circumventing traditional Pt resistance by bypassing canonical adduct-dependent pathways. In a murine triple-negative breast tumor model, DNATplatin produces profound tumor suppression and elicits a robust systemic immune response, characterized by CD4+/CD8+ T-cell activation and depletion of Foxp3+ regulatory T cells. Collectively, this work establishes a controllable “target-and-destroy” strategy and underscores the potential of Pt(IV) photooxidants for topology-selective genetic intervention.

title: Support Protection Mechanism Enables Efficient and Stable Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Designing oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and long-term stability remains a critical challenge for the development of alkaline anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). Here, we uncover a unique support protection mechanism in which lattice-confined ruthenium (Ru) single atoms offer robust protection for the spinel Co3O4 support, realizing outstanding stability in AEMWEs. Theoretical calculations and structural characterizations reveal that lattice confinement promotes the formation of robust Ru–O–Co bridges by simultaneously shortening the Co–O and Ru–O bond lengths, thereby suppressing Co dissolution and optimizing the electronic structure for efficient catalysis. Furthermore, in situ electrochemical analysis demonstrates that the lattice confinement of Ru atoms accelerates OER kinetics through facilitated proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) steps and partially activated lattice oxygen. As a result, the RuLCA-Co3O4 dominated by the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) exhibits a lower overpotential of 260 mV at 10 mA cm–2, which is lower than that of RuSCA-Co3O4 dominated by the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) pathway. Meanwhile, the lattice-confined RuLCA-Co3O4 exhibits nearly 9-fold lower Co dissolution compared to surface-coordinated RuSCA-Co3O4 after an accelerated durability test (ADT). Moreover, RuLCA-Co3O4 maintains an outstanding stability for over 1000 h in an AEMWE system with a low degradation rate of 88.1 μV h–1, outperforming RuSCA-Co3O4. This work establishes lattice confinement as an effective strategy to decouple activity-stability trade-offs in alkaline OER and provides a viable design principle for durable AEMWE anodes.

title: Boosting Ionomer Oxygen Transport via Pore Confinement in Carbon Supports for Low-Pt Fuel Cells
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Low-Pt proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are promising for hydrogen energy implementation, yet oxygen transport through ionomer-covered catalyst surfaces becomes increasingly limiting due to the resistance associated with dense ionomer films. Herein, we demonstrate a pore-confinement strategy to manipulate the spatial locality of Pt nanoparticles within porous carbon supports, enabling simultaneous regulation of ionomer distribution and molecular organization. Pt nanoparticles were selectively positioned on the external surfaces (Ptext/PC) or within the internal nanopores (Ptint/PC) of otherwise comparable supports, while maintaining similar Pt loading, particle size, and pore characteristics. Under H2-air condition, Ptint/PC delivered a peak power density ∼1.3 times higher than that of Ptext/PC, but a similar current density in the high-voltage region. Electrochemical analyses reveal that the performance enhancement originates from improved oxygen transport rather than catalytic activity. Wide-angle X-ray scattering and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the Pt nanoparticles confined within mesopores disrupt the dense packing of ionomer backbones, thereby boosting oxygen permeability at the catalyst–ionomer interface. By establishing a direct relationship between Pt locality, ionomer distribution, backbone organization, and oxygen transport, this work identifies catalyst locality as an effective parameter for engineering interfacial mass transport and provides a new design principle for low-Pt PEMFCs.

title: Scalable Fluorinated Copper-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks for Coupled Ultratrace Perfluoroalkyl Substances Monitoring and Efficient Remediation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent water contaminants that require both effective removal and reliable monitoring. However, these functions are typically performed separately, preventing real-time evaluation of treatment performance. Here we establish a cooperative host–guest-coupling principle, in which a single host–guest binding event simultaneously drives contaminant capture and modulates the Cu-centered redox process, thereby generating concentration-dependent electrochemical signals within a porous framework. Guided by this principle, we reported a scalable fluorinated copper-based covalent organic framework (F–Cu–COF) synthesized through an open-air one-pot strategy that enables gram-scale production while retaining high crystallinity and chemical stability. Fluorinated pore domains and redox-active Cu centers create a cooperative host–guest environment that promotes PFAS binding and enrichment with electrochemical signal generation. Consequently, F–Cu–COF achieves a detection limit of 5.2 pg L–1, an uptake capacity of 3824 mg g–1, and efficient flow-through removal. This work establishes host–guest coupling as a common molecular basis for linking electrochemical signal generation with contaminant capture in scalable porous materials, providing a general design strategy for multifunctional water-treatment platforms capable of integrated treatment verification.

title: Chloride-mediated SAM locking via ligand-exchange reaction enables 18.8% active-area efficiency and stable organic solar modules
abstract: The unstable ITO-SAM interface limits organic solar cell efficiency and stability. We introduce a molecular locking strategy using a vacuum-deposited InClx interlayer that triggers ligand exchange to form a robust multidentate In–O–P coordination network. This enhances SAM anchoring and coverage, delivering 20.4% efficiency in small-area cells and 18.8% active-area efficiency in modules, while enhancing device stability. This approach provides a generalizable interfacial platform that overcomes the efficiency-stability-scalability trilemma, paving a new pathway for advancing organic photovoltaics and beyond.

title: Singlet fission and triplet transfer to a metal halide perovskite absorber
abstract: Singlet fission in tetracene generates triplet excitons that are harvested by a metal halide perovskite through a ZnPc-mediated interface with energetics consistent with an interfacial hybrid charge-transfer (IHCT) pathway, enabling triplet sensitization and their contribution to photocurrent generation in perovskite photovoltaic devices.

title: Facet-directed hydroxyl-rich surface environments stabilize iridium single atoms for efficient acidic water oxidation
abstract: Crystal facet engineering tailors a self-adaptive microenvironment for acidic OERs. The α-MnO 2 {100} facet forms a hydroxyl-rich interface that stabilizes Ir single atoms and lowers water-oxidation barriers, improving activity and stability.

title: Triboelectric DC generation via dielectric polarization coupling for self-powered IoT systems
abstract: A contact-electrification-induced dielectric polarization mechanism enables unidirectional charge transfer for stable, low-crest-factor direct-current generation, thereby supporting robust self-powered operation of a multi-sensor IoT system.

title: Enhancing Propanol Production from CO2 Reduction with a Terbium-Doped Copper Nitride Electrocatalyst
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Propanol is one of the most complex products obtained from CO2 electroreduction (CO2R). Being an interesting precursor for synthetic fuels and a feedstock for the chemical industry, its electrochemical production has recently raised increasing interest. However, low selectivity for propanol has been achieved so far. Here, via exploring a variety of original lanthanide-doped copper nitride materials, we identified and characterized terbium-doped copper nitride as the most selective catalyst for propanol formation. It allowed CO2R to yield propanol with a Faradaic efficiency of 27% at a high current density of 300 mA cm–2 within a neutral (KHCO3 electrolyte) flow cell, surpassing the performance of previous CO2R catalysts. The high density of undercoordinated nitride-derived Cu sites, combined with the increased oxophilicity of the surface, likely promoted the selectivity toward alcohols. Thorough DFT calculations showed that Tb doping increased the affinity for oxygenate-associated C2* intermediates and lowered the free-energy barrier for reactions coupling the latter with CO* toward propanol.

title: Kinetic Control of Polymorphism in Li10.5Si1.5P1.5S12–Based Solid Electrolytes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS)-type solid electrolytes (SEs) are among the most promising materials for next-generation solid-state batteries (SSBs) due to their high lithium-ion conductivity. However, challenges related to phase stability and polymorphism, especially in Ge-free, Si-based systems, limit their practical implementation. Here, the crystallization and phase transition behavior of materials with a nominal composition of Li10.5–xSi1.5P1.5S12–xIx (x = 0, 0.2, 0.4) are systematically investigated. Operando high-temperature synchrotron X-ray diffraction, total scattering with pair distribution function analysis, and differential scanning calorimetry measurements reveal the formation of a metastable orthorhombic (o) phase, followed by transformation into the thermodynamically stable tetragonal (t) phase at elevated temperatures. Our findings indicate that lithium iodide (LiI) as an additive regulates the crystallization of the o-phase and thereby governs the transition kinetics. This enables the o-to-t phase transition to occur at much reduced temperatures and faster rates. Neutron powder diffraction further uncovers minor modifications to the Si/P ratio and lithium sublattice, as well as the fact that iodine is not incorporated into the t-phase; instead, a secondary Li4PS4I-type phase forms. Collectively, this work highlights the critical role of microstructural engineering on crystallization and polymorphism in LGPS-type SEs and also demonstrates the applicability of these dual-phase materials by enabling high-performance lithium–sulfur SSBs.

title: Engineering the paclitaxel biosynthetic pathway in Physcomitrium patens for de novo and stable biosynthesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Paclitaxel is a highly valuable diterpenoid anticancer drug originally extracted from the yew tree. Due to the low efficiency of plant extraction and the high cost of semi-synthesis, efforts have been made to produce paclitaxel through biosynthesis. However, there have been no reports to date on engineered strains capable of paclitaxel biosynthesis. Here, we engineer a paclitaxel-producing line using the moss (Physcomitrium patens) chassis cells by combining transient expression verification, cytoplasmic localization strategies, self-cleaving 2 A peptide-mediated multi-gene co-expression systems and a modular iterative transformation strategy for stable genetic inheritance. Even after continuous subculturing multiple times, the engineered paclitaxel-producing lines obtained through both the initial reconstructed pathway and the optimized pathway are able to stably produce paclitaxel. This study proposes that Physcomitrium patens can serve as a plant chassis for paclitaxel biosynthesis.

title: Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.

title: Strain-Release Cycloadditions: Bicyclobutanes and Beyond
abstract: Abstract Strain-release cycloadditions have emerged as powerful reactions for converting distorted ring systems into complex and otherwise hardly attainable organic molecular architectures. This Review encompasses the fundamentals of strain, its role in governing cycloaddition pathways, and offers a systematic examination of strained carbocycles and heterocycles, from bicyclo[1.1.1]butanes and 1-azabicyclo[1.1.1]butanes, housanes and aza-housanes, 2H-azirines and aziridines, azetidines, cyclopropanes, cyclobutanes, oxiranes, oxetanes, and strained alkynes and alkenes. Across these motifs, the general principles that dictate reactivity, the breadth of known cycloadditions and activation strategies, from Brønsted and Lewis acid catalysis to transition-metal activation, photocatalysis, and double strain-release mechanisms, are highlighted. Key opportunities, current limitations, and future directions are outlined.

title: Contrasting Oxygen and Chlorine Evolution Selectivity in Tunnel and Layered MnO2 Electrocatalysts
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Controlling competing oxygen and chlorine evolution is a key challenge in chloride-containing electrolysis, particularly under neutral saline conditions relevant to seawater electrolysis. Here, two phase-pure MnO2 polymorphs with contrasting crystallographic frameworks, α-MnO2 and δ-MnO2, were synthesized through surfactant-free routes and evaluated under comparable conditions. Tetragonal α-MnO2 with a 2 × 2 tunnel framework preferentially promoted oxygen evolution, whereas layered δ-MnO2 favored chlorine evolution. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed no detectable chlorine signal for α-MnO2 after chlorine evolution, while δ-MnO2 exhibited pronounced chloride-associated surface modification. Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations further revealed distinct defect characteristics and substantially different oxygen-vacancy formation tendencies between the two frameworks. These observations suggest that framework-dependent defect formation influences chloride-associated surface chemistry and contributes to the contrasting oxygen and chlorine evolution selectivity. Importantly, the selectivity trend was retained when the MnO2 phases were integrated onto iridium-ruthenium-based dimensionally stable anodes. These results demonstrate that contrasting crystallographic frameworks and their associated defect characteristics can markedly alter anodic selectivity and provide a structural basis for designing selective electrodes for chloride-containing electrochemical systems.

title: Field-induced near-unity spin polarization in a highly emissive organic diradical
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Spin polarization essentially drives a mixed spin population toward a well-defined state and represents a critical step in the construction of qubits. The degree of spin polarization directly determines the readout contrast and the signal-to-noise ratio of spin-based detection. Open-shell luminescent diradicals constitute a highly promising platform for optically addressable qubits, in which efficient spin polarization can be achieved via external magnetic fields, temperature control, and optical pumping. However, experimentally viable routes and representative examples for achieving near-unity spin polarization remain scarce. Here, we demonstrate that near-unity spin polarization can be realized in a luminescent diradical by applying a high magnetic field at low temperature. We first estimate the required temperature and magnetic-field strength through theoretical simulations, and then develop, via molecular engineering, a highly emissive luminescent diradical molecule. At 5.5 K and magnetic fields up to 46.6 T, we observe nearly saturated magnetoluminescence (MagLum) with a giant value of 112%, indicating that the spin population of a single ground-state triplet sublevel (T0,-) approaches unity. This work provides a representative case study toward realizing near-unity spin polarization in luminescent diradicals and offers a clear physical picture of MagLum under ultrahigh magnetic fields.

title: Controlled living ring expansion polymerization for the precision synthesis of cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides)
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cyclic polymers exhibit physical properties distinct from those of their linear polymer counterparts. Although cyclic polymer materials with advanced designs can be synthesized using methods that control their molecular weight, dispersity, and topology, synthetic limitations have thus far restricted structurally defined cyclic polymers to non-conjugated structures with sp³-hybridized carbon backbones. Here we report a living ring expansion polymerization that enables the precise synthesis of cyclic polymers composed of sp²-hybridized carbon backbones, that is, cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides). Polymerization is initiated from a diarylpalladacycle complex in the presence of iodobenzene dichloride and proceeds via the successive insertion of aryl isocyanides into the palladacycle. This living polymerization process yields structurally controlled cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides) with low dispersity and predefined, customizable, high or low-molecular weights. The cyclic topology was unambiguously characterized by multiple analytical techniques, including direct visualization by high-resolution atomic force microscopy. Furthermore, the high fidelity of the palladium center facilitates the controlled synthesis of cyclic block copolymers. This advancement opens avenues for the development of topologically conjugated polymer materials.

title: Strain-engineered fabrication of high-density aligned graphene-based nanoscrolls via UV-tunable adhesive tapes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Graphene nanoscrolls (GNSs), one-dimensional nanostructures formed by rolling up a single sheet of graphene, exhibit electronic and mechanical properties distinct from the original graphene sheet. Although several methods have been proposed to synthesize GNSs, achieving high-density GNSs with controlled scroll chirality and direction remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the strain-engineered fabrication of large-scale GNSs using an ultraviolet (UV) light-tunable adhesive tape. The UV tape is stretched to apply tensile strain to graphene stacked on it, and releasing the applied strain by detaching the graphene from the tape results in the formation of GNSs. This strain-assisted method gives isolated GNSs of increased density ( ≈ 380 nanoscrolls per mm) and length (90 μm). This method also allows control of the scroll angle, i.e., chiral angle, by controlling the stretch direction of the tape/graphene stack. The nanoscroll structure allows the intercalation of metal chloride molecules, resulting in an increase of the electrical conductivity. Furthermore, heteronanoscrolls of graphene and MoS2 are realized by stretching MoS2/graphene heterostacks, exhibiting clear optical response. Our controlled synthesis of GNSs and heteronanoscrolls provides an opportunity to manipulate nanomaterials through the strain engineering with the functional UV tape.

title: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage are more pronounced in lower-risk visits: a multicenter study
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage decisions persist, despite efforts to standardize protocols. Here, we analyze 1.35 million encounters at four U.S. emergency departments that all use the Emergency Severity Index triage protocol. We independently score visits as emergent (level 2) or urgent (level 3) by applying the criteria computationally and compare to nurse assignments. We show that, matched on clinical presentation and hospital context, Hispanic patients are less often triaged emergent than Non-Hispanic White (NHW) patients at every site (odds ratios (ORs): 0.75 [95% CI 0.72–0.78] to 0.90 [0.86–0.94]), and Non-Hispanic Black patients at two (0.73 [0.71–0.74], 0.89 [0.86–0.92]). Disparities increase where the algorithm scores patients lower-risk (Hispanic-NHW ORs: 0.73 [0.69–0.77] to 0.88 [0.83–0.94]), and attenuate where it scores them higher-risk (0.83 [0.79–0.89] to 0.95 [0.90–1.00]), suggesting a disparate “benefit-of-the-doubt” pattern of clinical discretion. Standardized decision support may reduce these disparities, and we estimate a worst-case increase on ED lengths of stay to be 1.0 -3.8% across sites.

title: A 700-kilometre copper supply network in Bronze Age China revealed by multi-proxy ore fingerprinting
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Copper provenance in Bronze Age China has long been hindered by the ternary alloying (Cu-Sn-Pb) of Shang bronzes, which masks the geochemical signatures of copper sources. Here we circumvent this problem by analyzing copper ore assemblages from two Upper Erligang period (ca. 1400 BC) bronze casting sites, Chuangxinjie School North Campus and Xiaoshuangqiao, associated with the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou. Through a multi-proxy geochemical approach combining garnet U-Pb dating and chemical composition, lead isotopes, and chalcopyrite trace elements, we systematically determine that the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou obtained copper from the Jiurui district in the Middle Yangtze Valley, ~700 km to the south. This confirms one of the earliest long-distance copper supply networks in East Asia, demonstrating that the Yangtze and Yellow River basins were linked through metal resource exchange during the formative period of Chinese civilization. The multi-proxy ore fingerprinting approach presented here also offers a transferable framework for resolving the copper provenance questions in other archaeological contexts worldwide.

title: Sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics with high sensitivity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The advent of spatial transcriptomics has dramatically expanded our ability to study the vast network of cell-cell interactions at the molecular level in tissue. Among current methods, sequencing-based approaches have great potential in discovery because of their unbiased capture of the whole transcriptome. In the last couple of years, the spatial resolution for the capture addresses has been improved from ~100 μm to

title: Molecular characterization of large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the lung by multilayered omics analysis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is a rare type of lung cancer with a very poor prognosis, and its underlying molecular features remain elusive. Here, multi-omics analysis of 27 LCNEC cases along with seven small cell lung carcinomas is performed. The genomic and epigenomic alterations as well as the correlation of the genomic mutations with the pathological subtypes are characterized, which are not always consistent. Spatial omics analyses are also conducted, and most of the cases are successfully grouped into a high ASCL1 neuroendocrine (NE) subtype and high ASCL2 or YAP1 non-NE subtypes; however, an ambiguous state is observed for some specimens, which shows the simultaneous expression of NE and non-NE lineage markers. The findings of this study indicate that LCNEC may transit toward the NE or non-NE directions. By controlling the transcriptional regulatory networks of such elasticity, a new approach may be contemplated to overcome the pleiotropic therapeutic responses of LCNEC.

title: PRMT5 activity sustains histone production to maintain genome integrity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Histone proteins package DNA into nucleosomes, forming chromatin and thereby safeguarding genome integrity. Proper histone expression is essential for cell proliferation and chromatin organization, yet the upstream regulators of histone supply remain incompletely understood. PRMT5, a protein arginine methyltransferase that catalyzes symmetric dimethylation of arginine residues, is frequently overexpressed in cancer and targeted in multiple clinical trials, but its cell-essential function remains unclear. Using time-resolved nascent transcriptional profiling, quantitative proteomics, and imaging, we show that PRMT5 activity is required to sustain histone transcription and histone protein synthesis during S phase. PRMT5 inhibition or knockdown leads to rapid, p53-independent depletion of histone mRNA, leading to loss of histone proteins and accumulation of replication-associated nuclear abnormalities. Parallel depletion of the histone gene transcription factor HINFP produces similar genomic instability, linking defective histone production to loss of genome integrity. We further show that histone H4 accumulates at both histone genes and histone locus bodies (HLBs) and that H4R3me2s is enriched at HLBs. These findings support a model in which PRMT5-mediated methylation of histone H4 regulates histone transcription. Our findings establish PRMT5 as a central coordinator of histone homeostasis and provide a mechanistic rationale for its essential role in proliferating cells.

title: DNA CODEC: compressed obfuscated DNA encoding in cells for secure in vivo data storage
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: DNA represents a compelling medium for data storage due to its density, durability, and compatibility with biological systems. Current in vivo DNA data storage strategies are largely restricted to single-population systems, limiting scalability and access control. Here, we present DNA CODEC, a multi-population in vivo DNA data storage platform that combines high-density encoding with molecular obfuscation across engineered human cell populations. CODEC uses 10-ary Huffman coding with degenerate bases to optimize compressibility while maintaining decoding accuracy despite biological and technical noise. Data payloads are stably integrated into the human genome using CRISPR-based targeted insertion. Obfuscation is introduced through heterogeneous populations containing decoy clones with structurally similar, non-informative masking sequences to conceal the true payload. CODEC stably maintains genomic payloads across extended cell culture, demonstrating robustness to replication errors and population drift. Together, these features establish a scalable framework for high-fidelity and secure DNA data storage in biological systems.

title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery.
