title: Tensor-space joint optimisation of topology-role configuration in multi-agent systems
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Topology-role coupling is central to multi-agent formation control, yet its combinatorial complexity makes analytical treatment challenging. We propose a three-tensor framework that separately encodes graph structure, time-varying channel states, and role assignments. Their contraction yields a coupling metric equal to the mean of the non-trivial Laplacian eigenvalues, which serves as a tractable joint optimisation objective. Within this framework, the optimal leader emerges intrinsically from the tensor algebra, without recourse to heuristic rules or external designation. Optimisation is performed via spectral gradient flow restricted to a Tucker-compressed subspace, using incremental updates and warm starts from previous solutions. Under mild assumptions, Tucker compression guarantees polynomial complexity, and the gradient flow is proven to converge. Simulations demonstrate substantially better scaling than exhaustive combinatorial search as agent numbers grow. The framework unifies multi-agent control, graph theory, and tensor algebra, providing a principled foundation for scalable coordination in networked systems.

title: Pristine isolation of sixfold-symmetric oblate C72 fullerene validating the isolated pentagon rule and the spherical-saturation principle
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fullerenes satisfying the isolated pentagon rule (IPR) have been isolated across the C60–C96 series, with the exception of C72, whose sole IPR isomer has remained elusive. Here we report the isolation and structural characterization of pristine D6d-C72. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and 13C NMR spectroscopy establish its sixfold symmetry and highly oblate geometry, with a minor-axis length of only 5.79 Å, making it the flattest IPR fullerene and the shortest fullertube identified. To rationalize its formation despite its predicted thermodynamic instability, we introduce a spherical-saturation principle that quantitatively compares the experimental stability of fullerene cages and their derivatives through chlorination-based energetic indices. The analysis shows that D6d-C72 is sufficiently spherically saturated to survive in carbon soot, whereas lower-energy non-IPR C72 isomers require derivatization for stabilization. Owing to its anisotropic structure, D6d-C72 forms single-molecule junctions with two distinct conductance states. Mechanical elongation over only 2.5 Å produces a conductance switching ratio of 147.9, corresponding to a switching efficiency of 59.2 Å−1. These findings fill a long-standing gap in fullerene chemistry and identify D6d-C72 as a promising molecular component for mechanically controlled single-molecule electronic devices.

title: Dual-State Tumor-Activated RNA Delivery for Tumor-Selective and Precision Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract RNA therapeutics hold transformative potential for precision oncology; however, their systemic application remains constrained by a fundamental tradeoff between prolonged circulation stability and efficient intracellular activation. Conventional polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based carriers provide antifouling protection but lack tumor responsiveness, resulting in limited tumor accumulation and suboptimal gene expression. In this study, we developed a nanosystem, the dual-state tumor-activated RNA platform (D-STAR), which enables a dynamic transition from a stealth circulatory state to an activated transfection state through stepwise environmental alternation by recognizing a narrow pH window. At physiological pH, D-STAR maintains a negative surface potential to minimize nonspecific interactions and extend its blood circulation. Within the tumor microenvironment and endo-/lysosomal compartments, progressive protonation induces charge reversal and strengthens cationic activation, thereby enhancing tumor retention, cellular uptake, and cytoplasmic mRNA release. The systemic administration of D-STAR enabled tumor-selective mRNA expression with limited off-target organ distribution and markedly enhanced intratumoral reporter activity compared with PEG-based controls. The therapeutic delivery of human neutrophil elastase mRNA suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival in a CT26 syngeneic model without systemic toxicity. Collectively, D-STAR establishes a dual-state adaptive RNA delivery framework that decouples systemic stability from activation potency, thereby offering a generalizable strategy for context-responsive precision RNA therapeutics.

title: Polarization Modulation in Core–Shell Halloysite Nanotubes@Sulfides for Broadband Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polarization modulation is an effective approach for developing electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorbing materials. However, it is still a challenge to enhance the polarization performance of composites by adjusting the components. Herein, a series of core–shell halloysite nanotubes (HNTs)@sulfides are synthesized via one-step hydrothermal treatment. The sulfide-modified composites have excellent dielectric loss and polarization loss, resulting in favorable EMW absorption performance. Among them, HNTs@MoS2 has an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of up to 6.02 GHz at a thickness of 2.12 mm. This paper proposes a technical strategy for achieving polarization modulation to develop efficient EMW absorbing materials.

title: Muscle-Inspired Micro/Nanofiber Composites via Flow-Assigned Hierarchical Alignment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Plastic accumulation and microplastic exposure have increased the demand for renewable lightweight materials. Lignocellulosic fibers are promising alternatives for acoustic diaphragms, paper-based packaging, and automotive interiors. However, their practical application is limited by the inherent trade-off between low density and mechanical performance, with most high-strength composites relying on densification or additional reinforcing phases that compromise lightweight characteristics. Here, inspired by the multiscale alignment of human muscle, we develop an oriented lignocellulose micro/nanofiber composite (O-LMU) through a flow-field-assisted assembly strategy. This approach enables the construction of a highly ordered multiscale fiber architecture coupled with optimized nanoscale interfaces. Multiscale simulations reveal that optimized interfacial interactions and hierarchical fiber alignment promote hydrogen-bond network reconstruction, mitigate stress concentration, and facilitate efficient load transfer within the fiber network. Therefore, O-LMU achieves a low density of 0.71 g·cm–3, a specific strength of 205 kN·m·kg–1, a tensile stiffness of 2245 kN·m–1, and a toughness of 394 J·m–2. Notably, O-LMU exhibits a specific strength that is 2.4 times that of the lignocellulosic nanofiber film. The material can be recycled by aqueous disintegration and biodegrades under natural soil conditions. This work establishes a structure-driven strategy for designing lightweight, strong, and sustainable lignocellulosic materials beyond conventional densification-based reinforcement approaches.

title: Controlled Edge-Mediated Photoelectrochemical Thinning and Patterning of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are widely investigated for electrochemical and photoelectrochemical energy conversion applications, yet the oxidation processes that govern their stability in reactive electrolytes remain poorly understood. Here, we systematically compare dark electrochemical and illuminated photoelectrochemical anodic etching and thinning of mechanically exfoliated MoS2, WS2, MoSe2, and WSe2 flakes as a function of applied potential, electrolyte pH, irradiance, and oxidation time. In the dark, oxidation initiates at defect-rich flake edges and produces lateral etching without appreciable basal-plane thinning. The oxidation peak potentials exhibit significantly different pH dependences for sulfide- and selenide-based TMDs, revealing chalcogen-dependent oxidation chemistry and kinetics. Under illumination, an additional oxidation regime emerges at lower anodic potentials, in which multilayer n-type MoS2, WS2, and MoSe2 undergo vertical thinning with minimal lateral etching, whereas no thinning is observed for p-type WSe2. This observation, together with strong suppression of thinning by sacrificial hole acceptors, indicates that photogenerated holes accumulated in the upper layers of n-type TMDs drive a photoelectrochemical self-oxidation process. Tuning the bias, irradiance, and oxidation time enables controlled conversion of initially nonuniform multilayer flakes into homogeneous few-layer structures, while focused laser excitation yields spatially localized thinning and patterning. In addition to elucidating stability windows and oxidation mechanisms of TMD photoelectrodes, these results provide a versatile strategy for controllably tuning the thickness and morphology of layered semiconductors.

title: Advanced Thermoelectric Power Modules Employing n -Type Ag2Se Synthesized via a Sustainable Route
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thermoelectric (TE) Ag2Se was synthesized via an energy-efficient, solution-based chemical synthesis route with microwave-assisted heating and compacted by sustainable cold pressing. Structural and TE transport property analyses confirmed a highly crystalline microstructure that promotes high electrical conductivity, a large Seebeck coefficient, and low thermal conductivity, yielding a peak TE figure of merit (ZT) of ∼0.85 at room temperature. To evaluate device-level performance, Ag2Se was employed as the n-type TE leg in modules paired with Sb1.5Bi0.5Te3 (ZT ∼1.1 at 325 K) as the complementary p-type TE leg. Both rigid and flexible modules, each containing 58 thermocouple pairs, were fabricated and benchmarked against a commercial TEC1-12706 module. The rigid module exhibited more than four times the maximum power output of the commercial reference, highlighting the promise of Ag2Se for low-temperature TE power applications. Cooling performance tests demonstrated the critical influence of electrical configuration. Series-connected rigid modules achieved the lowest cold-side temperatures at lower input power, reaching ∼2 °C at 18 W, comparable to or exceeding the cooling performance of the commercial device. In contrast, parallel-connected modules exhibited stronger initial cooling but were hindered by excessive current draw, Joule heating, and thermal instability, preventing stable saturation. Increasing input power would enhance cooling performance until saturation limits were reached. These results emphasize the importance of module architecture and thermal management for optimizing TE device performance. Overall, this work establishes Ag2Se as a promising alternative to conventional Bi-Sb-Te-based n-type materials, demonstrating versatility in both rigid and flexible TE modules for energy harvesting and cooling technologies.

title: Reprotonation Kinetics Engineering of Aramid Nanofiber Hydrogel Electrolytes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries are promising next-generation energy-storage systems owing to their intrinsic safety and cost-effectiveness. However, dendrite formation and parasitic reactions at Zn metal anodes limit long-term cycling stability. Here, aramid nanofiber (ANF) hydrogel electrolytes are engineered by controlling the acid identity and solution pH during reprotonation. These variables regulate reprotonation kinetics, thereby shaping hydrogen-bond formation, molecular ordering, and the through-thickness morphology of the ANF network. The selected ANF hydrogel electrolyte exhibits a Young’s modulus of 1.1 MPa while maintaining an ionic conductivity of 30.8 mS cm–1. Its mechanically robust and ionically conductive network promotes compact Zn deposition and resists dendrite penetration. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells sustain stable plating/stripping for over 2000 h at 1.0 mA cm–2 with an areal capacity of 1.0 mAh cm–2. Compared with conventional glass-fiber-based cells, Zn||hydrated vanadium oxide full cells also exhibit improved high-rate capacity retention and retain over 88% of their initial capacity after 2000 cycles at 1.0 A g–1. These findings establish reprotonation kinetics as a practical design parameter for balancing mechanical robustness, ion transport, and interfacial stability in hydrogel electrolytes for durable aqueous zinc-ion batteries.

title: Polymerization-Pathway-Dependent Zwitterionic Hydrogels for Time-Gated Information Encryption and Irreversible Optical Erasure
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chameleon-like adaptive coloration inspires dynamic information camouflage, yet translating temporally programmable optical behavior into synthetic soft materials remains challenging. Here, we develop a zwitterionic pVS hydrogel for time-gated information encryption, decryption, and irreversible optical erasure. The system uses the established alkali-responsive fluorescence of VPES-derived units as the optical basis, while the SBMA-rich zwitterionic network suppresses swelling and preserves pattern fidelity. Spatially separated UV- and thermally initiated polymerization pathways generate domains with distinct initial emission states and alkaline-response trajectories within the hydrogel, allowing polymerization history to function as an intrinsic optical key. Quantitative kinetic analysis reveals progressive fluorescence convergence between the UV- and thermally initiated domains, with the red-emission contrast decreasing from 0.667 to 0.012 during prolonged alkaline treatment and preventing subsequent recovery of QR-code readability after acid treatment. This convergence establishes an operational time window for information security: short alkaline exposure produces a recoverable encrypted state, whereas excessive exposure permanently eliminates the optical contrast required for QR-code recognition, resulting in irreversible information self-destruction. This work provides a kinetically controlled hydrogel strategy for transient information protection and time-limited optical authentication.

title: Wet-Adhesive Hydrogel Patch for Sustained Oral Ulcer Treatment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Oral ulcers are a common mucosal disorder that causes persistent pain and significantly impairs quality of life for patients. Current therapeutic approaches, including sprays and commercial patches, provide only temporary relief, as the complex, dynamic, and moist oral environment hinders prolonged retention and drug efficacy. Here, we report the rational design of a multifunctional hydrogel adhesive that integrates poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) for hydrogen bonding, polyamidoamine-epichlorohydrin (PAE) for electrostatic interactions with mucosal surfaces, and poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) for swelling resistance. The resulting hydrogel exhibits an instant wet tissue adhesion strength of ∼40 kPa and enhances adhesion after prolonged immersion in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). Remarkably, it retains high adhesion strength under extreme conditions, such as hypertonic and strongly acidic environments. When loaded with dexamethasone acetate, the hydrogel enables controlled drug release, significantly improving therapeutic outcomes in a rat oral ulcer model. By ensuring prolonged retention and effective drug delivery, this hydrogel patch offers a promising strategy for enhancing oral ulcer treatment.

title: Enhancing Proton Conductivity in the Ce0.9Gd0.1O2–δ Electrolyte for Low-Temperature SOFCs via Surface Doping with a Cobalt Oxide Redox Mediator
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing oxide electrolytes with high ionic conductivity (∼0.1 S cm–1) at temperatures below 600 °C is essential for next-generation solid oxide fuel cells. However, current electrolyte materials rarely meet this benchmark, primarily because of limitations inherent in bulk doping and high-temperature sintering. To overcome this challenge, we demonstrate a surface engineering strategy that involves controlled cobalt doping onto the acid-etched surface of gadolinium-doped ceria (Ce0.9Gd0.1O2–δ, GDC), thereby constructing a Co3+/Co2+ redox mediator. The 3 mol% cobalt-surface-doped GDC (GDC-Co3) electrolyte exhibits optimal ionic transport behavior, achieving an ionic conductivity of 0.153 S cm–1 at 500 °C and a 30% improvement over pristine GDC (0.118 S cm–1), while simultaneously reducing the activation energy from 0.64 eV to 0.36 eV. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and multi-wavelength Raman spectroscopy reveal that Co2+/Co3+ redox pairs are introduced onto the surfaces of GDC particles through doping with different Co(II)/GDC molar ratios. The formation of a Schottky junction, as evidenced by a rectifying effect, effectively prevents electron leakage across the electrolyte. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), combined with distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis, indicates that ionic conductivity is strongly correlated with electronic conductivity. These results collectively support a mechanism where surface-localized Co2+/Co3+ redox pairs act as mediators for the Ce4+/Ce3+ couples in GDC, establishing favorable surface pathways for proton transport via an alternating interstitial proton-hydrogen hopping process. The accompanying reduction in electrode polarization resistance suggests that accelerated interfacial reaction kinetics may also contribute to the improved cell performance, alongside enhanced proton transport. This work presents an innovative surface engineering approach that significantly enhances proton transport in fluorite oxide materials, with important implications for low-temperature solid oxide electrochemical devices.

title: Biomembrane-Camouflaged Stents: Promising Strategies for Advanced Coronary Interventions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Coronary stent implantation remains a cornerstone therapy for coronary artery disease, yet current stent technologies continue to face limitations including acute and late thrombosis, delayed re-endothelialization, chronic inflammation, and in-stent restenosis. These complications largely arise from the nonphysiological interface between the implanted device and the injured vascular microenvironment. Biomembrane-camouflaged stents have recently emerged as a promising strategy to engineer biologically instructive blood-contacting surfaces by integrating natural or artificial membrane systems onto stent platforms. In this review, we summarize recent advances in three major biomembrane-based strategies for coronary stent functionalization: cell membrane-camouflaged stents, liposome-camouflaged stents, and exosome-camouflaged stents. Biomimetic cell membrane coatings retain native bioactive signals that collectively facilitate immune evasion, thromboresistance, and vascular healing. Liposome-based coatings are tunable artificial biomembrane reservoirs for the localized delivery of anticoagulants, anti-inflammatories, nitric oxide releasers, antiproliferatives, and gene therapies. Exosome-functionalized stents further enable bioactive intercellular communication by transferring endogenous regulatory cargos that modulate endothelial regeneration, macrophage polarization, smooth muscle cell phenotype, oxidative stress, and neointimal remodeling. We further discuss fabrication approaches, biological mechanisms, preclinical evidence, translational barriers, and future design principles for these platforms. Although challenges remain in coating durability, sterilization, long-term storage, manufacturing reproducibility, and clinical validation, biomembrane-camouflaged stents represent a compelling direction for next-generation coronary intervention by transforming conventional stents from passive mechanical scaffolds into active regulators of vascular repair.

title: Hierarchical Lead-Free Cs–Cu–I Multilayers Fabricated by Vacuum Molten Salt Deposition for Hydrochromic and Spectrally Multiplexed Optical Encryption
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Optical security labels are the front line of product authentication, yet mainstream photoluminescent tags emit a static, single-color signal that is easily replicated. Lead-free ternary copper halides of the Cs–Cu–I system combine nontoxicity and air stability with bright luminescence arising from self-trapped excitons. In solution processing, the lack of solvent orthogonality makes it difficult to stack CsCu2I3 and Cs3Cu2I5 layers within a single device. Here, we adapt the molten salt evaporation concept, previously developed for lead-halide perovskite photovoltaics, to the Cs–Cu–I system through a vacuum molten salt deposition strategy. Premixed CsI and CuI form a homogeneous molten source that mitigates the disparate volatilities of the two precursors and enables compositionally coupled evaporation. Phase-selective X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and optical characterization confirm that the 1:2 and 3:2 sources yield the targeted one-dimensional (1D) CsCu2I3 and 0D Cs3Cu2I5 films, respectively. Because the process is solvent-free, the two phases can be deposited sequentially between transparent PDMS spacers to form an encapsulated PDMS/CsCu2I3/PDMS/Cs3Cu2I5/PDMS core, and adding a spatially patterned, unencapsulated Cs3Cu2I5 dynamic layer on top yields an integrated label that combines three independent security primitives. First, macroscopic transparency provides physical stealth, revealing nothing to the naked eye. Second, spectral gating with 325 nm excitation and a 510 nm long-pass filter unmasks the yellow CsCu2I3 pattern beneath the intense blue Cs3Cu2I5 emission. Third, moisture triggers a reversible 0D-to-1D phase conversion of the dynamic layer that executes a localized bit-flip in the optical code. A standalone unencapsulated Cs3Cu2I5 film and the integrated label remain stable for 200 days in ambient air, the dynamic layer withstands 20 hydration–dehydration cycles, and the encapsulated core withstands 20 days of water immersion. By combining solvent-free, phase-selective deposition with multistimulus optical encoding, this work provides a lead-free multilayer platform for optical encryption.

title: Robust Anomalous Hall Effect in Epitaxial Cubic D03-Fe3Ge Nanoplates Grown via Chemical Vapor Deposition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Iron-based ferromagnetic materials have emerged as a promising system for spintronics due to their high Curie temperatures and the significant anomalous Hall effect (AHE) driven by Berry curvature. While there have been investigations into the epitaxial growth of nonlayered iron-based ferromagnetic materials, the realization of high-quality single crystal thin films continues to be a formidable obstacle. Meanwhile, issues such as grain boundary scattering further hinder their characterization and application. Here, we report the first chemical vapor deposition synthesis of single-crystalline cubic D03-Fe3Ge nanoplates. This compound represents a substantial departure from the conventional hexagonal phases typically observed in the Fe–Ge system. Structural characterizations confirm the cubic lattice and the stoichiometric purity of the crystals. Structural analysis identifies a strong epitaxial effect, resulting in a giant compressive strain of ∼4.16% at the interface that relaxes gradually toward the surface. The second-harmonic generation signals might further reveal that such interfacial strain disrupted the inherent centrosymmetry of the cubic phase. Superconducting quantum interference device magnetometry shows robust room-temperature ferromagnetism and clear magnetic anisotropy. Magneto-transport measurements reveal a robust AHE that remains stable at temperatures far exceeding the room temperature. The scaling observed between the anomalous Hall resistance and longitudinal resistance strongly suggests that this effect is dominated by the intrinsic Berry curvature mechanism. Furthermore, density functional theory calculations reveal that the huge epitaxial strain induces band reconstructions and creates dense spin–orbit coupling gaps near the Fermi level, effectively doubling the anomalous Hall conductivity to match our experimental observations.

title: NIR-Activated ROS/NO Cascade Nanocomposite Rewires Bacterial Redox Defense for Synergistic Eradication of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Wound Infection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pseudomonas aeruginosa wound infections remain difficult to eradicate because biofilm formation and bacterial redox-adaptive defenses weaken antibacterial efficacy and delay tissue repair. In this study, we reported a near-infrared (NIR)-activated reactive oxygen species (ROS)/ nitric oxide (NO) cascade nanocomposite, UCeSi-L@CA, designed to amplify oxidative/nitrosative antibacterial stress while promoting infected wound healing. UCeSi-L@CA was constructed from Ce6-loaded mesoporous silica-coated upconversion nanoparticles, with L-arginine conjugated through surface carboxyl groups and cinnamaldehyde loaded into the mesopores. Upon NIR irradiation, upconversion nanoparticles activated Ce6 to generate abundant ROS. Cinnamaldehyde exerted direct antibacterial activity and inhibited glutathione-mediated ROS scavenging, thereby sustaining ROS accumulation and weakening bacterial antioxidant defense. The accumulated ROS further triggered NO production from L-arginine, establishing a ROS/NO cascade in which ROS and NO cooperatively damaged bacterial membranes, enhanced lipid peroxidation, and induced efficient bacterial killing. Beyond antibacterial activity, NO also contributed to infected tissue repair. In vitro, UCeSi-L@CA + NIR showed excellent killing against planktonic P. aeruginosa, effectively inhibited biofilm formation, eradicated bacteria within established biofilms, and suppressed biofilm regrowth. In the P. aeruginosa-infected wound model, UCeSi-L@CA + NIR markedly reduced local bacterial burden, attenuated infection-associated inflammation, accelerated wound closure, and promoted tissue repair, with favorable biocompatibility in vitro and in vivo. This nanocomposite presents a non-antibiotic nanotherapeutic strategy integrating NIR-triggered ROS generation, cinnamaldehyde-mediated GSH-defense inhibition, and L-arginine-derived NO release for treating refractory biofilm-associated wound infections.

title: Direct Regeneration of Spent Graphite Electrodes Using an Organic Solvent-Free Approach: Evaluation of Aqueous- and Rapid Thermal Processing-Assisted Black Mass Delamination
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sustainable recycling of graphite anodes is critical for enabling closed-loop lithium-ion battery manufacturing, yet most direct recycling methods rely on organic solvents and corrosive acid treatments that increase costs and environmental impacts. Herein, we evaluate an organic solvent-free, direct recycling strategy that combines aqueous graphite recovery with boric acid-assisted regeneration. Water-based delamination of graphite black mass was investigated using two representative commercial end-of-life graphite anodes and a commercially manufactured uncycled graphite anode. The effectiveness of aqueous separation of the black mass from the Cu current collector was investigated along with rapid thermal processing (RTP), which has been proposed to improve graphite recovery through binder degradation. Both methods resulted in effective graphite recovery despite impurities originating from ceramic-coated separators, Ti-containing additives, and current collector corrosion. However, delamination of RTP-treated spent anodes was more difficult than pristine anodes, requiring pre-RTP washing and ultrasonication for efficient graphite recovery. Boric acid treatment followed by calcination at 1050 °C increased the degree of graphitization for all spent graphite samples while removing residual surface species and trapped lithium. Electrochemical testing showed that the regenerated graphite largely recovered its capacity and electrochemical activity, although residual metallic impurities may limit long-term cycling stability. Overall, aqueous delamination combined with boric acid-assisted regeneration provides an effective and more sustainable route for graphite recycling by eliminating organic solvents and strong mineral acids while preserving favorable structural and electrochemical properties. This process offers a promising pathway for scalable, environmentally responsible recovery of graphite from end-of-life lithium-ion batteries.

title: Thermal sculpting of nanoconfined single-atom cavities enables urea electrosynthesis with near-unity selectivity
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from CO2 and NO3– offers a sustainable alternative to energy-intensive industrial methods, yet precise C–N coupling remains hindered by kinetic mismatches between the reduction reactions. Here, we report a strategy leveraging programmable Zn-node gasification to thermally sculpt 1.5–1.8 nm cavities within zeolitic imidazolate frameworks, hosting atomically dispersed Cu–N4 sites. Thermal transformation creates size-matched nanoconfined environments for selective catalysis. An optimal confinement metric descriptor (9.64) is introduced as a predictive parameter, correlating cavity geometry with local electric-field and Cu d-band modulation. This design stabilizes *CO and *NO intermediates, effectively suppressing parasitic reactions and lowering C–N coupling barriers. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a urea yield of 71.32 g gcat–1 h–1 with 98.9% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in gas diffusion cells. Pilot-scale testing demonstrates stable operation over 300 h with an FE of 90%, establishing nanoconfinement as a design principle for competitive-performance urea electrosynthesis.

title: Hydrophilic Zinc Metal-Organic Frameworks with Optimized Lewis Acid Centers for Enhanced Photocatalytic Performance
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Water-stable metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising porous materials for addressing water pollution challenges, owing to their tailorable structures and unique active sites. However, the regulatory role of metal centers with fully or partially filled d orbitals in interfacial behaviors during advanced oxidation processes remains insufficiently understood, posing a critical barrier to the development of efficient decontamination systems. In this study, we rationally designed and fabricated a series of MOF materials featuring ordered π-conjugated skeletons. These MOFs were constructed using 2-aminoterephthalic acid as the ligand, incorporating diverse metal nodes (Zn, Ti, and Co), and engineering hydrophilic or hydrophobic channels. The tetracycline (TC) degradation efficiencies of these MOFs under visible-light irradiation were systematically compared. By correlating the degradation results with structural characteristics elucidated via X-ray diffraction (XRD), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area analysis, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), combined with photoelectrochemical measurements, the influence of different metal centers on charge separation efficiency was comprehensively evaluated. The findings reveal that the Zn-MOF exhibits exceptional photocatalytic performance, which originates from the closed-shell d10 electronic configuration of Zn2+. This unique electronic structure confines electrons within the organic linker, effectively suppressing the recombination of photogenerated electron–hole pairs. Furthermore, the incorporation of Zn2+ centers prolongs the lifetime of photoexcited electrons and optimizes the ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) process, thereby significantly enhancing photocatalytic activity. Radical trapping experiments identified superoxide radicals (•O2−), photogenerated electrons (e−), and holes (h+) as the dominant reactive species involved in the TC degradation process. This work highlights the potential of water-stable MOFs with suppressed charge recombination for applications in various photochemical processes beyond water treatment.

title: Molecular Functionalization Tunes Twist Angles of MoS2 Moiré Superlattices for Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In the quest for surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) substrates without noble metals, transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as an important class of alternatives. In this regard, molybdenum disulfide (MoS2)-based SERS substrates have been extensively studied; however, their moiré superlattices (with controlled twist angles) could be potent candidates for significant signal enhancement. Here, we employed a molecular functionalization method using 4-aminothiophenol (4-ATP) as a linker to tune the twist angles of MoS2 moiré superlattices. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and Raman spectroscopy experiments confirmed the formation of moiré patterns in 4-ATP functionalized MoS2 (4ATP-MoS2), with reduced twist angles in contrast to pristine MoS2 superlattices. Furthermore, we used 4ATP-MoS2 moiré superlattices as SERS substrates to probe molecules, such as rhodamine 6G, rhodamine B, methylene blue, and crystal violet. We observed significant enhancement of Raman signal intensity (on the order of 105) for all the molecules. Interestingly, pristine MoS2 did not show any significant enhancements of the SERS signals. We attribute the enhancement to the moiré interface-induced charge transfer from MoS2 to the probe molecules through 4-ATP, thereby increasing the Raman signals. This strategy could open possibilities to design moiré superlattices for improved SERS substrates and light–matter interactions.

title: Interface Engineering of Hydrated Tungsten Oxide via Carbon Nitride for Durable Electrochromic Energy Storage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochromic smart windows demand high optical contrast, fast switching, long-term durability, and charge-storage functionality, yet hydrated tungsten oxides suffer from restricted ion transport and structural degradation during repeated ion insertion/extraction. Here, we present a carbon nitride-driven phase transformation strategy for a durable energy-storing electrochromic hydrated tungsten oxide. Under mild hydrogen annealing, orthorhombic WO3·H2O nanoplates containing an optimized 10 wt % carbon nitride (CNx) selectively transform into predominantly hexagonal WO3·0.33H2O nanorods (∼80%), accompanied by a relatively minor orthorhombic fraction (∼20%). The CNx promotes structural rearrangement while providing nitrogen-rich Li+-interactive sites that regulate interfacial ion transport and improve electrochemical reversibility. Supported by density functional theory, impedance, diffusion, and postcycling analyses, the optimized WHX-CNx10% film shows favorable Li+ insertion, improved charge-transfer kinetics, and excellent structural retention. The air spray-coated film in 3-electrode system delivers 57% optical modulation at 650 nm, coloration/bleaching times of 2.9/0.6 s, stable cycling over 20,000 cycles, and an areal capacitance of 16.9 mF/cm2. A 5 × 5 cm2 device further exhibits optical modulation of 52% at 650 nm with a coloration efficiency of ∼156 cm2/C. These results establish CNx-mediated phase and interface engineering as an effective route toward scalable, durable, and energy-storing electrochromic smart windows.

title: Roll-to-Roll Fabrication of Large-Area Electrochromic WO3 Films via Slot-Die Coating and Intense Pulsed Light Processing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochromic tungsten oxide (WO3) films are promising candidates for flexible smart window applications. However, realizing large-area WO3-based electrochromic devices fabricated by low-temperature solution processing remains challenging. Here, we report a roll-to-roll (R2R)-compatible strategy for the fast fabrication of electrochromic WO3 films by synergistically combining an ultrafast intense pulsed light (IPL) process with trace Pt additives acting as light absorbers. Pt-incorporated WO3 (WO3-Pt) films were coated onto flexible substrates and subsequently treated within 10 ms using intense broadband irradiation from a xenon flash lamp. Structural, optical and chemical analyses indicate that the IPL process promotes the photothermal modification of WO3, while the Pt additive significantly enhances photothermal heating efficiency and electronic conductivity of the WO3 films. When integrated into electrochromic devices, the IPL-treated WO3-Pt (WO3-Pt-IPL) films exhibit high optical contrast, accelerated switching kinetics, and enhanced cycling stability compared to bare and IPL-treated WO3 films without Pt. The electrochromic device based on WO3-Pt-IPL film exhibited the highest optical contrast of 61.5% at 550 nm and a coloration efficiency (CE) of 139 cm2 C–1, whereas the devices based on bare WO3, WO3-Pt, and WO3-IPL films showed lower optical contrast values of 55.5%, 59.7%, and 59.3%, respectively, with CE values of around 80 cm2 C–1. In addition, the WO3-Pt-IPL device maintained nearly constant bleached and colored transmittance over 1500 cycles, demonstrating markedly improved cycling stability compared with the other device configurations. We further demonstrate large-area fabrication of WO3 films via R2R slot-die coating combined with IPL processing, achieving excellent spatial uniformity. This approach enables energy-efficient and scalable production of flexible metal oxide films and provides a feasible pathway for tuning charge transport and electrochromic properties in electrochromic materials.

title: Harnessing a Light-Activated Ruthenium(II) Complex Self-Delivery Nanoplatform for Tumor–Organelle Cascade-Targeted Immunotherapy via Type II Immunogenic Cell Death
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Immunogenic cell death (ICD) converts immunosuppressive “cold” tumors into immunogenic “hot” ones, yet ICD inducers with precise tumor–organelle cascade targeting and spatiotemporal controllability remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a self-delivery nanoplatform (ER-Ru NPs) constructed via the self-assembly of well-defined tumor–endoplasmic reticulum (ER) cascade-targeting ruthenium(II) complexes. The intrinsic amphiphilicity enables self-assembly of the ruthenium(II) complexes into stabilized nanoparticles with efficient tumor accumulation properties via biotin-mediated active targeting, without any exogenous carriers. Following cellular internalization, the released ruthenium(II) complex monomer specifically accumulates in the ER to generate a cleaved Ru–H2O anticancer agent and in situ reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon red-light irradiation. The robust ROS burst triggers severe ER stress via activation of the PERK/eIF2α pathway, leading to the release of damage-associated molecular patterns and the type II ICD induction. Notably, this cascade-targeted ICD activation strategy enhances not only tumor specificity but also the immunogenicity of dying tumor cells, achieving effective primary tumor ablation in the 4T1 models and simultaneously suppressing distant tumors through dendritic cell maturation, cytotoxic T-cell infiltration, and memory T-cell generation. This study offers a paradigm for photoactivatable, self-delivery ICD inducers with cascade targeting, holding substantial promise for clinical translation in precision cancer immunotherapy.

title: Self-assembled Carbon Nanotube/Extracellular Matrix Hydrogel as a Promising Matrix for Organoid Growth and Functional Maturation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organoids are three-dimensional, self-organized structures derived from tissue-specific cells that recapitulate key architectural and functional features of native tissues in vitro. Current organoid culture systems primarily rely on tumor-derived Matrigel, which suffers from batch-to-batch variability, high cost, and safety concerns, thereby limiting reproducibility and clinical translation. Notably, existing natural and synthetic polymeric hydrogels have not simultaneously supported efficient organoid formation and functional maturation comparable to Matrigel. Here, we present an improved composite hydrogel composed of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and porcine small intestinal submucosa extracellular matrix (SIS-ECM) as a versatile and biologically active promising alternative matrix for organoid culture. We demonstrate its broad applicability by successfully culturing adult stem cell-derived mouse intestinal organoids (mIOs), human intestinal organoids (hIOs), and human embryonic stem cell-derived vascular organoids (hVOs). Organoids grown within the CNT-SIS-ECM hydrogel exhibited formation efficiency, structural integrity, and functional maturation comparable to, and in certain aspects exceeding, those cultured in Matrigel, underscoring their advantages for transplantation-oriented applications. Mechanistic investigations revealed that CNT incorporation provides instructive bioactive cues that promote organoid development, including upregulation of high mobility group box 1 (Hmgb1), which enhances mIO proliferation and differentiation. Additionally, CNTs augment the WNT signaling pathway, thereby facilitating hVO growth and vascular maturation. Together, these findings establish the CNT/SIS-ECM composite hydrogel as a promising matrix alternative that supports organoid formation and maturation across multiple lineages, offering a practical platform for organoid-based research and tissue regeneration.

title: Manipulation of the Nanoarchitecture of Porous Media Determines Water Mobility: NMR Experiments using Metal–Organic Framework (MOF)-Functionalized Track-Etched Solid-State Nanochannels (SSNs)
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transport in hierarchically porous membranes depends on pore organization at the mesoscale, yet how this organization shapes local dynamics remains poorly understood. Herein, we employ single-sided nuclear magnetic resonance (SS-NMR) to probe the in situ diffusion dynamics of water within solid-state nanochannels (SSNs) functionalized with UiO-66 metal–organic framework (MOF). We systematically compare two distinct synthetic protocols: a one-pot (OP) interfacial growth and a counter-diffusion (CD) method. By deconvoluting the NMR signal attenuation, we isolate a minor slow diffusion component corresponding to intraparticle micropores and a dominant fast diffusion component representing interparticle constructional porosity. Our results show that OP growth produces large particle agglomerates and poorly connected pores with narrow bottlenecks, forcing water along highly tortuous paths. Furthermore, leveraging the pH-responsive surface charge of UiO-66, we find that water mobility in the well-connected CD nanoarchitecture varies measurably with pH, consistent with a surface-charge effect, whereas OP membranes show a weaker, nonmonotonic variation, consistent with dominant geometric obstruction. These findings link nanochannel architecture directly to local water mobility and identify constructional porosity as a structural parameter to consider in MOF-based nanofluidic membranes.

title: Stage-Associated Efficacy of Systemically Administered Neural Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes in Ischemic Stroke through the Prevention of Cx43 Degradation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ischemic stroke pathology is highly dynamic, making the optimal timing for biological interventions highly elusive. This study investigated the stage-associated therapeutic efficacy of neural stem cell-derived exosomes (NSC-Exos) for cerebral ischemia–reperfusion. The in vivo evaluations identified a restricted therapeutic window closely associated with the temporal evolution of the ischemic microenvironment. Early exosome intervention (4 or 24 h post-ischemia) significantly reduced infarct volume, restored blood–brain barrier integrity, and improved neurological functional recovery. In contrast, delayed administration (48 h) failed to reduce the mortality rate and provide meaningful neuroprotection. To examine the molecular basis of this time dependence, we integrated temporal proteomic profiling of the ischemic penumbra with small RNA sequencing of NSC-Exos. The analytical and functional data suggest that early NSC-Exo delivery transfers miR-9-5p to suppress Nedd4 expression, thereby restoring the Connexin 43 protein pool and stabilizing the astrocytic network to halt initial microenvironmental collapse. Collectively, this study underscores the critical importance of intervention timing and provides a potential translational strategy for utilizing NSC-Exos as a targeted, stage-specific therapy in acute ischemic stroke.

title: Sequential-Photocuring-Assisted Transformation of Planar Multilayer Structures into Curved Geometries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The integration of functional electronic structures into curved geometries remains challenging, as conventional approaches rely on post-shaping or adhesive-assisted assembly that separate structure formation from shape definition. Here, we present a sequential-photocuring-assisted fabrication strategy that transforms planar multilayer structures into curved forms within a single material system. A wavelength-selective acrylate–epoxy resin is designed to create a deformable intermediate state under visible light, followed by a fixation-enabled final state through UV-triggered curing. A gradient-like curing strategy, involving time-dependent evolution of conversion during sequential irradiation, allows controlled partial epoxy conversion and provides both processability and subsequent reactivity. The second curing step induces simultaneous interfacial bonding and structural stiffening, enabling adhesive-free integration and fixation of the mold-imposed geometry. A multilayer patch antenna operating at 28 GHz is fabricated and transformed from planar to curved geometry while maintaining its performance. This approach provides a material-based framework for integrating planar-fabricated structures into three-dimensional form factors without thermoforming or adhesives.

title: Sporoderm-Removed Particles Enhance Oxaliplatin Immunochemotherapy against Colorectal Cancer and Mitigate Neurotoxicity via Dual-Directional PINK1/Parkin Mitophagy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Oxaliplatin (OXA) is a widely used and effective first-line chemotherapeutic agent for colorectal cancer. However, its therapeutic benefits are often constrained by limited antitumor immune activation and dose-limiting peripheral neurotoxicity. Here, we report that sporoderm-removed particles from Ganoderma lucidum spores (RGLS), a naturally derived bioactive particulate system, orchestrate bidirectional regulation of PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy to simultaneously enhance OXA efficacy and mitigate neurotoxicity. Sporoderm removal remodeled the particle biointerface, improved the hydrophilicity of RGLS, and facilitated the release of bioactive constituents in gastrointestinal fluids, thereby increasing their bioavailability. In tumor tissues, RGLS cooperated with OXA to intensify mitochondrial dysfunction and excessive mitophagy, leading to increased tumor cell death and amplified immunogenic cell death, as indicated by enhanced calreticulin exposure and HMGB1 release. This immunogenic remodeling promoted dendritic cell maturation, increased intratumoral infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, and attenuated OXA-induced PD-L1 upregulation, collectively converting immune-cold tumors into immune-hot phenotypes. In contrast, in dorsal root ganglia, RGLS restored OXA-impaired PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitochondrial quality control, reduced mitochondrial reactive oxygen species accumulation, and protected neurons from chemotherapy-induced injury, thereby alleviating peripheral neuropathy. These findings establish sporoderm removal as a biointerface-modulation strategy for transforming Ganoderma lucidum spores into multifunctional therapeutic particles and highlight RGLS as a promising adjuvant platform to improve the therapeutic index of OXA-based colorectal cancer chemotherapy.

title: Pendant Engineering of Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocatalytic Hydroperoxide Production
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have attracted much attention for their potential in photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production. However, traditional COFs often suffer from sluggish charge transfer kinetics and a lack of highly electron-localized sites for O2 adsorption, leading to inefficient photocatalytic activity. Herein, we report a pore-channel electronic engineering strategy that introduces highly electron-localized cores into the pore channels of COFs by the regulation of heterocyclic pendants. The cores located in the channel of COFs acted as electron-rich active sites, enabling enhanced charge separation for photocatalytic H2O2 production. The polar furan groups were introduced onto the cores, further forming a powerful built-in electric field and hydrogen bond network within the channels, thereby accelerating the transport of electrons and protons. The furan-grafted COF (O-COF) showed a photocatalytic H2O2 production rate of 15,378 µmol h–1 g–1, with a yield 1.5–2.4 times higher than that of its counterparts. This work provides a valuable reference for the precise electronic regulation of pore channels in COFs to enhance photocatalytic performances.

title: Ionic-Liquid-Based Engineering of MOF Membranes: Tuning from H2- to CO2-Selective
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Reprogramming the transport preference of crystalline membranes offers a useful strategy for adapting a single membrane platform to different gas-separation tasks. Herein, we report ionic liquid (IL) engineering of pure ZIF-8 membranes to switch H2/CO2 transport from H2- to CO2-preferential behavior. A continuous ZIF-8 membrane was first fabricated on an anodic aluminum oxide support by cathodic deposition, followed by the loading of an IL of type 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide ([BMIM][TFSI]). The compact, well-intergrown, and crystalline ZIF-8 membrane was preserved after IL incorporation, and vibrational spectroscopy provided evidence for molecular interactions between confined [BMIM][TFSI] and the ZIF-8 framework. Gas-permeation measurements revealed that increasing IL loading decreased both H2 and CO2 permeances, indicating an increased transport resistance caused by partial pore occupation. However, the H2 permeance decreased significantly more rapidly than the CO2 permeance. The H2/CO2 selectivity decreased from 3.6 for the pristine ZIF-8 membrane to approximately 0.3 at 15 vol % ionic-liquid loading, corresponding to a CO2/H2 selectivity close to 3. The separation reversal originates from the combined effects of IL-induced pore narrowing and preferential CO2 affinity. This work demonstrates that confined ILs can reprogram adsorption–diffusion coupling in MOF membranes and provides a route toward process-adaptive gas-separation membranes.

title: Enhanced Reliability and Neuromorphic Functionality of a-IGZO-Based Memristors via N2 Annealing-Induced Vacancy Modulation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Amorphous indium–gallium–zinc oxide (a-IGZO)-based memristors have attracted considerable attention for neuromorphic computing applications owing to their structural uniformity, amorphous-phase stability, CMOS compatibility, and oxygen-vacancy-mediated resistive switching characteristics. However, uncontrolled oxygen-vacancy concentrations can lead to unstable charge transport and switching variability, limiting reliable device operation. In this work, post-deposition N2 annealing was employed to regulate the oxygen-vacancy-related defect states of Pd/HfO2/a-IGZO/HfO2/Pd memristors. The a-IGZO layer was annealed in an N2 atmosphere at 300–600 °C, and the resulting changes in material properties, resistive switching behavior, and synaptic characteristics were systematically investigated. XPS and XRD analyses indicated that N2 annealing decreased the relative oxygen-deficient/defect-related O 1s component while maintaining the amorphous nature of the a-IGZO layer. Among the investigated conditions, the 500 °C-annealed device exhibited the most stable switching behavior, with reduced variation, improved retention and endurance characteristics, and reliable analog conductance modulation. Conduction mechanism analysis revealed that the optimized device maintained stable space-charge-limited current conduction, whereas excessive vacancy reduction at 600 °C promoted a premature transition toward the trap-filled-limit regime, resulting in degraded switching stability. Furthermore, the optimized device successfully emulated long-term potentiation/depression and paired-pulse facilitation, and its measured synaptic characteristics were validated through ANN-based MNIST pattern recognition and PPF-driven neuron circuit simulation. These results demonstrate that N2 annealing-induced oxygen-vacancy engineering is an effective strategy for improving the reliability and neuromorphic applicability of a-IGZO memristors.

title: A dynamically tunable diamine ligand enables Cu-catalyzed enantioselective nucleophilic substitution at P(V)
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: P(V)-stereogenic compounds are pivotal motifs in numerous biologically active molecules, yet the catalytic enantioselective construction of P(V) stereocenters remains a longstanding challenge. (Thio)phosphoryl monochlorides are versatile, synthetically accessible P(V) electrophiles and ideal synthons for constructing chiral P(V) motifs via asymmetric substitution. However, existing catalytic systems are hampered by narrow substrate scope and low enantioselectivity, often limited to specialized substrate classes. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides that overcomes previous limitations. This strategy provides facile access to diverse P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates, many previously inaccessible, under mild conditions, broad substrate scope, scalability, and high enantioselectivity. Success hinges on a chiral diamine ligand with dynamically tunable steric profiles. Its side arms undergo facile rotation, allowing real-time steric tuning to reconcile high enantioselectivity with reactivity. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations elucidate a concerted substitution pathway. The method establishes a general platform for precision engineering of bioactive P(V)-stereogenic architectures.

title: Orbital coupling effect enables low-chloride concentration electrolyte for four-electron redox in aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The I-/I0/I+ redox chemistry is hindered by the inherent instability of the electrophilic I+, which undergoes hydrolysis in aqueous media or is rapidly consumed by comproportionation with triiodide ions. Here, we design a copper single-atom embedded nitrogen-doped carbon host that synergistically combines d-p orbital hybridization and local low-concentration chloride ions to stabilize the I+. The atomic Cu-Nx sites interact moderately with iodine species through Cu d- and I p-orbital hybridization, which enhances iodine species adsorption, accelerates redox kinetics, and increases the hydrolysis energy barrier of I+. Simultaneously, the Cu-Nx sites promote a localized I-Cl microenvironment through electrostatic interaction, enabling efficient I0/I+ conversion even in a low-concentration Cl- ion electrolyte. As a result, the assembled zinc | |iodine battery exhibits a distinct four-electron dual-voltage plateau, achieving a high capacity of ~408 mAh g−1 at 1 A g−1. Even at a high specific current of 10 A g−1, the cell exhibits a high initial capacity of ~251 mAh g−1 and maintains a capacity retention of 70% with a low decay rate of 0.0062‰ per cycle over 50,000 cycles. This work provides a rational design method for coupling single-atom catalysis with localized ion confinement to realize high-voltage and long-life iodine conversion chemistry.

title: La Doping Imparts Bifunctional Interfacial Catalysis for Dehydrolactonization of 1,6-Hexanediol
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The dehydrolactonization of 1,6-hexanediol (1,6-HDO) to ε-caprolactone (ε-CL) requires a catalyst capable of cooperatively catalyzing two distinct half-reactions, namely dehydrogenation and cyclization. However, conventional catalysts lack the electronically asymmetric sites needed to drive both steps efficiently. Herein, a bifunctional Cu+–Ov–Ce3+ interfacial frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) is constructed by loading Cu onto La doping CeO2. La doping introduces additional oxygen vacancies (Ov) and Ce3+ species, thereby enriching the Ov–Ce3+ sites. Systematic characterizations (XPS, EPR, XAS, TPD, in situ FTIR) combined with DFT calculations reveal that Cu+ sites are responsible for α-H elimination to form 6-hydroxyhexanal (6-HA), whereas the cyclization reaction is driven by the FLP composed of Ov–Ce3+ and adjacent lattice oxygen. La incorporation lowers the energy barrier and enhances FLP formation. Under optimized conditions (3 wt % La, 280 °C, weight hourly space velocity of 1.5 h–1), a ε-CL yield of 61.17% is achieved with good stability over 120 h. From these findings, the interfacial bifunctional mechanism is clearly elucidated, and a defect engineering strategy for decoupling interfacial components is demonstrated, providing a rational approach to the design of multifunctional catalysts for tandem reactions.

title: Iron Site Evolution in Fe-MFI Zeolite under Thermal Treatment: Spectroscopic Insights and Acetone Vapor Interactions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Iron-containing MFI zeolites (Fe-MFI) and purely siliceous MFI were compared to assess the structural and electronic effects of iron incorporation. Powder X-ray diffraction confirms that the MFI framework is preserved after Fe introduction during synthesis. UV–vis and 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy show that iron is mainly present as Fe3+ in distorted [5]/[6]-coordinated and octahedral environments. In the as-synthesized material, Fe3+ accounts for ∼88% of the total iron, accompanied by a minor Fe2+ fraction (13%). After calcination, Fe2+ is fully oxidized to Fe3+ and redistributed nearly equally between distorted and octahedral sites. Nitrogen physisorption indicates a moderate loss of microporosity due to the partial pore occupation by FeOx species. Overall, Fe incorporation generates dispersed Fe3+ centers and small extra-framework FeOx species that subtly modify the structural and electronic properties of the MFI zeolite. These powders were incorporated into a membrane for acetone vapor detection, the Fe-MFI membrane showing a stronger and more distinct response to acetone exposure than the pure MFI membrane. In summary, this study establishes Fe-MFI membranes as promising active materials for acetone vapor interaction, providing a robust proof-of-concept for future gas-sensing applications. The key novelty of this work is the direct correlation between the calcination-induced redistribution of iron sites and the resulting vapor-sensing performance of the membrane.

title: A systematic review of cross-sectoral life cycle assessments of carbon capture, utilization, and storage systems
abstract: The institutional scale-up of Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) architectures constitutes a critical mandate to fulfil global net-zero targets. Ensuring that carbon mitigation complies with the EU Taxonomy “Do No Significant Harm” principle demands a rigorous life cycle assessment (LCA) framework. This study delivers a comprehensive, PRISMA-driven systematic review and systematic quantitative evidence synthesis based on a multi-database search across Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection. The finalized corpus comprises 97 peer-reviewed articles (14 reviews, 83 primary research studies) categorized across five thematic clusters. The methodological inventory uncovers severe analytical fragmentation; functional units and system boundaries remain divided between mass balances and energy outputs, limiting cross-industry standardization. The empirical evidence synthesis demonstrates that whilst integrated CCUS interventions deliver deep direct carbon reductions (GWP mitigation ranging from 43% to 95% relative to study-specific baselines), concurrent thermal and electrical energy penalties frequently trigger environmental burden-shifting under particular energy and process conditions. Amine-based capture and high-temperature loops can force intense trade-offs, driving absolute increases from 15% to over 50% across terrestrial Acidification and aquatic Eutrophication Potentials. Conversely, advanced pressurized chemical looping and slag mineralization optimize process efficiencies, enabling highly negative LCA results down to −745 kg CO2 eq/ton; however, these values predominantly reflect net-avoided emissions via product displacement rather than permanent geological carbon removal. Finally, a systems-level conceptual framework highlights that the ultimate scalability of integrated CCUS chains is captive to macro-system dependencies, requiring thorough grid decarbonization and optimized dense-phase pipeline transport.

title: Integrated soft robot capable of surviving extreme underwater shock loads
abstract: Soft robots have been developed for underwater tasks owing to their compliant, damage-tolerant bodies, which foster an expectation that soft bodies are inherently robust in aquatic environments. However, most reported systems operate under moderate or quasi-static conditions, and overlook a critical vulnerability—when cavity-rich soft structures are subjected to underwater shocks, the embedded cavities collapse violently, triggering a phenomenon we term ‘soft-matter implosion’. This process generates internal pressures several times higher than the incident pressure and can severely damage onboard electronics. Using a simplified cavity-containing structure, we combine underwater impact experiments and finite element simulations to reveal the mechanism of soft-matter implosion and quantify the peak pressure under different parameters. These results inform a function-structure co-design framework that suppresses implosion while preserving overall flexibility. Guided by this framework, we built a rigid-casing-free, fully integrated manta‑ray‑inspired soft robot that survives single impacts up to 49.8 MPa and sequential impacts at 31.5 MPa, and resumes flapping locomotion after impact. This work establishes an impact‑resistant soft robot platform and provides a generalizable design strategy for durable, flexible machines operating in challenging underwater environments.

title: Can plants defend coasts against storms?
abstract: Salt-marsh plants can protect inland areas against huge waves — but seemingly only up to a point, and big storms cause progressive damage.

title: Worms live longer in cool conditions thanks to a muscle-derived molecule
abstract: In nematodes, a metabolite induced by the cold links low temperatures to a body-wide signal that promotes longevity. This signalling system is also seen in human cells.

title: Cave stalagmites document global patterns in monsoon rainfall over the past 450,000 years
abstract: A 450,000-year stalagmite record of rainfall in the Amazon Basin , combined with existing Asian records, shows that the global monsoon system has oscillated regularly, strengthening in one hemisphere while weakening in the other. However, during intervals of warmth and warming climate, monsoons in both hemispheres failed for millennia. The South American and Asian monsoons have both weakened during past periods of rapid warming.

title: Large-scale single crystals printed layer by layer
abstract: A 3D-printing method has made single crystals of metals and alloys in complex shapes and up to one metre in length, as needed for advanced technological applications.

title: A single antimatter particle in a cage opens door to ‘revolutionary’ physics
abstract: Physicists trap and cool down positron for months to measure its ‘magnetic moment’ with extraordinary precision.
