title: Plastics embedded with enzymes degrade readily in the sea
abstract: Embedding enzymes that break down ester bonds into compostable polyesters enables rapid and complete biodegradation even in microbe-scarce environments. This method is effective in marine sites ranging from coastal sea water to the deep sea, and could therefore contribute towards solving the global plastic pollution problem. Polyesters containing ester-bond-breaking enzymes could help to reduce plastic pollution in marine environments.

title: Rational Ionomer Design Directs Hydrogenation Pathways and Reactant Accessibility in Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ionomer engineering offers a powerful yet underexplored strategy for electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR), since the polymer tailors the microenvironment at the catalyst surface. Here, we rationally design high-performance ionomers by applying fixed-charge sign and hydration as design criteria. Synthetic anion-exchange ionomers (AEIs) enhance NO3– accessibility, and the highest AEI hydration is accompanied by a shift in the dominant hydrogenation pathway toward a favorable *H-mediated regime. Time-dependent attenuated total reflection surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) coupled with numerical simulation yields a 40.7-fold higher NO3– diffusion coefficient for the AEI than for Nafion. Potential-dependent in situ ATR-SEIRAS combined with kinetic isotope effect measurements and *H scavenging supports a pathway shift arising from a hydrated microenvironment enriched in free and weakly hydrogen-bonded water. The AEI-modified commercial Cu nanoparticle electrode reaches an NH3 yield rate of 13.8 mg h–1cm–2 and 98.0% Faradaic efficiency, positioning the fixed-charge sign and hydration as accessible design descriptors potentially transferable to other electrocatalytic reactions.

title: Cesium-Triiodide-Mediated Crystallization Regulation of Pure-Iodide Wide-Bandgap Perovskites Enables Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Solar Cells Exceeding 30% Efficiency
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pure-iodide wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites (∼1.68 eV) featuring eliminated photoinduced halide segregation are compelling top-cell absorbers for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells. However, their complex crystallization readily induces heterogeneous composition and structural defects, hindering performance improvements in the resulting devices. Here, we develop a cesium triiodide (CsI3)-mediated strategy to regulate intermediate-phase evolution of pure-iodide WBG perovskites. The CsI3-derived precursor chemistry reconstructs Pb-I coordination networks, suppresses premature organic-dominated intermediate nucleation, and promotes homogeneous phase conversion. The modulated crystallization pathway yields highly crystalline films with improved iodine uniformity and reduced non-radiative recombination losses. Consequently, single-junction solar cells achieve a stabilized power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 22.40%, which retains 95% of its initial efficiency after 1500 h of maximum power point tracking. More importantly, the associated perovskite-silicon solar cells deliver a stabilized PCE of 30.74% along with improved thermal stability, highlighting the great potential of pure-iodide WBG perovskites for efficient and durable tandem photovoltaics.

title: Electrically Enabled Isothermal CeO2 Thermochemical Water Splitting below 900 °C
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ceria-based thermochemical cycles offer a promising route to solar hydrogen, but require reduction above 1400 °C and large temperature swings. Here, building on electrically assisted CeO2 reduction, we demonstrate repeated isothermal CeO2-based water-splitting cycles at 700–900 °C and 0.5–2.0 V. Porous CeO2−YSZ bilayer pellets with different composition ratios undergo electrically assisted reduction and steam re-oxidation at the same temperature, producing O2 and H2 in separate steps without thermal cycling. The process reaches H2/O2 ratios up to 1.9, reproducible H2 productivity over 10 cycles, and H2 yields up to 49 ± 2 μmol gCeO2−1 cycle−1 after only 20 min of electrically assisted reduction. Extended-reduction experiments show that the best composition remains only ∼0.10 V below the applied bias on an equivalent thermodynamic-voltage basis. Reactor-scale projections based on gas utilization in an existing ceria reactor give a solar-to-H2 efficiency of 5.6% without assuming improvements to the CeO2−YSZ architecture.

title: The anatomy of a personal health agent
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Large language models are enabling a new generation of health agents, yet their ability to address the diverse needs of individuals in everyday health settings remains underexplored
                    1,2
                    . Here we developed a comprehensive personal health agent that reasons over multimodal data from consumer wellness devices and medical records to provide personalized health support. Through analysis of web search and health forum queries, together with user-centred research involving end users and health experts, we identified four key user journeys: general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice, and symptom assessment. These journeys informed three specialist sub-agents: (1) a data science agent that analyses longitudinal wearable and medical data, incorporating population-level statistics to contextualize numerical insights; (2) a health domain expert agent that integrates personal and contextual data with health knowledge to generate personalized insights; and (3) a health coach agent that synthesizes insights, supports multi-turn interaction and goal setting, applies specified psychological strategies and tracks progress. We integrated these capabilities in the personal health agent, an open-source multi-agent framework for dynamic, personalized health interactions. We evaluated the sub-agents and full system across 11 benchmark tasks using automated and human evaluation, with more than 7,000 annotations and 1,350 h of effort from health experts and end users. This represents the most comprehensive evaluation of a personal health agent thus far and provides a concrete foundation for improving access to high-quality personalized health support more broadly.

title: Enzyme-embedded polyesters for accelerated biodegradation in the deep sea
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The accumulation of persistent plastics in the ocean is causing wide-ranging environmental problems
                    1–3
                    . Some commercially available compostable plastics
                    4–7
                    , developed to address these issues, degrade efficiently under industrial composting conditions; however, their degradation in marine environments, particularly in the deep sea, remains limited
                    8–10
                    . Here we demonstrate that thermally embedding enzymes into compostable polyesters (poly(butylene succinate) (PBS), poly(butylene succinate-
                    co
                    -adipate) (PBSA), poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) and poly(butylene adipate-
                    co
                    -terephthalate) (PBAT)) significantly accelerates their degradation in both coastal and deep-sea environments from water depths of 2–6 m to 5,503 m. Enzyme-embedded polyesters achieved near-complete degradation at a deep-sea depth of 757 m within 5 months. Furthermore, moderate biodegradation of enzyme-embedded polyesters was observed under extreme conditions on deep-sea floors of 5,503 m. In coastal seawater, films embedded with trace amounts (0.1 wt%) of enzyme underwent rapid degradation. The mechanical properties of enzyme-embedded polyesters were similar to those of enzyme-free polyesters. Chemical analysis confirmed the formation of low-molecular-mass degradation products and biochemical oxygen demand measurements supported the mineralization of the enzyme-embedded polyesters. The enzyme-embedding strategy enables enhanced marine degradation of compostable polyesters and represents a potential solution to marine plastic pollution.

title: The right of way in Dublin
abstract: At the front gate of Trinity College Dublin, trams, buses, taxis, bicycles and pedestrians compete for the same seconds of green. Xiaowen Tao reflects on how a city decides, signal by signal, who goes first and whose time is worth more, and argues that those decisions deserve to be debated as openly as any other public choice.

title: Institutional lock-in in urban building may constrain climate ambitions
abstract: Cities are moving from climate pledges to delivery, yet construction rules still reward inherited routines. Using timber as an analytical lens, we highlight how institutional lock-in could delay low-carbon material transitions even as carbon caps and supply-chain scrutiny tighten.

title: Solar vapor generation technologies: fundamentals, innovations and applications
abstract: This Tutorial Review establishes a unified framework connecting the fundamentals of solar vapor generation with materials and structural design, providing guiding principles for efficient, scalable, and sustainable water production.

title: Recent applications of asymmetric hydrogenation in total synthesis of natural products and drugs
abstract: This review focuses on recent advances of asymmetric hydrogenation in the strategic total synthesis of natural products and drug molecules, and outlines future perspectives for this field.

title: Programming hot-carrier dynamics in gold nanoclusters for high-gain photodetectors
abstract: Gold nanoclusters have long been limited in optoelectronic applications by sub-picosecond hot-carrier cooling. Here, electron-donating ligands spatially separate the frontier orbitals of Au22 nanoclusters, extending hot-carrier lifetime to nanoseconds and enabling high-performance, stable photodetectors. This work establishes ligand engineering as a general strategy to tune excited-state dynamics in metal nanoclusters, offering chemists a new materials design route for next-generation optoelectronics beyond conventional semiconductors.

title: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Interactions among species are increasingly recognized as key determinants of climate change impacts on ecosystems
                    1–5
                    . However, we know little about how climatic perturbations affect interactions among top vertebrate predators. Here we show that, when an emergent disease caused the decline of shared prey (rabbits), after decades of neutral co-existence a mammalian carnivore (lynx) started to prey heavily on a top predatory raptor (kites). These predation bouts occurred exclusively under drought conditions and when lynx found rabbit remains under the raptor nests, consistent with the removal of a potential competitor. Drought-induced lynx predation depressed lifetime reproductive success and triggered territory abandonment and dispersal by the raptor, suggestive of a new arms race among predators. A reduction in raptor abundance was associated with an increase in an insectivorous bird (a small owl), showing that the new interaction had the potential to reach lower trophic levels. These results underline the importance of diet flexibility and mobility as important mediators of resilience to stressors. In the future, synergistic effects of multiple anthropogenic stressors may reshape the interactions and ecological roles of many apex predators, with potential cascading consequences for whole ecosystems. A key to forecasting the future impact of global change may reside in understanding how behavioural flexibility and interacting keystone species respond to interacting shocks.

title: De novo design of enantioselective artificial metalloenzyme photocatalysts
abstract: The ability to create protein scaffolds that impart enantioselectivity to simple, readily available metal catalysts could redefine the landscape of asymmetric catalysis. Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs), hybrid catalysts that combine a synthetic metal cofactor with a protein scaffold, offer a potential means to achieve this goal, but scaffold discovery has remained constrained by trial-and-error approaches and the functional limits of extant proteins.1–5 This challenge is acute for metal polypyridine photocatalysts, which are widely used in visible-light chemistry but have not enabled highly enantioselective photocatalysis within protein scaffolds. In this study, we show that generative protein design6–8 can create de novo scaffolds that selectively bind these photocatalysts and that directed evolution converts the resulting artificial metalloenzymes into efficient, highly enantioselective photocatalysts9. The evolved proteins support diverse light-driven reactions, high catalyst turnover and catalyst recycling, and can function with commercially available racemic metal complexes. Spectroscopic studies show that the protein environment extends the photocatalyst excited-state lifetime and organizes substrate near the cofactor, altering energy transfer and controlling stereoselectivity. These findings establish de novo protein design as a route to functional scaffolds for synthetic metal complexes that lack natural protein partners and provide a strategy for combining protein design and evolution to control non-natural catalytic chemistry.

title: Using AI to offer personalized health advice
abstract: The use of artificial-intelligence tools in medicine is increasing. What types of technology might be on the horizon and how can such health-advice tools be tested?

title: Teen depression and anxiety predicted by childhood brain development
abstract: Analysis of nearly 30,000 brain scans yields detailed timeline of how the brain matures — and hints at the consequences of disrupting it.

title: Global emissions slow — but world hurtles towards 2 °C of warming
abstract: The United Nations’ latest climate report is a stark reminder that limiting warming to the safest levels is now likely out of reach.

title: An AI tool improves weather forecasts up to a month ahead
abstract: An innovative artificial-intelligence application enhances weather forecasting in the difficult subseasonal range, providing accurate forecasts of precipitation, temperature and pressure 3–5 weeks in advance. The tool refines both physics- and AI-based weather models and improves the early prediction of extremes of heat, cold, rainfall and flooding. The tool boosts the ability of physics- and AI-based forecasting models to predict typical and extreme weather events.

title: Surprise! White dwarf stars come in a rainbow of colours
abstract: Analysis of some nearby stars shows that, despite their name, these bodies can be pink, yellow and more.

title: Scientists put a salt marsh in a giant wave-machine: here's what they learned
abstract: Experiment shows how these ecosystems could protect coastlines from huge storms — plus, new evidence hints at what Denisovans might have looked like.

title: To heal sick cities, scientists and residents must work together
abstract: Tolullah Oni has developed a platform to transfer the intellectual capital of African diaspora scholars back to the continent.

title: AI doctors’ orders come with a sky-high bill
abstract: Large language models suggest more tests, referrals and medications than human physicians do, driving up the cost of care.

title: Daily briefing: How tech billionaires are changing science funding
abstract: Ultra-rich philanthropists are disrupting biomedical science. Plus, why physicists have kept an antimatter particle caged for months and whether it’s really possible to be swallowed by a whale and survive.

title: Helical Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters for High‐Performance Anti‐Quenching Narrowband Blue OLEDs
abstract: ABSTRACT Multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) has established a new approach for narrowband blue organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs), yet effectively suppressing intermolecular interactions especially at high doping concentrations while preserving the intrinsic narrowband emission remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel designing paradigm is proposed for achieving anti‐quenching narrowband emission in MR‐TADF molecules by embedding the indeno[2,1‐b]carbazole unit into the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon skeleton. The proof‐of‐concept emitter DT‐BON1 reveals a favorable twist angle of 31.8°, manifesting formation of helical architecture within MR core. As a result, the emission peaks and full width at half maximum show virtually no variation with changing doping concentration from 1 wt% to 20 wt%. Moreover, the photoluminance quantum yields exceed 90% even at 20 wt% doping concentration endowed by the outstanding anti‐quenching characteristics. The DT‐BON1 based OLEDs can achieve maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE max ) of exceeding 30%. Especially, the alleviated exciton quenching effects can be firmly demonstrated by marginally decreased EQE max values, attaining 29.2% in 10 wt%‐based OLEDs and 27.3% even in heavily doped devices (20 wt%), which is at a record high for MR‐TADF with blue emission at such high doping concentration.

title: Supramolecular Enforcement of Planar Tetracoordinate Halides
abstract: ABSTRACT Planar tetracoordinate halides have been widely explored by quantum computational approaches but remain rare as deliberately targeted experimental motifs. Here we show that these geometries can be accessed by supramolecular enforcement, and challenge its connection to the VSEPR model. Bowl‐shaped calix[4]pyrrolato indium units preorganize four lithium ions into a confined Li 4 pocket that traps Cl − , Br − , and I − in strongly flattened to ideal planar tetracoordinate environments. Computational analysis of the parent tetrahedral [Li 4 X] 3 + units reveals small planarization energies that can be overcome by a charge‐attenuating host of appropriate shape. The experimental series shows that halide planarity is highly sensitive to subtle supramolecular effects, such as calix[4]pyrrolato doming and crystal packing, experimentally confirming the generally low angular deformation energies. The results establish supramolecular enforcement as a rational design principle for planar tetracoordinate heavier halides and show that such motifs are accessible outcomes of engineered electrostatic cavities.

title: Anion‐Cation Targeted Regulation Enables Ultrafast and Stable Sodium Metal Batteries at Low Temperatures
abstract: ABSTRACT Anion‐dominated solvation and artificial interfacial engineering have been intensively pursued for low‐temperature sodium‐metal batteries (SMBs), yet they face constraints from temperature‐sensitive solvation dynamics and interfacial control. Here we propose anion‐cation‐targeted regulation via Sn(OTf) 2 that simultaneously constructs a solvent‐reinforced solvation structure and electrochemically induces an alloy‐based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) (Na 15 Sn 4 ), which goes beyond the prevailing anion‐centric strategy to address the critical challenges of SMBs at subzero temperatures. Competitive Sn 2+ ‐Na + coordination excludes PF 6 − from the primary solvation sheath, while OTf − and the ether groups of diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (DEGDME) coupling foster a solvent‐dominated configuration, substantially reducing the Na + desolvation energy barrier at low temperatures. This design enables Na||Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 cells to deliver a recorded 1050 cycles at −20°C and 20 C, and nearly 700 cycles at −50°C. Ah‐scale pouch cells sustain durable 450 cycles at −20°C, with a 6 Ah cell reaching 215 Wh kg −1 at 25°C (total cell mass). Our findings resolve the longstanding trade‐off between low‐temperature kinetics and stability in SMBs, offering a new design rationale beyond conventional interfacial engineering.

title: Unidirectional Hydrogen Migration Through Interfacial Engineering for Promoted Brønsted Acid Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Though playing a critical role, the controllable and directional migration of reactive species in chemical reactions is still hard to achieve. Here, we propose an interfacial engineering strategy for constructing a hydrogen spillover nanodiode that channels hydrogen unidirectionally. Such a nanodiode design is materialized in a composite WO x /TiO 2 /Pt catalyst with spatially separated structure, where WO x and Pt particles are dispersed on the outer and inner surfaces of porous TiO 2 nanotubes, respectively. This nanodevice permits forward H migration (Pt→TiO 2 →WO x ) while suppresses the reverse path (WO x →TiO 2 ), as directly evidenced by in situ x‐ray absorption fine structure characterization under hydrogenation and H 2 generation reactions. This rectification behavior originates from the diode characteristics of the TiO 2 –WO x heterojunction, which hinders both proton and electron transfer from WO x to TiO 2 . Consequently, WO x /TiO 2 /Pt accumulates highly concentrated Brønsted acid sites in H 2 atmosphere and thus exhibits superior catalytic performance compared to the closely contacted WO x –Pt/TiO 2 catalyst. Up to 5.3 times higher liquid alkane yield has been achieved over WO x /TiO 2 /Pt relative to WO x –Pt/TiO 2 in the polyethylene hydrocracking reaction. This nanodiode design strategy is general and can be extended to other catalysts/species, offering mechanistic insight and boosting catalytic performance in diverse reactions.

title: Tailoring Crystal Facets Enables Scalable Synthesis of Highly Dispersed Single Crystal NCM90
abstract: ABSTRACT The single crystal cathodes show significant superiority in cycling stability and safety, but are restricted by high costs, as current preparation strategies often lead to particle agglomeration. Here, we develop a new strategy of surface high‐valence metal doping to prepare the highly dispersed single crystal LiNi 0.90 Mn 0.05 Co 0.05 O 2 (SC‐NCM90) in low‐cost. The surface substitution of Ni 2+/3+ by W 6+ /Mo 6+ facilitates to enhancing the bond with O, suppressing cation interdiffusion, benefiting particle dispersion, and high voltage stability. The surface Mo‐doping lowers the energy of (104) plane and stimulates its prior growth, favoring fast Li + ‐migration and endowing the Mo 6+ ‐doped SC‐NCM90 with the capacity of 111.0 mAh g −1 at 5C, achieving the desired fast charging for SC‐NCM90. W‐doping facilitates the growth of both (003) and (104) planes, benefiting the particle segregation, as (003) plane inhibits ionic fusion. W‐ and Mo‐doped SC‐NCM90 deliver markedly improved cycling life and safety performance than polycrystalline NCM90. This work establishes the strategy of high‐valence elemental surface doping as a dual‐functional paradigm that simultaneously manipulates crystal facet evolution for suppressing particle agglomeration and fortifies transition metal (TM)─O bonding for stabilizing interface, producing highly dispersed SC‐NCM90 with faster charging capability and durability.

title: Electric Double Layer‐Driven Surface Reconstruction Enables Cooperative Zn(002)/(101) Growth for High‐Utilization Zinc Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc batteries are limited by the mismatch between dynamic interfacial chemistry and anisotropic Zn crystallization. Here, imidazolidinyl urea (IDU) is used to couple electric double layer (EDL) reconstruction with Zn surface reorganization. IDU preferentially enriches at the Zn/electrolyte interface, displaces interfacial water, and interacts strongly with Zn(100). In situ spectroscopic ellipsometry, quartz crystal microbalance, and neutron reflectivity reveal transient removal and reconstruction of surface Zn rather than simple molecular adsorption. The reconstructed interface suppresses Zn(100) and promotes cooperative Zn(002)/(101) evolution, enabling compact deposition with favorable kinetics. Meanwhile, the water‐deficient EDL and hybrid organic‐inorganic interphase inhibit parasitic reactions and stabilize the interfacial environment. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells cycle for over 6000 h at 4 mA cm −2 and 2 mAh cm −2 , while Zn||Cu cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.81% over 3000 cycles. Stable operation is further maintained at −10°C and under high Zn utilization. Zn||CVO full cells retain 75% capacity after 650 cycles at an N/P ratio of 2.9, and a 21 mAh pouch cell preserves 84% capacity after 400 cycles. This work links EDL reconstruction with crystallographic evolution to enable highly reversible and practically relevant Zn metal anodes.

title: Dual Anion‐Involved Interfacial Chemistry Enables Ultra‐Stable PEO‐Based Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries by Suppressing NMP‐Induced Side Reactions
abstract: ABSTRACT The incorporation of solvent N‐methylpyrrolidone (NMP) into polyethylene oxide (PEO) weakens EO‐Li + interaction and boosts Li + transport via strong Li + affinity, but free NMP inevitably reacts with Li metal, undermining interface stability. Herein, we report a dual‐anion coordination strategy that repurposes the residual NMP from a “side‐reaction source” into a “functional component”. LiDFOB and LiNO 3 are introduced as dual‐salt additives into an NMP‐containing PEO/LiTFSI system. Leveraging the preferential coordination of DFOB– and NO 3 – with Li + , an anion‐enriched solvation sheath is constructed, which strengthens the Li + ‐NMP interactions. The modified coordination environment facilitates the preferential formation of a kinetically stable, anion‐derived solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), effectively mitigating interfacial side reactions between the NMP and Li metal. As a result, the obtained electrolyte delivers a high ionic conductivity of 1.69 × 10 −4 S cm −1 and stable cycling over 1200 h at room temperature. The assembled Li/LFP cell exhibits a high capacity retention of 93% after 2000 cycles. Even at room temperate and 0°C, the assembled Li/LFP cell maintains stable and efficient cycling. This work establishes a universal solvent structure tailoring strategy to regulate reactive solvent molecules, opening a fresh avenue for high‐performance PEO‐based solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

title: Synergistic Proton Transport Regulation and Interfacial Anion Adsorption Engineering in ZIF‐8‐Derived PtCu Electrocatalysts for High‐Performance Light and Heavy‐Duty PEM Fuel Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Engineering catalyst‐ionomer interfaces is critical for overcoming the coupled kinetic and transport limitations that impede the commercialization of low‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (LT‐PEMFCs). Herein, a PtCu alloy supported on a zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8‐derived 3D‐hierarchical carbon framework is developed to simultaneously regulate proton transport and interfacial anion adsorption within the catalyst layer. Oxophilic Cu preferentially interacts with Nafion's sulfonate groups, mitigating excessive adsorption on Pt, while the 3D‐hierarchical porous architecture promotes homogeneous ionomer distribution, continuous proton‐conduction pathways, and efficient water transport. Hydrogen underpotential deposition (HUPD) half‐cell analysis across various concentrations of Nafion revealed Temkin‐type adsorption features and demonstrated weakened Nafion adsorption following Cu incorporation, supported by various physical and theoretical analyses. The optimized catalyst exhibits a reduced Tafel slope of 55.8 mV dec − 1 , delivering 0.75 A mg Pt −1 at 0.90 V IR‐free under H 2 ‐O 2 operation, exceeding the U.S. DOE target. Membrane electrode assemblies achieved 1.52 and 1.80 A cm − 2 at 0.70 V under light‐ and heavy‐duty conditions after 30k accelerated stress‐test cycles. Sequential Distribution of Relaxation Time impedance analysis further demonstrates that synergistic regulation of catalyst‐ionomer interactions and proton transport simultaneously mitigates kinetic, ohmic, and mass‐transport losses, providing a general design strategy for high‐performance LT‐PEMFC.

title: An Ultrathin Ionic COF Self‐Supporting Proton Exchange Membrane Through Stacking of Few‐Layer Nanosheets Grown From High‐Curvature Micro‐Interface for Fuel Cell
abstract: ABSTRACT Ultrathin self‐supporting ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) proton exchange membranes (PEM) are crucial for low‐resistance sustainable energy applications but remain challenging to fabricate. The key to fabricating ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF membranes lies in the compact stacking of iCOF nanosheets, which remains inaccessible through micro‐interfacial polymerization systems. Herein, we report for the first time an ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF PEM constructed by growing few‐layer iCOF nanosheets at high‐curvature micro‐interfaces, alongside a proposed growth mechanism. The curved iCOF exhibits reduced interlayer attraction due to a twisted configuration, and enhanced solvation‐driven exfoliation arising from greater exposure of sulfonic acid groups to water. It avoids the commonly reported nanosphere‐like morphologies in previously reported micro‐interfacial assembly systems by regulating the oil‐in‐water microemulsion interface using weakly surface‐active octanoic acid, which effectively balances between the confined oil phase growth and the unconfined aqueous phase exfoliation. As‐prepared iCOF few‐layer nanosheets (1.3–1.5 nm) expose abundant reactive terminal groups for interlayer crosslinking under the vacuum filtration pressure gradient, leading to ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF PEM (3.2–15.1 µm) with compact layer stacking, good mechanical robustness, and excellent scalability (20 cm in diameter). A fuel cell peak power density of 2017.7 mW cm −2 at 80°C is achieved, surpassing recently reported iCOF‐based membranes.

title: Vortex-mediated spin current injection into two-dimensional superconductor NbSe2
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Injection of pure spin current into superconductors remains a major challenge in superconducting spintronics. Previous studies have primarily focused on spin-polarized quasiparticles and spin-triplet supercurrents, while vortices—ubiquitous topological defects in type-II superconductors—have been theoretically proposed as alternative carriers of spin angular momentum, yet direct experimental evidence is still lacking. Here, we report the vortex-mediated spin current injection in NbSe
                    2
                    /LiAl
                    2
                    Fe
                    3
                    O
                    8
                    (LAFO) bilayer, an Ising superconductor/ferrimagnetic insulator heterostructure. Under an out-of-plane temperature gradient and an in-plane magnetic field, the NbSe
                    2
                    /LAFO bilayer shows a pronounced thermoelectric peak near the upper critical magnetic field, which has the opposite sign to the conventional vortex Nernst signal observed in a single-layer NbSe
                    2
                    . The sign reversal suggests that the vortex flow induced by spin current injection is opposite to the flow driven by the temperature gradient, which is consistent with theoretical mechanisms including spin-vorticity transmutation and the inverse vortex spin Hall effect. By mapping the field–temperature phase diagram, we reveal that the spin current injection occurs exclusively in the vortex liquid phase of NbSe
                    2
                    . Absence of the thermoelectric signal above the superconducting transition temperature further rules out the quasiparticle contribution. Our results establish vortices as efficient carriers of spin information in superconductors, opening a new route towards vortex-mediated superconducting spintronic devices.

title: Stable coexistence and transport of lytic phage infections with migrating bacterial hosts
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Bacteriophages (phages), viruses that exclusively infect bacteria, coexist with their bacterial hosts across diverse environments at densities exceeding 10
                    7
                     per milliliter in marine surface waters, 10
                    8
                     per milliliter in soils, and 10
                    9
                     per milliliter in the human gut. In contrast, phage lysis of bacterial populations within well-mixed in vitro environments select for the emergence of phage-resistant bacterial mutants, which, in turn, select for host-range expansion phage mutants and, typically, the collapse of phage populations altogether. This gap in outcome raises a question: What enables long-term phage-bacteria coexistence? Here, we show how interactions in space can facilitate stable coexistence and long-range transport of virulent phage along with migrating bacteria. Combining theory, simulation, and experiments across multiple phage-bacteria systems, we reveal a chemotaxis-driven mechanism that robustly stabilizes coexistence and dispersal of virulent phages with migrating hosts. These findings suggest the ecological relevance of spatial interaction mechanisms that reinforce stability between antagonistic partners in the absence of perpetual cycles of defense and counterdefense, which may be broadly applicable across phage-bacteria systems.

title: Anomalous phonon selection rules and Raman optical activity in RuO2
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Breakdown of selection rules and emergence of optical activity in Raman spectroscopy typically signal symmetry-breaking events essential for understanding novel phases of solids. Here, we apply our recently developed rotational anisotropy Raman spectroscopy technique to single-crystal ruthenium dioxide—a compound of recent interest as a candidate workhorse material for altermagnetism yet whose magnetic ground state remains under intense debate. Our data reveal a salient breakdown of selection rules for zone-center phonons, accompanied by clear splitting in the angle-dependent polarimetry plots for the two opposite helicity-nonconserving circularly polarized scattering channels. These observations provide definitive evidence of a previously overlooked symmetry-breaking event, involving either spatial or time-reversal symmetry. In either scenario, the underlying mechanism is likely a bulk hidden order parameter, potentially involving multipole moments of Ruthenium(IV) set by the local crystal field environment. Our work demonstrates how subtle symmetry-breaking events can manifest through lattice dynamics and calls for renewed experimental and theoretical efforts to map the phase diagram of ruthenium dioxide as a system poised near quantum phase transition boundaries.

title: Distinct chalcophile-element inheritance from subducted continental crust in metasomatized mantle
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Subduction recycles surface materials into the mantle and shapes its chemical evolution. Whether continental subduction leaves chalcophile-element imprints in the mantle that differ from those of oceanic subduction remains poorly understood. Here, we show that primitive basaltic magmas from the North China Craton exhibit pronounced copper depletion, silver enrichment, and low copper/silver (200 to 1200), together with continental crust–like trace element patterns and radiogenic-isotope compositions. These features contrast sharply with those of the convective mantle, mid-ocean ridge basalts, and oceanic arc basalts, and reflect chemical signatures inherited from subducted continental crust and retained over geological timescales in metasomatized domains of a relatively cold lithospheric mantle. Coupled lead enrichment and unradiogenic lead-isotope signatures further identify metasomatized mantle as an important reservoir of Earth’s unradiogenic lead. Our results reveal distinct modes of chalcophile-element recycling and mantle inheritance during continental and oceanic subduction, with broad implications for mantle chemical evolution and the critical-metal fertility of continental lithosphere.

title: Classical quantum chemical solution of the FeMo-cofactor model to chemical accuracy and its implications
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: We use classical quantum chemistry methods to estimate the ground-state energy to chemical accuracy in a model of the FeMo cofactor of nitrogenase, which is widely studied as a target of quantum computing. Our result relies on the insight that the ground-state problem can be characterized as one of ranking many competing, but largely single-configuration, states. This allows a combination of systematic high-order coupled cluster and density matrix renormalization group calculations together with an extrapolation protocol to obtain an accurate energy. Within the model, we identify several spin isomer candidates for the ground state that are degenerate to chemical accuracy. Beyond this model, we characterize the impact of additional electronic excitations and the cluster and protein geometric fluctuations on the low-lying electronic landscape. We find that many features of the landscape are retained in more detailed representations of nitrogenase, which points to the complexity of spectroscopic interpretations of the electronic structure of the FeMo cofactor.

title: High ambipolar mobility fluorinated MXene for ultrasensitive biosensing transistors
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) are emerging as transformative materials for bioelectronics. However, the advancement of MXene-based field-effect transistor (FET) biosensors is hindered by the lack of high-quality aqueous-stable materials and the low signal transduction efficiency intrinsic to their metallic nature. To address these issues, we report an ultrasensitive biosensing platform enabled by an in-situ fluorination strategy of MXene. By substituting unstable oxygen-containing terminations with chemically stable fluorine terminations in a mild reaction, we synthesized high-quality fluorinated MXene with the record-breaking ambipolar field-effect mobility (μ
                    p
                     = 10.42 cm
                    2
                     V
                    −1
                     s
                    −1
                    , μ
                    n
                     = 30.23 cm
                    2
                     V
                    −1
                     s
                    −1
                    ). The highly electronegative fluorinated interface suppresses interfacial electrical double-layer capacitance, boosting signal transduction efficiency. Consequently, the platform achieves the lowest limit of detection (LOD) of 0.26 fg ml
                    −1
                    for
                    Mycobacterium tuberculosis
                    antigen MPT64 among MXene FETs up to date, accompanied by a high current response of 35.02% at LOD. Clinical validation across 126 serum samples demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 97.6% with a detection time of 38 s, exhibiting the high-performance and reliable biosensing in complex physiological environments.

title: Multiple allosteric sites allow for synergistic enhancement of GPCR signaling
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Allosteric modulation of G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers promising therapeutic opportunities. Although multiple allosteric binding sites have been identified in GPCRs, whether and how these spatially distinct sites cooperate to regulate receptor activation remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of cooperative multisite allostery in the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We developed two novel D1R positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), UNC9815 and UNC10062, and used cryo–electron microscopy to structurally identify two previously uncharacterized D1R allosteric sites occupied by UNC9815/UNC10062 and another D1R PAM, BMS-A1. Both sites localize to the transmembrane helix (TM) 1 to 7 interface as vertically adjacent allosteric pockets organized in a spatially complementary manner. Our structures demonstrate the simultaneous binding of the chemically distinct PAMs (LY3154207, BMS-A1, and UNC9815/UNC10062) in three nonoverlapping pockets. Concurrent engagement of all three allosteric sites produces pronounced functional cooperativity, increasing dopamine potency by >1000-fold, thereby demonstrating that coordinated multisite modulation can achieve substantial pharmacological amplification beyond the limits imposed by single PAM administration. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that multisite PAM engagement restricts intracellular loop 3 dynamics and stabilizes the TM7-NPxxY activation motif, effects not achieved by binding of LY3154207 alone, thereby biasing the receptor toward a more stabilized active conformation, and may also improve agonist potency by stabilizing extracellular loop 2. Together, these findings establish the structural framework for cooperative multisite allostery in a GPCR, revealing how distributed allosteric sites act in concert to amplify receptor activation and providing a conceptual foundation for developing innovative GPCR allosteric therapeutics.

title: RanGAP1 coordinates the ER-lamina interface to drive de novo nuclear envelope reassembly in mouse embryos
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Nuclear envelope (NE) reassembly is essential for the zygote-to-totipotency transition in mammalian embryos. Beyond its classical roles in nuclear transport and maintenance of the RanGTP gradient, the function of RanGAP1 in embryonic NE reassembly has remained elusive. Here, we show that RanGAP1 localizes to the early embryonic NE, driving reassembly via a distinct structural mechanism. Trim-Away–mediated RanGAP1 depletion causes two-cell stage arrest and severe NE defects, including nuclear pore complex (NPC) loss, failed reassembly, and aberrant “fishnet” membrane structures. Mechanistically, RanGAP1 establishes a structural paradigm for endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–lamina coupling by recruiting Lamin A/C, B1, and B2 to the ER for coassembly. The acidic domain and SUMO-1 modification at Lys
                    526
                    (K526) are essential for the NPC localization of RanGAP1. Thus, RanGAP1 orchestrates nuclear lamina (NL) assembly by targeting lamins to the ER. These findings uncover mechanisms of NE reassembly that are critical for early embryogenesis and provide insights into NE-related developmental disorders.

title: Predicting upcoming visual features during eye movements yields scene representations aligned with human visual cortex
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Natural scenes are complex arrangements of objects, surfaces, and backgrounds. For the brain’s visual system to effectively operate, it needs to extract not only what objects are present but also their spatial and semantic relations. We hypothesize that such structures may be learned, in a self-supervised fashion, by exploiting temporal regularities of natural active vision: Each fixation reveals a glimpse that is related to the previous one via co-occurrence and saccade-conditioned spatial regularities. We instantiate this idea with glimpse prediction networks (GPNs), recurrent models trained to predict the embedding of the next glimpse along human-like scanpaths. GPNs are shown to successfully extract complex scene information, including object co-occurrences and spatial object arrangements, and integrate information across glimpses. GPN representations align strongly with human fMRI responses in mid- and higher-level visual cortex and match, often outperform, alternative state-of-the-art ANN models, establishing next-glimpse-prediction as a biologically plausible route toward brain-aligned scene representations.

title: Staphylococcus aureus wall teichoic acid structure dictates virulence potential and resistance to host defenses
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Staphylococcus aureus
                    is a formidable pathogen and the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections. We recently showed that the highly conserved
                    sasF
                    gene, encoding for an uncharacterized sortase-anchored surface protein, is up-regulated when
                    S. aureus
                    colonizes skin. Here, we demonstrate that SasF is an enzyme that has glycoside epimerase activity, which is required for
                    S. aureus
                    resistance to skin fatty acids. Mutants of
                    sasF
                    are highly impaired in skin colonization and acute infection models. The SasF enzyme is crucial for maintaining the structure of wall teichoic acids and proper
                    S. aureus
                    surface chemistry. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a bacterial surface epimerase in this pathogen, suggesting that SasF could be a therapeutic target.

title: CCAN forms the spherical shell-like structure in interphase kinetochores
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The kinetochore is an essential structure for the faithful chromosome segregation during mitosis. The 16-protein complex known as the constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN) localizes the centromere throughout the cell cycle and forms the basis of the kinetochore. Although cryo–electron microscopy has provided a structural model of an individual CCAN unit, how multiple CCAN units are organized within cells remains unclear. Here, using in silico and in vivo analyses, we demonstrate that multiple CCAN units form a spherical shell-like structure in interphase DT40 kinetochores. CENP-T and CENP-N localize to the CCAN shell, whereas the CENP-C cupin domain clusters at the center. Molecular dynamics simulations of CCAN assembly suggest that CENP-C–DNA interactions constrain the orientation of CCAN units, supporting a spherical shell-like organization via CENP-C oligomerization. Super-resolution imaging reveals the spherical shell-like structure at DT40 kinetochores, and CENP-C knockout or expression of a CENP-C DNA binding deficient mutant abolishes the structure, consistent with the simulation-derived model. These findings provide important insights into the spatial organization of functional kinetochores within cells.

title: Ultrasonic metamaterial at MHz frequencies using microstructured glass
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Acoustic metamaterials enhance traditional material properties, providing opportunities to shape sound fields in applications ranging from biomedical imaging and clinical therapy to nondestructive testing. However, at the megahertz frequency range, only a few metamaterial architectures exist. They are often highly attenuating or difficult to manufacture and generally provide limited control. Here, we introduce a megahertz-frequency ultrasonic metamaterial based on laser-engraved glass. By structuring metavoxels with different engraving patterns, we define an anisotropic metamaterial exhibiting local variations in the sound speed of up to 20% compared to unstructured glass and losses 100× lower than in comparable three-dimensional–printed metamaterials. We use this metamaterial to define a library of standard elements that can be modularly combined to shape complex-patterned ultrasonic fields. Our experiments are supported by a theoretical model, which provides additional insights into the microstructural origin of the metamaterial behavior and opens the door to designing tailored ultrasound fields and responses.

title: Scentronic: An artificial intelligence–assisted olfactory interface for remote odor sharing and transmission
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Recent years have witnessed the surge of human–machine interfaces (HMIs) for various applications. Olfaction is a fundamental chemical sense crucial to perception, memory, and emotion. Current limitations arise from the difficulty of accurately capturing, transmitting, and reproducing odor signals, and the lack of standardized, network-enabled platforms. This work presents an internet of things (IoT)–enabled olfactory interface for remote odor sensing and stimulation. The system integrates an artificial intelligence-assisted odor sensing platform with a wearable piezoelectric olfactory actuation system. We demonstrate the design, characterization, and application of this framework, which integrates devices, circuit architecture, and software algorithms. Applications in medical contexts include psychophysical testing to study olfactory pathways and evaluate sensory loss. We further showcase multisensory stimulation through integrated olfactory and gustatory interfaces for enhanced immersion. This study establishes a scalable framework for IoT-based olfactory interaction, advancing HMIs toward a future that includes the long-overlooked chemical senses.

title: Voice patches in the marmoset auditory cortex revealed by multimodal optical imaging
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Species-specific vocalizations (including human voices) are important for the survival and social interactions of both humans and animals. In both humans and nonhuman primates, voice/vocalization–selective regions have been identified on the lateral temporal cortex. Here, we provide evidence of localized and hierarchically organized voice patches in the auditory cortex of the common marmoset, a highly vocal New World primate, using multimodal optical imaging techniques that directly measure activity from the smooth cortical surface in a noise-controlled environment. Both intrinsic imaging and calcium imaging data revealed two discrete voice patches in a region of the auditory cortex. Our results provided precise functional localization of the two voice patches (posterior and anterior) by anchoring their positions to the tonotopic map and core/noncore areas of the auditory cortex. Both patches preferentially respond to marmoset vocalizations, exhibit quantifiable neural selectivity beyond spectral features, and encode call type and caller identity. Distinct response properties reveal functional differentiation between the posterior and anterior voice patches, with latency differences consistent with a hierarchical relationship. These findings provide new evidence for an evolutionarily conserved cortical architecture in primates that supports vocal communication via voice patches, analogous to face processing systems in human and nonhuman primate brains.

title: Towards intense single-digit attosecond pulses with a 100-mJ-class mid-infrared sub-cycle laser
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The duration of isolated attosecond pulses created via high-order harmonic generation is determined by the number of optical cycles in the driving laser. Achieving shorter attosecond soft x-ray pulses requires minimizing the number of cycles while maintaining a high pulse energy. Here, we demonstrate a carrier-envelope-phase-stable, 100-mJ-class sub-cycle mid-infrared laser that produces a supercontinuum coherent soft-x-ray with unprecedented bandwidth. The system delivers 50-mJ, 6.7-fs (0.88-cycle) pulses at a center wavelength of 2.26 μm—over two orders of magnitude more energetic than any previous sub-cycle laser. We applied the system to high-order harmonic generation and compared the results to simulations based on the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation to identify unique features of sub-cycle lasers. This work represents a decisive step toward high-energy half-cycle lasers and high-energy single-digit attosecond soft x-ray pulses that can be used to probe matter and light-matter interactions at previously inaccessible temporal resolutions.

title: How high-pressure ices on large ocean worlds can support habitability: The compatibility of amino acids into ice VI and VII
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Water oceans in large icy moons and exoplanets are isolated from the rocky interior by thick layers of high-pressure ice, which hinder the direct release of nutrients and organics derived from water-rock interaction to the ocean. Possible uptake of these bio-essential compounds into high-pressure ice phases could regulate their availability in the ocean, but this process is poorly constrained. Here, we measured partition coefficients of glycine and alanine into ices VI and VII under elevated temperature-pressure conditions using a diamond-anvil cell. We observed moderate compatibility of glycine and alanine with partition coefficients:
                    K
                    
                      p
                      ,glycine
                    
                     = 0.14 and 0.40 in ices VI and VII, respectively;
                    K
                    
                      p
                      ,alanine
                    
                     = 0.21 and 0.35 in ices VI and VII, respectively. First-principles calculations suggested that amino acids could be incorporated into high-pressure ice’s lattice via cogrowth. Compatibility of amino acids into high-pressure ices would favor their transport in large extraterrestrial oceans, opening an avenue to habitability.

title: Coordinated mosquito biting dynamics at the human skin interface
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The bite of a female mosquito is the critical point of pathogen transmission, yet the fine-scale biting dynamics on human skin remain unknown. Here, we combine high-speed videography, deep-learning–based tracking, and electrophysiology to analyze biting dynamics of the malaria vector
                    Anopheles coluzzii
                    in real time at the human skin interface. We uncover a previously uncharacterized synchronization of mouthpart and leg movements during probing and identify five distinct below skin sub-behaviors: piercing, vessel searching, blood ingestion, retraction, and withdrawal. We show that disruption of the
                    orco
                    and
                    IR76b
                    chemosensory genes can alter some components of normal biting but these effects are subtle, suggesting possible plasticity in direct-contact chemosensation and mosquito bite execution. Comparative analyses show genus-specific biting strategies between
                    An. coluzzii
                    and
                    Aedes aegypti
                    linked to distinct ways they find blood vessels. Our findings indicate that female mosquitoes exhibit a complex synchronization of body parts at the bite site via motor and chemosensory processes.

title: Prioritizing reducing impacts on species to minimize residual reserves
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: International conservation goals have driven rapid expansion of protected areas. This growth has favored quantity over quality, and often results in residual reserves (i.e., areas where species already experience minimal anthropogenic impact). Spatial prioritization is commonly used to help design protected area networks that represent species while minimizing costs to stakeholders. This approach can result in the siting of protected areas that do not decrease impacts on species of conservation concern. Here, we show how measures of cumulative impacts on species can be used in a spatial prioritization to site protected areas to reduce impacts on species of conservation concern. We use a trait-based vulnerability framework and anthropogenic stressor maps to quantify cumulative impacts from four human activities, and incorporate those impacts into spatial prioritizations. We demonstrate that the inclusion of cumulative impacts on species in spatial prioritization can more efficiently protect biodiversity, balance socioeconomic objectives, and avoid residual reserve outcomes.

title: p75NTR orchestrates chondrogenesis and mechanoadaptation to preserve temporomandibular joint development and homeostasis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is essential for oral functions such as chewing, speaking, and swallowing. Temporomandibular disorders that impair these functions notably reduce patients’ quality of life, and few therapeutic strategies are available to ameliorate these conditions. Here, we identify the neurotrophin receptor (p75
                    NTR
                    ) as a central regulator of mandibular condylar cartilage development, mechanoadaptation, and homeostasis.
                    
                      p75
                      NTR
                    
                    loss causes condylar and disc hypoplasia, reduced chondrocyte number, impaired load-induced anabolism, and accelerated degeneration. Conditional deletion experiments demonstrate chondrocyte-autonomous requirements for the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)–p75
                    NTR
                    axis, which activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase AKT serine/threonine kinase and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling to promote proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation while restraining apoptosis. Degenerative human condyles exhibit reduced
                    
                      p75
                      NTR
                    
                    expression levels. Together, these data establish p75
                    NTR
                    as a molecular hub integrating neurotrophic and mechanical cues to preserve postnatal TMJ architecture and highlight the BDNF-p75
                    NTR
                    axis as a potential therapeutic target.

title: The mRNA-based RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 induces robust and durable CD4+ T cell responses against RSV in younger and older adults
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4
                    +
                    and CD8
                    +
                    T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4
                    +
                    responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4
                    +
                    response was strongly T helper 1 (T
                    H
                    1)–polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor–α and minimal T
                    H
                    2 cytokines. Both CD4
                    +
                    and CD8
                    +
                    T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F–specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.

title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer’s disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2–magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer–MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

title: Spatial decoupling of recognition and signaling in aptamer switches via tri-strand intermolecular competition
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Despite decades of progress in aptamer engineering, the development of a single, modular signaling architecture capable of transducing target recognition into a measurable output across structurally diverse analytes remains an unmet challenge in biosensing. We report the Competitor Bridge Aptamer (CoBrA) framework: a modular DNA tridomain architecture that functionally isolates target recognition from signal transduction. Unlike conventional sensors where signal output depends on unpredictable aptamer folding, the CoBrA system uses an aptamer switch to trigger a predictable, concerted spatial displacement between signaling end points. By leveraging computational simulations and energetic balancing, we systematically optimized the CoBrA framework to consolidate recognition, displacement, and ratiometric signaling within a single, minimal-component system. Using the dopamine and cortisol aptamers as models, we demonstrate strong thermodynamic and kinetic synchronization between the Cy3 and Cy5 channels across both targets for dopamine (Cy3:

Because the signaling event is a predictable, geometry-defined change rather than a fluorescence-specific phenomenon, this architecture is in principle adaptable to surface-based transduction modalities, including electrochemical, field-effect transistor, and plasmonic readouts.

title: Building digital pregnancies from the single cell up
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Single-cell digital twins connect in vitro drug screening studies with clinical outcomes, providing a new framework to evaluate therapies and advance precision medicine in pregnancy.

title: Wave vortices around oscillating subwavelength holes: Water-wave observation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: We consider a two-dimensional wave system containing a subwavelength hole, such as an aperture in an interface supporting surface electromagnetic or acoustic waves or an island in a fluid surface sustaining gravity-capillary waves. Recent studies have revealed the emergence of pronounced wave vortices around such structures, termed type II vortices, in contrast to conventional (type I) vortices associated with phase singularities and intensity nulls. A notable natural manifestation of type II vortices occurs in ocean tides around islands such as New Zealand, Madagascar, and Iceland, where the tidal phase increases by ±2π around the island. Although this phenomenon is usually associated with the Coriolis effect from the rotation of the Earth, here, we demonstrate the controlled generation of type II vortices using a minimal and tunable setup: a dipole-oscillating subwavelength hole and a single incident plane wave. Using laboratory gravity-capillary waves and an oscillating subwavelength “island,” we directly measure the resulting phase structure, topological charge, and wave angular momentum. We show that the emergence and handedness of the vortices can be precisely controlled via the relative phase between the dipolar source and the incident wave. Our results offer a simple and versatile mechanism for engineering subwavelength wave vortices, with potential applications in a variety of two-dimensional wave systems.

title: Climatic niche conservatism shapes the macroevolution, extinction, and survivorship of crocodile-line archosaurs
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Crocodylians are iconic thermophiles. Over 250 million years, crocodile-line archosaurs endured hyperthermals, climatic and range shifts, and two mass extinctions. Whether this niche conservatism reflects a deep evolutionary constraint or recent adaptation to novel climates remains unclear. We integrate present-day occurrences with a time-scaled phylogeny of >400 fossil and extant species. Niche models calibrated on living crocodylians were projected across 245 million years and compared with paleophylogeographic reconstructions. Macroevolutionary model fitting shows that temperature and precipitation exhibit strong phylogenetic structure, best described by bounded Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics, indicating long-term niche conservatism. Poleward expansions in warm intervals and contractions in cool phases reflect tracking of conserved optima rather than niche evolution. Unlike non-avian dinosaurs, low-latitude suitability persisted across all but the most extreme end-Cretaceous scenarios, with recovery expanding from tropical refugia. Thermal and precipitation regimes shifted near the Cenomanian/Turonian hyperthermal (∼93.9 Ma) and Eocene/Oligocene aridification transition (∼33.9 Ma), respectively. Climatic niche conservatism is therefore ancient in crocodile-line archosaurs, but not completely static.

title: Neurophysiological dynamics related to perception, action, and language in schizophrenia
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Schizophrenia disrupts both how people perceive the world and how they express and act on their thoughts, yet these symptoms are usually studied separately. Using magnetoencephalography during multisensory and motor tasks, we tested whether reduced event-related beta-band (15 to 30 hertz) modulation, a signal implicated in predictive control, provides a candidate neural marker across these domains. Compared to healthy individuals, patients showed diminished beta changes during sensory processing and movement completion, suggesting reduced flexibility in updating internal models. This neural pattern covaried with audiovisual simultaneity-judgment behavior, disorganized natural speech, and greater clinical severity. These findings suggest that distributed beta modulation may serve as a candidate cross-domain marker associated with perceptual, motor, and language disturbances in schizophrenia, motivating future studies that directly test predictive updating mechanisms.

title: Single-cell–level digital twins for preterm birth prevention strategies
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Digital twin models can accelerate therapeutic development by enabling low-risk testing of candidate interventions. In preterm labor (PTL), a major pregnancy complication where clinical trials face ethical and financial barriers, digital twins are especially valuable for evaluating new therapies targeting immune dysfunctions driving PTL. Yet, current models lack single-cell resolution, limiting detection of cell type–specific mechanisms, off-target effects, and the design of personalized interventions. We present Simulated Immunome Modeling of Clinical Outcomes (SIMCO), a single-cell–level digital twin framework that models immunomodulatory treatment effects on the timing of labor using immunome-wide, single-cell simulations. SIMCO’s digital twins are trained and validated on a newly generated mass cytometry atlas of the pregnant immunome exposed to nine candidate drugs preselected for PTL prevention. Applying SIMCO to an independent cohort of pregnant individuals, we simulate treatment effects on gestational length, screening for candidate drugs that delay labor timing and providing system-level mechanistic insight for each drug candidate. Tetrahydrofolate and the combination of aspirin and lansoprazole emerged as top candidates for PTL prevention, delaying labor onset primarily through enhanced mTOR signaling in innate immune cells and attenuated JAK/STAT signaling in naïve CD4
                    +
                    T cells.

title: In situ processing of fibrous hydrogels by photochemistry for adaptive cellular microenvironments
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Omnipresent in biology, fibrous networks like collagen possess unique properties: dynamic network via crosslinking and degradation. This intrinsic adaptivity plays a critical role in regulating cell behavior via cell-matrix interactions. Built from biological building blocks, however, these networks are challenging to manipulate or even control. Here, we introduce dynamic network regulation via photochemical control in a synthetic and fibrous highly biomimetic hydrogel. As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrate that the dynamic control over the mechanical properties of this adaptive in vitro model can be used to modulate cell spreading and mechanotransduction in three-dimensional (3D) mesenchymal stromal cell cultures. Our approach not only opens the door to on-demand mechanically adaptive gels with unprecedented control, but simultaneously offers easy processibility and cell extraction of the used synthetic gel.

title: Chemically encoded pH-tunable covalent adhesion by a bacterial thioester domain
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Thioester domains (TEDs) represent a family of bacterial adhesin domains that mediate covalent anchoring to target ligands via an intramolecular thioester bond. Although the broad distribution of TEDs among Gram-positive bacteria suggests a critical functional role, the biological significance of this covalent mechanism remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrated that TED-mediated covalent anchoring is reversible and that its equilibrium is regulated by pH. Specifically, SfbI-TED from group A
                    Streptococcus
                    binds tightly to fibrinogen at physiological pH, whereas mild acidification to pH 6.0 induces rapid dissociation of the complex. Thermodynamic analyses indicated that this pH responsiveness is largely dictated by the intrinsic pH sensitivity of the thioester-mediated acyl transfer reaction conserved within TEDs, rather than by surface residues specific to individual TEDs. Similar pH-dependent behavior was observed in phylogenetically distinct TEDs, suggesting that pH-responsive adhesion is likely to be a broadly shared feature of TED-containing adhesins across Gram-positive bacteria.

title: In-memory phononic learning toward cognitive mechanical intelligence
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Mechanical intelligence seeks autonomous materials that embody memory, perception, learning, and decision-making within the mechanical domain. A fundamental challenge is to integrate memory with information processing in an efficient, scalable, and interpretable way that supports cognitive learning and decision-making. Here, we introduce in-memory phononic learning, a framework that unifies non-volatile mechanical memory with wave-based perception in a phononic metastructure. Spatial information is stored as structural states that program elastic-wave responses, allowing probing waves to act as queries that retrieve informative features through parallel, physically transparent localization modes. Learning is achieved by offline optimization of input waveforms to selectively combine these features for multitask memory-pattern recognition without hardware redesign, with decisions inferred directly from output-energy responses. We experimentally and numerically demonstrate high-accuracy classification across tasks from geometric shapes to handwritten digits. Overall, this work elevates “materials that compute” toward “cognitive matter” that can interpret, reason, and learn through wave physics, laying a foundation for scalable and robust autonomous material systems.

title: Furan fatty acids reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism via acyl-CoA conjugates in obesity
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Dietary fish oil (FO) and omega-3 fatty acids are associated with cardiometabolic benefits, yet their molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Furan fatty acids (FuFAs), a distinct lipid class enriched in FO, have emerged as potential regulators of metabolic health. Here, we identify and quantify FuFA species in prescription omega-3 formulations and natural fish oils, and synthesize structurally engineered analogs designed to isolate antioxidant activity and β-oxidation susceptibility from FuFA bioactivity. In a diet-induced obesity mouse model, both natural and synthetic FuFAs reduced fat accumulation and inflammatory markers, while 11U3-2M additionally produced significant improvement in glucose tolerance, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis. The superior activity of 11U3-2M reflects the stable accumulation of its acyl-CoA conjugate that activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) signaling and allosterically inhibits acetyl-CoA carboxylases (ACCs) to reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism. These findings position FuFAs as functional dietary lipids contributing to fish oil’s metabolic effects and define fatty acid structural determinants that govern hepatic metabolic activity.

title: Accessing invasion-competent Plasmodium vivax merozoites reveals antibody-dependent NK cell activation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Malaria pathogenesis and clinical symptoms arise from blood-stage replication of
                    Plasmodium
                    parasites, which depends on rapid invasion of red blood cells by merozoites. Despite the central importance of this stage, direct functional studies of
                    Plasmodium vivax
                    (
                    P. vivax
                    ) merozoites remain limited by the lack of continuous in vitro culture and restricted access to viable, invasion-competent merozoites from clinical isolates. Consequently, key aspects of
                    P. vivax
                    merozoite biology and immune recognition remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a robust platform enabling synchronized release and high-yield isolation of invasion-competent
                    P. vivax
                    merozoites from ex vivo cultures. Reversible inhibition of parasite egress using the PKG inhibitor ML10 enables synchronization at the segmented schizont stage, followed by rapid mechanical release of merozoites using a liposome-based extrusion approach. This workflow yields highly pure merozoites with recovery rates exceeding 75% while preserving structural integrity and invasive capacity. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate that antibody-opsonized
                    P. vivax
                    merozoites activate human natural killer cells, revealing functional antibody-dependent immune responses.

title: Ocean carbon sequestration during glacial climates due to combined Antarctic sea ice expansion and ocean circulation change
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Glacial-interglacial transitions punctuate Earth’s Quaternary climate, accompanied by substantial atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon storage changes. The cause of atmospheric carbon drawdown during glaciations is uncertain, involving many mechanisms whose interactions are poorly understood. Here, we show that the combined expansion of Antarctic sea ice and associated changes in the meridional overturning efficiently sequester carbon in the ocean abyss, leading to a decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide. In contrast, changes in sea ice and circulation individually result in ocean carbon dioxide outgassing. When sea ice expansion and circulation changes act together, they enhance biological carbon storage by reducing ocean-atmosphere fluxes in the Southern Ocean, without invoking external drivers of the biological pump. This reduction inhibits the outgassing of upwelled remineralized carbon and promotes its resubduction into the abyss. Together, these results reveal a reinforcing feedback linking atmospheric cooling, Antarctic sea ice expansion, and ocean circulation changes to enhanced biological carbon storage and atmospheric carbon dioxide drawdown.

title: A phosphorylation-gated GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 module controls drought-responsive transcription
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Drought adaptation requires rapid spatial reorganization of signaling proteins to reprogram stress-responsive transcription, yet how phosphorylation coordinates this process remains unclear. Here we aimed to define how phosphorylation-gated protein relocalization regulates a BpLBD1-centered drought pathway in
                    Betula platyphylla
                    (birch). Drought activated two kinase branches: BpAGC phosphorylated BpMAPK6 at Ser318 within a cryptic nuclear localization signal, promoting importin α recognition, whereas BpCKII phosphorylated BpGAPDH at Thr109, Thr270, Ser279 and Thr298, promoting importin β recognition. Dual phosphorylation enabled coordinated nuclear accumulation of BpMAPK6 and BpGAPDH. In the nucleus, phosphorylated BpGAPDH acted as a scaffold-like adaptor coupling BpMAPK6 to BpLBD1, enabling BpMAPK6-mediated phosphorylation of BpLBD1 at Ser29. This weakened BpLBD1 binding to the
                    BpMYB123
                    promoter, reduced expression of the drought-sensitivity regulator
                    BpMYB123
                    , and de-repressed drought-responsive genes such as
                    BpRD29B
                    . Disrupting
                    BpGAPDH
                    or BpLBD1 Ser29 phosphorylation compromised drought tolerance. Thus, a phospho-spatial GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 switch couples nuclear protein assembly to drought-responsive transcription.

source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents

title: Interpreting the Hall effect of highly doped conducting polymers
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:

Here, we resolve this problem using a quasi–one-dimensional (Q1D) tight-binding model of the band structure of uniaxially aligned polymer films to analyze the p-type to n-type transition in the Hall effect observed upon increased doping.
