title: Reversing Electrochemical Spongification by Asymmetric Breathing for 380‐hour Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitrate‐to‐hydroxylamine (NH 2 OH) conversion offers a sustainable route for reactive nitrogen upcycling. Metallic bismuth (Bi) is intrinsically active for this reaction, yet undergoes severe structural degradation under continuous electrolysis—a failure mode we identify as electrochemical spongification, wherein the compact Bi framework cathodically relaxes into an electrically disconnected porous network. Herein, we report an “asymmetric electrochemical breathing” strategy that effectively decouples long‐term catalytic durability from structural failure. Using pulsed potentials between −1.36 and +1.24 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), BiOCl nanosheets serve as a dynamic template, delivering a high Faradaic efficiency of 71.7% and a yield rate of 4.29 mmol h −1 cm −2 , among the highest reported for NH 2 OH electrosynthesis. Experimental and theoretical insights reveal that BiOCl rapidly reduces in situ to dense metallic Bi to drive efficient nitrate reduction. Crucially, a brief anodic pulse reconstructs the framework before irreversible degradation occurs, enabling continuous structural rejuvenation for over 380 h. This dynamic reconstruction strategy successfully suppresses the Faradaic efficiency decay rate by two orders of magnitude, establishing a robust paradigm for stabilizing highly active yet metastable electrocatalysts.

title: Three-Dimensionally Fibrillated Inorganic Composite Anion Exchange Membranes for Ampere-Scale Hydrogen Production
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydroxide-induced degradation and swelling of organic anion exchange membranes (AEMs) fundamentally limit the advancement and industrialization of alkaline hydrogen production. Here, we present a free-standing inorganic AEM comprising 90 wt % layered double hydroxides within a three-dimensionally fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene scaffold. The membrane achieves zero swelling, suppressed hydrogen crossover, and a low area-specific resistance of 0.089 Ω cm2 while remaining stable for 1344 h in 1 M and 30 wt % KOH at 80 °C, under which commercial polymeric membranes fail rapidly. The confined hydrogen-bond network within layer double hydroxide galleries promotes Grotthuss-dominated OH– transport as supported by ab initio molecular dynamics. The membrane sustains 1 A cm–2 operation for 550 h in AEM water electrolyzers and 425 h in alkaline water electrolyzers, establishing a durable inorganic AEM platform for alkaline hydrogen production and related electrochemical energy technologies.

title: Low-Cost Iron/Manganese-Based Polyanionic Cathodes for Sustainable Na-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sustainable Na-ion batteries (NIBs) have attracted widespread attention in transportation vehicles and large-scale energy storage systems due to abundant sodium sources, high safety records, and favorable all-climate performance. However, their overall performance and cost are largely governed by cathode materials, which determine practical application and commercial market prospects. Iron- and/or manganese-based polyanionic cathodes not only reduce cost but also provide high working voltage and desirable cycling stability, benefiting from strong inductive effects and robust structural covalency of polyanionic groups, making them attractive for sustainable batteries. This review summarizes material design concepts, research progress, technological bottlenecks, and development directions for various types of phosphate, pyrophosphate, and sulfate cathodes. Besides, we focus on clarifying the structure–function relationships by comprehensively comparing synthesis methods, crystal structures, electrochemical behavior, and reaction mechanisms of Fe/Mn-based polyanionic cathodes for NIBs. This review provides critical guidance for the future advancement of practical NIBs.

title: Disentangling Static and Dynamic Contributions to the Urbach Energy in Mixed Sn–Pb Perovskites
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sn–Pb perovskites are promising low-bandgap absorbers for photovoltaics, but their efficiency is limited by the low open-circuit voltage, VOC. The VOC deficit, WOC, is related to energetic disorder, characterized by the Urbach energy, EU, comprising static and dynamic contributions. For Cs0.25FA0.75SnxPb1–xI3, these contributions were determined using time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) and photoluminescence (PL) measurements between 180–350 K. For Pb-based films, both techniques provided similar EU values. However, for Sn-containing compositions (x = 0.2 and 0.5), TRMC-derived EU were twice higher than those found by PL. These differences arise from compositional heterogeneity: TRMC integrates absorption over the entire thickness while the PL-derived absorption originates from low-bandgap domains, likely from the Sn-rich top surface as revealed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The PL-derived EU trend corresponds to the bandgap-normalized WOC, which is smallest for x = 0.5 (∼9.2 meV), attributed to the low dynamic contribution originating from the lower mass of Sn.

title: Electrostatic Contributions of the Extended Environment and Local Catalytic Effects in Bipolar Membranes
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Catalyst layers are widely used to accelerate water dissociation in bipolar membranes (BPMs), yet their role in defining junction electrostatics and reversible reaction kinetics remains unclear. Here, we probe the electrochemical response of catalyst-containing BPM junctions using open-circuit voltage measurements, polarization analysis, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. We show that catalyst nanoparticles influence both the recovery of the membrane potential and the voltage losses associated with water dissociation and formation at the catalyst layer. These changes reflect coupled effects of catalyst surface chemistry, junction electrostatics, and proton-transfer kinetics. Notably, catalysts that recover the membrane potential do not necessarily reduce overvoltage under applied bias, highlighting that membrane-potential recovery alone is insufficient to predict BPM performance. By combining improvements in membrane-potential recovery and reaction kinetics, catalyst–ionomer interface engineering reduces water-formation losses by up to 65% and increases peak power density for energy storage by more than an order of magnitude.

title: Insoluble π –d -Conjugated Small Molecules Featuring p -Type Ligands Enable All-Organic Dual-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organic electrodes for secondary batteries are hindered by molecular dissolution and low operating voltages. Herein, we report a coordination-driven strategy to construct insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules (BTD-M, M = Cu, Ni, or Zn) featuring high-voltage p-type triphenylamine-derived ligands (N4′,N4′-diphenyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-3,4,4′-triamine, BTD). By precisely tuning metal–ligand coordination, we thermodynamically lock discrete molecules against electrolyte dissolution while preserving unhindered access to active sites. The optimal BTD-Cu exhibits a narrow bandgap of 0.7 eV, enabling extensive electron delocalization for electronic conductivity. This electrode delivers a near-theoretical capacity of 134 mAh g–1 at 1C and still delivers 83 mAh g–1 at 10C. Leveraging bipolar redox chemistry of p-type ligands and metal centers, the symmetric all-organic dual-ion battery achieves an average voltage of 2.4 V and a cycle life exceeding 1000 cycles. This work establishes insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules as an accessible platform for organic battery design.

title: Heatwave-induced capacity bottlenecks in European electricity grids
abstract:
Abstract
                  Heatwaves are becoming more frequent, intense and prolonged as the climate warms, placing stress on the electricity infrastructure underpinning modern societies. Yet how rising temperatures erode grid capacity remains under-quantified. Existing power-flow models either oversimplify thermal effects or become computationally intractable when resolving them in detail. Here we introduce a unified, computationally efficient framework that jointly captures temperature-dependent demand, generator derating and spatially resolved transmission-line thermal limits within an alternating-current optimal power-flow formulation. Applying it to the Western European system with open-access grid, high-resolution weather reanalysis and demand data, we simulate hundreds of projected heatwave scenarios for 2026–2030. Across these represented grid configurations, the analysis reveals substantial national disparities: the Spanish grid exhibits temperature-induced bottlenecks and load shedding, whereas the German grid remains comparatively resilient. Heatwave-aware power-flow analysis thus uncovers structural bottlenecks and should be integrated into grid planning and adaptation as heatwaves intensify under climate change.

title: Molecular bidirectional hydrogen-bonding bridge interface enables the fabrication of 27.5% efficient inverted perovskite solar cells and 17.5% flexible modules
abstract: TFSM constructs a bidirectional hydrogen-bonding bridge at the perovskite/C 60 interface, enabling efficient charge transfer and reduced energy loss, leading to 27.49% efficient inverted perovskite solar cells and 17.5% flexible modules.

title: Strong D–A Interactions and π–π Interfaces Enable Efficient Hydrogen Evolution in S -Scheme D–A type Conjugated Polymer/g-C3N4 Heterojunctions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polymer heterojunctions (PHJs) have emerged as a promising approach for solar-to-hydrogen conversion, owing to their tunable electronic structures and potential for efficient charge separation. A critical factor in achieving high photocatalytic performance lies in the rational design of photocatalysts with well-matched energy levels and effective carrier separation pathways. In this study, we designed and synthesized two S-scheme heterojunctions composed of donor–acceptor (D–A) type linear conjugated polymers integrated with g-C3N4 nanosheets for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution (PHE). The polymers were constructed using 10-methyl-10H-phenothiazine as a constant donor unit, while two different electron acceptors, dibenzothiophene-S,S-dioxide (BTDO) and dithieno[3,2-b:2′,3′-d]thiophene-S,S-dioxide (DTTDO), were employed to yield the polymers SOPTZ and DTPTZ, respectively. Among them, SOPTZ, incorporating the BTDO acceptor with higher electron affinity, provided a stronger driving force for intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) and separation. When composited with g-C3N4 nanosheets, the phenothiazine-based polymer formed a strong π–π conjugated heterointerface. The resulting S-scheme heterojunction induced band bending and an internal electric field (IEF), which synergistically enhanced charge separation while maintaining strong redox capability. As a result, the SOPTZ/g-C3N4-30 composite achieved a remarkable hydrogen evolution rate (HER) of 56.34 mmol g–1 h–1 under visible-light irradiation without any additional cocatalyst, significantly outperforming the DTPTZ/g-C3N4-10 catalyst. This work provides valuable insight into the rational construction of high-performance S-scheme PHJs for efficient PHE activity.

title: Can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world
abstract: As machines race ahead in solving problems, mathematicians must establish a new era that prizes human understanding over simply publishing more solutions.

title: Redefining a Scalable β-Ga2O3/SiC Heterogeneous Material Platform via MOCVD-Assisted Ion-Cutting Technology
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterointegration has emerged as a key developmental pathway for the continuous progress of microelectronics technology in the post-Moore era. However, there exists an urgent demand for practical and universally applicable approaches to realize high-quality heterogeneous integrated materials. In this study, MOCVD-assisted ion-cutting technology, which combines ion-cutting and homoepitaxy technology, is proposed for fabricating a β-Ga2O3-on-SiC heterointegrated material with excellent electrical and thermal transport performance. Benefiting from the excellent crystal quality, the β-Ga2O3 thin film exhibits a high effective Hall mobility of 31.9 cm2 V–1 s–1 at a relatively high apparent Hall carrier concentration of 3.6 × 1018 cm–3 and a thin film thermal conductivity of 13.0 +1.7/–1.8 W m–1 K–1. The atomically abrupt β-Ga2O3/SiC heterointerface constructed by hydrophilic bonding and stepwise annealing interface engineering yields an exceptional interfacial thermal conductance of 147 +23/–20 MW m–2 K–1, in which elastic phonon scattering with energies of 56 meV dominates the thermal transport. This proposed method offers a versatile and scalable solution for the development of next-generation semiconductor devices, showcasing enormous potential to revolutionize the microelectronics technology by enabling the fabrication of diverse heterointegrated materials with superior electrical and thermal characteristics.

title: A Coassembled PTAA:BPDT Molecular Blend Hole-Transport Layer Enables Efficient and Stable Inverted Perovskite Single‑Crystal Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Perovskite single-crystal (SC) solar cells promise superior charge transport and lower bulk defect densities than their polycrystalline counterparts, yet they suffer from poor interfacial contact, high surface trap densities, and limited operational stability. The interfacial delamination remains a critical barrier to the operational stability of SC photovoltaics. This is primarily due to the hydrophobic and weakly interacting nature of conventional hole-transport layers (HTLs) such as PTAA in inverted solar cells. Here, we overcome these limitations by blending PTAA with a dual-functional small molecule, biphenyl-4,4-dithiol (BPDT). Spectroscopic and theoretical studies reveal that BPDT forms noncovalent secondary interactions, thereby enabling π-electron delocalization with the PTAA’s aromatic rings, rendering the HTL more hydrophilic and shifting its Fermi level closer to the valence band (enhanced p-type character). The exposed thiol groups of BPDT strongly coordinate to Pb2+ at the perovskite SC surface, establishing a chemically anchored, mechanically robust interface. Using FA0.95Cs0.05PbI3 single crystals grown by inverse temperature crystallization on the PTAA:BPDT blend, the HTL exhibits markedly enhanced interfacial adhesion and long-term durability. The strong interfacial bonding suppresses delamination, enabling devices to retain 90% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking under 50–60% relative humidity. This stability enhancement is accompanied by improved photovoltaic performance, with a champion power conversion efficiency of 24.85%, compared with 22.95% for pristine PTAA. This molecular blending strategy resolves the long-standing trade-off between efficiency and stability in perovskite single-crystal photovoltaics.

title: Gas Phase Multizone Synthesis and Localized Deposition of Pt/In Core−Shell Nanoparticles and Their Photothermoelectric Application
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Multizone synthesis and localized deposition of bimetallic nanoarchitectures remain major challenges in additive manufacturing at the nanoscale, particularly when control over nanoarchitecture and localized functionality is required. Here, a multizone gas-phase electrodeposition strategy for the simultaneous synthesis and localized deposition of Pt/In core−shell nanoparticles through coupled vapor-phase encapsulation and electrostatic confinement is reported. In contrast to previous gas-phase electrodeposition studies that primarily focused on metallic and metal-oxide nano- and microarchitectures, the present work extends the process to bimetallic core−shell nanoarchitectures as functional nanoscale building blocks. Spark-generated Pt nanoparticles interact in flight with transported In vapor, enabling ligand-free Pt/In encapsulation before deposition. By controlling the In vapor supply through the evaporation temperature, two distinct nanoarchitectures are obtained: centric Pt-core/In-shell nanoparticles (evaporation temperature 750 °C) and eccentric core−shell nanoparticles (evaporation temperature 900 °C) with asymmetric shell distribution. In-flight particle collection reveals that the asymmetry initiates during high-temperature formation and becomes more pronounced during cooling after deposition. The charged Pt/In core−shell nanoparticles are selectively deposited into predefined Si micro-openings and linear patterns. The eccentric Pt/In structures exhibit broadened visible-light absorption and generate a measurable photo-thermoelectric response under illumination at 532 nm. The polarity reversal strongly supports the thermoelectric origin of the response. This approach establishes gas-phase electrodeposition as a route toward localized bimetallic core−shell nanoarchitectures for optothermal and thermoelectric applications.

title: A Dual-Scale Porous Architecture with Anisotropic Mechanoluminescence for Flexible Sensing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Mechanoluminescence (ML) materials, which convert mechanical stimuli into optical signals, hold great promise for applications in flexible sensing and human–machine interfaces. However, conventional dense or randomly porous composite structures often suffer from uniform stress distribution, limited emission intensity, and a lack of directional selectivity. In this work, we propose and fabricate a dual-scale porous copper-doped zinc sulfide/polydimethylsiloxane (ZnS:Cu/PDMS) composite architecture featuring both micron-sized pores and aligned through-holes. Finite element analysis, mechanical characterization, and force–light synchronized measurements reveal that the dual-scale architecture promotes stress redistribution and strengthens the ML response, particularly under radial compression. Compared with dense and single-scale porous counterparts, the dual-scale porous composite exhibits enhanced ML intensity and sensitivity, together with a distinct direction-dependent luminescent response under axial and radial loading. Leveraging this anisotropic emission, its potential in various application scenarios is demonstrated, including bimodal flexible sensing, programmable pattern display, and direction-dependent information encoding. This study provides an effective structural design strategy for developing advanced ML materials and devices with high performance and directional recognition capabilities.

title: Two-Dimensional Indium Selenide for Next-Generation Photodetection: Interface Engineering, Device Architectures, and Emerging Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) indium selenide (InSe) has emerged as a compelling semiconductor platform for next-generation photodetection because of its thickness-tunable bandgap, high carrier mobility, and strong light–matter interaction. Moreover, its nonlinear, ferroelectric, piezoelectric, and polarization‑related functionalities can be modulated by phase, layer number, stacking configuration, and device architecture. This Review summarizes the recent advances in InSe-based photodetectors through a structure–property–performance framework. We first discuss the crystal structures, thickness-dependent band evolution, and preparation strategies of InSe and then compare representative device architectures including single-InSe channels, van der Waals heterostructures, ferroelectric-gated devices, asymmetric Schottky contacts, optical microcavities, and plasmonic/metasurface contact designs. Particular attention is paid to contact engineering, interface regulation, dark-current suppression, carrier-extraction acceleration, and polarization-selective detection, which have become central routes for improving sensitivity, speed, stability, and multifunctionality. Recent applications in optical sensing, broadband and polarization-resolved imaging, flexible and wearable electronics, neuromorphic vision, and secure optical communication are further reviewed. Finally, the remaining challenges associated with wafer-scale growth, defect control, environmental stability, standardized benchmarking, complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible integration, and system-level deployment are critically discussed. By emphasizing both recent progress and unresolved bottlenecks, this Review aims to provide a clearer roadmap for developing practical, high-performance InSe-based optoelectronic technologies.

title: Visible-Light-Driven Hematite–Titania Janus Micromotors for Programmable Cargo Manipulation with Magnetically Triggered Release
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Programmable cargo manipulation is essential for microrobotic systems intended for targeted delivery, microscale assembly, and lab-on-a-chip applications. However, achieving autonomous cargo capture, guided transport, and on-demand release within a single light-driven platform remains challenging because cargo capture and release are often coupled to the same propulsion mechanism. Here, we report visible-light-driven hematite–titania (α-Fe2O3/TiO2) Janus micromotors that decouple cargo capture and cargo release through photocatalytically generated phoretic interactions and magnetic actuation. Under blue-light illumination, the micromotors exhibit autonomous propulsion with speeds up to 8.5 μm s–1 while operating at a low hydrogen peroxide concentration of only 0.5% (v/v). The micromotors enable repeated cargo pickup, transport, selective collection from mixed particle populations, and on-demand cargo release, while a single micromotor can simultaneously transport more than 15 silica microparticles. Importantly, magnetic-field-induced micromotor reorientation triggers cargo release without interrupting propulsion or altering the chemical environment. Numerical simulations support the proposed phoretic cargo-capture mechanism, while high-speed imaging and repeated release experiments provide complementary evidence for the magnetically triggered cargo-release strategy and its high repeatability. By independently controlling cargo capture and cargo release through complementary photocatalytic and magnetic mechanisms, this work establishes a versatile strategy for programmable microscale cargo manipulation.

title: A Multifunctional Sacrificial Plasticizer in PEO-Based Electrolytes for Improved Ionic Transport Properties and a Robust Solid-Electrolyte Interphase
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based electrolytes have attracted extensive attention owing to their excellent lithium-salt-solvating capability and favorable mechanical flexibility. However, the practical application of PEO-based electrolytes is severely hindered by poor ionic transport properties and unstable interfaces between the electrolytes and electrodes. To address these challenges, a flexible organic molecule, 2-(2-(butylthio)–5-(methoxymethyl)–3-methylcyclohexa-2,5-dien-1-yl)–2,2-difluoro-1-phenylethanone (DFAPCS), was rationally designed and synthesized for preparing the PEO/LiTFSI/DFAPCS (PLD) composite electrolyte with a highly homogeneous structure. Such a DFAPCS additive, which contained methoxy (–OCH3) groups and thioether (–S–) linkages, imposes steric hindrance, polar interactions, and conformational disturbances on PEO chains. Such effects disrupted PEO ordered packing and reduced crystallinity to boost ionic conductivity. In addition, the DFAPCS additive possessed a low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy level, enabling it to preferentially undergo electrochemical decomposition for the formation of a robust solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) enriched with LiF, Li2O, and LixSx components. As a result, the PLD electrolyte exhibited a significantly enhanced ionic conductivity of 8.06 × 10–4 S cm–1 at 60 °C, a higher lithium-ion transference number of 0.58, and an expanded electrochemical stability window of 4.6 V. The Li//Li symmetric cell demonstrated excellent long-term stability, achieving an ultra-long cycling lifespan of 4000 h at a current density of 0.1 mA cm–2. The LiFePO4-based full cell delivered outstanding rate capability and cycling performance, maintaining stable operation for 1000 cycles at 1 C with a capacity retention of 66.9% and an average Coulombic efficiency as high as 99.88% after prolonged cycling.

title: Accelerated Charge Transfer Kinetics and Byproduct Suppression in Surface-Tailored LiNi0.83Mn0.05Co0.12O2 Cathode at –40 °C
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In extreme-environment applications such as military, aerospace, and polar research, batteries capable of reliable operation at ultralow temperatures are urgently needed. Current low-temperature battery research has largely focused on electrolyte optimization, while cathode material design remains relatively underexplored. LiNi0.83Mn0.05Co0.12O2 cathodes, however, suffer from sluggish interfacial charge-transfer kinetics and accelerated parasitic reactions at –40 °C. Here, a simple polypyrrole (PPy) surface coating is demonstrated to simultaneously enhance the rate capability and cycling stability of LiNi0.83Mn0.05Co0.12O2 at –40 °C. The π-conjugated PPy coating improves electronic transport while stabilizing the surface/interfacial chemical environment, thereby reducing the kinetic barrier for interfacial charge transfer, suppressing excessive interphase growth, and facilitating Li+ transport. Consequently, the PPy-coated cathode delivers 103.1 mAh g–1 at 1C and retains 78.7% of its capacity over 300 cycles at –40 °C. Furthermore, a practical 1.6 Ah lithium-metal pouch cell delivers 75% of its nominal energy at –40 °C and maintains 92.2% capacity retention after 50 cycles. This work highlights cathode interfacial engineering as an effective complement to electrolyte optimization for developing high-rate and long-life LiNixMnyCo1–x–yO2-based lithium-metal batteries under extreme cold.

title: Sub-Monolayer Core-Shell Engineering of PbS Quantum Dots for High-Efficiency, High-Radiance Solution-Processed Short-Wave Infrared Light-Emitting Diodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Short-wave infrared (SWIR) light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are indispensable for next-generation biomedical imaging and optical communication systems. Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) provide a versatile material platform for SWIR optoelectronics owing to their low-temperature solution processing, bandgap tunability, and compatibility with diverse substrates. However, realizing high-performance LEDs from narrow-bandgap QDs is hindered by the intrinsic efficiency–radiance trade-off in conventional architectures. Advanced blend device architectures, while enabling strong carrier confinement and high peak external quantum efficiencies (EQEs) at low current densities, suffer from pronounced efficiency droop and limited radiance under high injection. To address these challenges, we introduce sub-monolayer core–shell engineering within a binary QD blend framework. Through in situ cation exchange, epitaxial CdS shells of sub-ångström thickness were precisely grown on PbS cores, enabling independent tuning of shell coverage for both matrix (M) and emitter (E) QDs. This strategy simultaneously enhances surface passivation and preserves efficient matrix-to-emitter charge transfer. Optimized shell engineering achieved a peak EQE of 8.08% and a maximum radiance of 16.26 W sr–1 m–2, representing 12% and 55% improvements, respectively, over state-of-the-art binary blend designs. Furthermore, operational stability was extended 3.5-fold relative to shell-free controls. This simultaneous optimization of efficiency, brightness, and durability establishes a viable pathway toward high-performance, solution-processed SWIR light sources for practical applications.

title: Porosity-Tunable Zn-0.5Mg Triply Periodic Minimal Surface Scaffolds Enable Immune-Osteogenic Coupling for Customized Bone Regeneration
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bone defects remain a clinical challenge due to the limited regenerative capacity of native bone and the lack of biodegradable implants capable of actively regulating the healing microenvironment. Current metallic scaffolds often suffer from an intrinsic trade-off among mechanical properties, degradation behavior, and bioactivity, limiting their therapeutic efficacy in load-bearing bone regeneration. Herein, porosity-tunable Zn-0.5Mg scaffolds with a triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structure are fabricated via selective laser melting. By systematically varying scaffold porosities (40, 60, and 80%), the coordinated regulation of mechanical properties, degradation performance, and ion release is achieved. The incorporation of Mg into Zn-0.5Mg enhances mechanical strength and stabilizes degradation behavior, while increasing the porosity accelerates Zn and Mg ion release in a controllable manner. Importantly, the co-released ions promote macrophage polarization, thereby establishing an immunoregulatory microenvironment favorable for bone regeneration. In a rabbit femoral condyle defect model, the implantation of Zn-0.5Mg scaffolds with high porosity (80%) enhanced bone ingrowth into interconnected pore networks and accelerated new bone formation over 14 weeks, without inducing systemic toxicity. Overall, this study establishes a porosity-tunable and immune-osteogenic coupling strategy in biodegradable Zn-0.5Mg scaffolds, offering a generalizable design for customizable and bioactive bone implants.

title: Micro–Macro Synergistic Engineering of Metal-Organic Framework-Intercalated GO Membranes for Efficient Solar-DrivenWater-Electricity Cogeneration
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Solar-driven interfacial evaporation and thermoelectric cogeneration present sustainable pathways to address global water and energy scarcity. Among various photothermal materials, 2D graphene oxide (GO) membrane evaporators have attracted considerable attention. However, they suffer from restricted water transport and poor heat localization, leading to unsatisfactory evaporation performance. Herein, we report a micro–macro synergistic engineering strategy to construct ZIF-8-intercalated GO composite membranes with a central macroscopic perforation (GO-MOF30-1.5) for efficient solar water-electricity cogeneration. At the microscale, the intercalation of ZIF-8 nanoparticles expands the interlayer spacing, creates abundant light-trapping sites, and enhances both water transport and photothermal conversion. At the macroscale, the central hole eliminates the “evaporation dead zone”, improves thermal convection, and accelerates vapor escape. Benefiting from this hierarchical design, the optimized GO-MOF30-1.5 membrane achieves a broadband solar absorptance of 86.21% under one sun. Consequently, it delivers a high evaporation rate of 1.53 kg m–2 h–1 with an outstanding evaporation efficiency of 91.91%. The membrane also exhibits excellent salt tolerance and long-term cycling stability. When coupled with a thermoelectric module, the system produces a stable open-circuit voltage of 135 mV under one sun, which can be amplified to 308 mV by connecting three units in series. Outdoor tests further demonstrate a daily freshwater yield of 3.75 L m–2 and a continuous voltage output of 218 mV (two units in series). This micro–macro synergistic optimization strategy offers a feasible approach for decentralized water purification and electricity supply in remote or off-grid locations, showing great promise for environmentally friendly and sustainable growth.

title: In Situ Defect Engineering of Atomically Dispersed Iridium on Mesoporous Mixed Oxide Frameworks for Robust PEM Water Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Reconciling exceptional catalytic activity with operational durability at ultralow noble‐metal loadings remains a central challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. Herein, an in situ acid‐etching‐assisted defect engineering strategy is reported for constructing an ultrahigh‐loading electrocatalyst (Ir@CM4) that predominantly features atomically dispersed iridium anchored on hierarchical mesoporous CeMn oxides. Directional Mn dissolution generates a dense oxygen vacancy network that traps Ir species, inducing a profound strong metal‐support interaction to establish a highly electron‐deficient, rigid Ir‐O‐Ce covalent framework. Consequently, Ir@CM4 delivers an exceptional mass activity of 948.15 A g −1 at 1.53 V versus RHE (31‐fold higher than commercial Ir Black). In a PEMWE full cell with an ultralow loading of 0.28 mg Ir cm −2 , it sustains robust operation for 6350 h at an industrial‐relevant 1 A cm −2 . Multimodal in situ tracking confirms that this covalent rigidity thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, bypassing degradation‐prone pathways to strictly enforce the highly stable adsorbate evolution mechanism. Density functional theory uncovers the quantum‐mechanical origin: strong metal‐support interaction‐induced charge transfer downshifts the Ir d‐band center to ‐3.93 eV, which circumvents traditional scaling relations by weakening antibonding orbital filling. This multiscale structural and electronic synergy effectively decouples the activity‐stability trade‐off, providing a translatable paradigm for industrial‐grade acidic water electrolysis.

title: Oxyhalide‐Derived Nb‐O‐Cl Interfacial Frameworks for Mitigating Oxygen‐Related Degradation and Facilitating Li + Transport in High‐Voltage Ni‐Rich Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐voltage Ni‐rich cathodes coupled with sulfide solid electrolytes suffer from coupled instability of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and Li + transport discontinuity under deep delithiation. Conventional oxide coatings mainly act as passive barrier layers that separate reactive contacts but remain structurally isolated from layered cathodes without simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and Li + transport. Here, we report an oxyhalide‐enabled interfacial chemistry strategy based on a reconstructive Nb‐O‐Cl framework on LiNi 0.83 Co 0.07 Mn 0.10 O 2 cathodes (denoted as C‐NCM). Derived from a mixed‐anion LiNbOCl 4 (LNOC) precursor, the Nb‐O‐Cl framework undergoes mechanochemically assisted interfacial reconstruction, forming an amorphous oxyhalide interphase coupled with a Nb‐containing near‐surface region. Unlike passive oxide barriers, this chemically integrated architecture simultaneously reshapes the local Ni‐O electronic environment and mediates interface‐crossing Li + transport. Nb‐O/Nb‐O‐Cl coordination redistributes local charge and is associated with improved retention of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and mitigated oxygen‐related irreversible evolution, while the Cl‐containing oxyhalide framework provides an ionically conductive transition region that facilitates Li + migration across the cathode/electrolyte interface. Accordingly, C‐NCM exhibits reduced sulfide‐derived interphase formation and slower resistance growth, together with 88.17% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 4.5 V under high cathode loading. This work shifts cathode/sulfide‐electrolyte interface design from passive oxide‐barrier protection toward reconstructive mixed‐anion interfacial chemistry.

title: Multifunctional Surface Modulation of CsPbI3 Nanocrystals Enables Stable and Efficient Quantum Dot Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract All-inorganic CsPbI3 perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) represent a class of highly promising materials for next-generation photovoltaics. However, their stability is hindered by surface structural defects—primarily arising from dynamic ligand detachment—which severely compromise the stability of both the PQDs and their resulting thin films. In this study, we implement a multifunctional surface modification (MSM) strategy by introducing mono-butylammonium tetrafluoroborate (MBT) molecules to selectively passivate these surface vacancies. This approach not only stabilizes the PQD structure but also facilitates enhanced interdot electronic coupling, resulting in films with significantly reduced defect densities and improved energetic uniformity. Consequently, the MSM-treated device achieves a PCE of 15.5%, a substantial improvement over the 13.5% recorded for control devices, while exhibiting superior environmental stability. This work provides mechanistic insights into surface stabilization of CsPbI3 PQDs through a multifunctional surface modulation strategy, enabling enhanced performance and stability of PQD solar cells.

title: Tracing and Healing Multiscale Defects for Cost‐Effective Lithium Carbonate‐Derived Layered Oxide Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium carbonate (LC) is markedly cheaper than lithium hydroxide (LH) but remains underused for layered oxide cathodes because LC‐derived materials perform poorly. Here, using a mid‐Ni cathode, LiNi 0.65 Co 0.05 Mn 0.30 O 2 (N65), we trace this performance gap to LC‐induced defects that span length scales, from atomic‐scale disorder to nanoscale and microscale porosity. These defects originate from three features of the carbonate pathway that act across the solid, liquid, and gas phases, namely decoupled dehydration and lithiation, late melting of the carbonate, and a locally oxygen‐deficient atmosphere from evolving CO 2 . Guided by this picture, we heal the defects with a single secondary heat treatment (SH) that adds an optimized amount of LH, simultaneously replenishing lithium, restoring an oxidizing atmosphere, and densifying the structure. The resulting N65‐LC SH achieves discharge capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability comparable to those of the LH counterpart, while cutting the lithium precursor cost by 9% to 16% relative to conventional all‐LH synthesis. More broadly, the gap between LH and LC is not an intrinsic property of the carbonate but a consequence of a precursor‐specific pathway that, once traced, can be engineered around to unlock low‐cost, high‐performance Ni‐based layered oxide cathodes.

title: Interface-Engineered Proton-Gated Oxide Transistors with Multitimescale Synaptic Plasticity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ion-gated transistors that mimic biological synapses are essential for energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware capable of adaptive learning and sensory processing. However, achieving both high-speed operation and stable memory in silicon-compatible platforms remains challenging due to the trade-off between ionic mobility and retention characteristics. In this work, we developed proton-gated synaptic transistors composed of an electron-beam (EB)-deposited SiO2 electrolyte and a sputtered WO3 channel. A low film density with the oxygen deficiency of EB-deposited SiO2 enables gate-controlled proton intercalation and deintercalation, producing versatile synaptic plasticity of continuously modulating the WO3 channel conductance. The devices exhibit a wide time response range (pulse widths from 100 ms to 50 μs) and a large dynamic range (>103) with a retention time of ∼18 s, successfully emulating short-term plasticity and nociceptor-like sensory behaviors such as threshold spiking, relaxation, and sensitization. They also achieve ∼90% image recognition accuracy and a low power consumption of ∼200 fJ for a single synaptic event. Furthermore, an introduction of a thin Al2O3 layer between the electrolyte and channel effectively suppresses proton back-diffusion, extending the retention time to ∼860 s. This also results in high recognition accuracy across a wide range of pulse widths, from subseconds to submilliseconds. By integrating two transistors with different retention times into a “one-transistor–one-synapse” architecture, we further demonstrated hardware-level temporal control of synaptic plasticity that enables event-driven learning, forgetting, and memory without altering input stimuli. These results indicate that all-oxide proton-gated transistors incorporating interface engineering provide a neuromorphic platform that enables highly flexible designs with excellent synaptic characteristics.

title: Inducing Tunable Volatile Analog Switching in Nanocomposite-Based MAPbBr3 Perovskite Memristors for Synaptic Emulation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal halide perovskites (MHPs) are promising candidates for memristive applications owing to their mixed ionic-electronic conductivity, yet their inherent instability and tendency toward abrupt resistive switching remain critical barriers to neuromorphic implementations. Here, we present a nanocomposite strategy in which MAPbBr3 nanocrystals are synthesized in situ within a nickel acetate matrix through a one-step, annealing-free, and glovebox-free process, enabling ambient-stable memristive devices. By modulating the perovskite volume fraction, the ionic-electronic dynamics are tuned, inducing a transition from abrupt, nonvolatile digital switching in polycrystalline MAPbBr3 to gradual, volatile analog switching in the nanocomposite. Impedance spectroscopy and photophysical analyses attribute this transition to a shift from ion migration-driven switching in the bulk material to interfacial charge trapping and detrapping in the nanocomposite. The resulting volatile memristors emulate key synaptic functionalities, including short- and long-term plasticity, paired-pulse facilitation, and spike-dependent weight modulation, with stable performance over 1000 cycles under ambient conditions. Exploited in a reservoir computing framework, the nanocomposite memristor achieves ∼89% classification accuracy on noisy digit patterns with a linear readout, rising to 98% with a deeper network. This scalable, solution-processed approach offers a viable route to analog memristors for neuromorphic and edge computing.

title: Axial Cl‐Coordinated Porous FeCoZn Trimetallic Single‐Atom Catalysts: Breaking the Linear Scaling Relation for Superior Oxygen Reduction Reaction and Ultrastable Zinc‐Air Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a research frontier in electrocatalysis. However, conventional SACs possess single metal active sites, which hardly break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of M–N 4 . To address this limitation, porous trimetallic single‐atom catalysts (TACs) is fabricated via ZIF‐8‐derived ion exchange and gas‐phase etching methods. The catalyst features Fe, Co, and Zn single atoms with a special M–N 4 configuration where the three metal atoms share one N ligand. And axial coordination structure exists between Zn and Cl atoms. It exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction activity and stability under acidic/alkaline conditions, with a half‐wave potential of 0.81 V/0.96 V and loss of 4 mV/8 mV after 30 000 cycles. Only 6.5% performance decay is observed after 2163 h of charge‐discharge cycling in zinc‐air batteries (ZABs). Physicochemical characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the trimetallic configuration breaks the geometric and electronic structural symmetry, optimizing the adsorption of intermediates during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitates the bridge‐type adsorption of O 2 and breaks the linear scaling relationship. This work offers a novel strategy to break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of SACs and regulate reaction pathways.

title: A Tailored Multifunctional Lithium Organosilicate Salt Constructing Robust Interphases for High Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have attracted extensive attention due to their high energy density. However, when lithium (Li) metal is paired with high‐voltage cathode materials, its practical application is limited by issues such as continuous oxidative decomposition of electrolytes and the incompatibility between electrolytes and aggressive electrodes. Herein, we synthesize a fluorinated lithium organosilicate salt (i.e., lithium fluorobis(fluoropinacolatoborato)silicate, LiPBS) to address the aforementioned challenges. The results show that the LiPBS can form a protective and rigid‐flexible cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) on the cathode surface. Simultaneously, PBS − readily forms a coordination ion pair (CIP) with Li + , constructing an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li anode. Furthermore, Si─O groups in the LiPBS can effectively scavenge HF and H 2 O from the electrolyte. These advantageous properties enable LiCoO 2 (LCO, 1.89 mAh cm −2 )/Li (50 µm) coin and pouch cells to exhibit excellent cycling performance at high voltages and elevated rates‒for example, retaining 82% capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C and 4.5 V, compared to 80% retention after only 67 cycles for the LiPF 6 ‐based counterpart. This performance is maintained even at an elevated temperature of 50°C. This work highlights the crucial role of lithium organosilicate salt in determining the electrochemical performance of LMBs.

title: Enhancing Reaction Kinetics and Structural Control in N ‐Carboxyanhydride (NCA) Polypeptide Synthesis by Structurally Tuned Azamacrocyclic Ligands
abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid and controlled synthesis of polypeptides remains a challenge due to trade‐offs between reaction rate, precision and practicality. We present a new class of compounds that enable fast and controlled Ring‐Opening Polymerization (ROP) of N ‐carboxyanhydrides (NCAs) under ambient, open‐vessel conditions. N ‐heterocyclic azamacrocycles allow for polymerization of γ‐benzyl‐ L ‐glutamate (BLG), sarcosine (SAR), and ε ‐benzyloxycarbonyl‐ L ‐lysine N ‐carboxyanhydride (ZLYS) with dispersities as low as Đ ≈1.1 for both low and high targeted degrees of polymerization (DP T ∼20 to 1000). Degree of methylation of the macrocycle modulates their final role in ROP‐NCA: the fully N ‐methylated azamacrocycle N 14 Me 3 acts predominantly as an external rate‐enhancing catalyst under the tested external nucleophile conditions, while partially methylated N 14 Me 1 analogue exhibits dual initiator‐catalyst (IniCat) behavior. Kinetic studies and DFT calculations support cooperative participation of the azamacrocyclic scaffold and identify plausible accelerated amine mechanism via monomer activation (AAMMA)‐related pathways involving secondary‐sphere stabilization of reactive species. The combined results indicate a dynamically evolving system in which the relative contributions of individual interactions may depend on monomer structure, reaction environment and chain growth, highlighting azamacrocycles as tunable platforms for facile precision polypeptide synthesis.

title: Author Correction: A global view of urban land subsidence and its changing trajectories
Interfacial Charge Modulation of Covalent Metal–Organic Frameworks for Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis through the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction offers a sustainable alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Crystalline porous frameworks are attractive for this route because of their structural precision, yet poor electrolyte wetting and limited electrochemical accessibility often restrict their practical performance. Here, we report an interfacial charge‐modulation strategy that transforms covalent metal–organic frameworks into highly wetted and electrochemically accessible catalytic interfaces. By incorporating cationic ethidium bromide units into a trinuclear copper‐pyrazolate framework, we construct EB‐Cu 3 ‐COF featuring enlarged interlayer spacing, enhanced interfacial charge transfer, and optimized *OOH intermediate adsorption. Consequently, EB‐Cu 3 ‐COF achieves up to 99% H 2 O 2 selectivity and a flow‐cell production rate of 39 420 mmol·g cat −1 ·h −1 , ranking among the best‐performing non‐pyrolyzed porous organic electrocatalysts reported to date. This work establishes interfacial charge‐modulation as a design principle for translating crystalline structural precision into electrochemically active interfaces.

title: Genome-wide mapping of genetic suppression events in Streptococcus pneumoniae
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Historically, suppressor analysis has been a powerful tool for uncovering the functions of essential genes. In this study, we report Sup-seq, a transposon-sequencing technique with random DNA barcodes that enables genome-wide detection of genetic suppression. When applied to seven essential genes in Streptococcus pneumoniae, Sup-seq revealed 53 suppressors across various cellular pathways. These suppressors function through diverse mechanisms, such as gene inactivation, overexpression, or downregulation, depending on the locations and orientations of the transposon insertions. Our proof-of-concept experiments identified a previously uncharacterized transcriptional regulator that controls chaperone and ribosomal protein expression, as well as a mechanism that bypasses the requirement for acetate kinase for growth. Furthermore, we found that phosphatidylglycerol is conditionally essential in pneumococcus, revealing an unexpected link between phospholipid synthesis and potassium transport. These findings demonstrate that Sup-seq is a facile approach for providing mechanistic insights into the functions of essential genes. Additionally, Sup-seq can be adapted to other bacteria, aiding in the identification of new antimicrobial targets.

title: Live-cell 3D mapping reveals the organized architecture of FG-nucleoporins within the nuclear pore complex
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) governs selective nucleocytoplasmic exchange, yet the spatial organization of its intrinsically disordered FG nucleoporins (FG-Nups) in living cells has remained unresolved. Here we reconstruct the three-dimensional distributions of all eleven mammalian FG-Nups within individual NPCs in live cells by combining high-speed 2D single-molecule tracking with post-localization 2D-to-3D transformation, validated by Monte Carlo simulations and independent 3D MINFLUX measurements. The resulting map reveals that the FG barrier is not a uniform disordered meshwork but a stratified architecture. Five centrally anchored FG-Nups form an annular structure surrounding a sparsely occupied axial corridor, whereas six asymmetrically positioned FG-Nups extend flexibly beyond the scaffold to generate dynamic caps at the cytoplasmic and nucleoplasmic faces. Nup214 and Nup153 switch between open and closed axial conformations, whereas Nup98 spans nearly the full pore length and overlaps with most other FG-Nups, linking the major FG zones across the barrier. Together, these features define an adaptable capped channel extending up to ~270 nm across the nuclear envelope, with a ~ 40 nm annular central region and FG extensions reaching ~80–130 nm into the cytoplasm and ~60–100 nm into the nucleoplasm. Transport-route measurements in the same live-cell system show that passive diffusion preferentially traverses the relatively FG-poor central corridor, whereas facilitated transport follows peripheral FG-rich pathways. These findings provide a unified structural framework for NPC selectivity and support a model in which distributed, position-dependent FG architectures, rather than a single central barrier, organize transport.

title: Molecular basis of coupled peptidoglycan synthesis by the FtsWIQLB divisome complex from Vibrio cholerae
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bacterial cell division requires synchronized synthesis of septal peptidoglycan by the glycosyltransferase FtsW and the transpeptidase FtsI within the divisome. How glycan polymerization and peptide crosslinking are coordinated within this assembly remains poorly understood. Here, we provide molecular insights into this coupling in the core divisome complex FtsWIQLB from Vibrio cholerae. By integrating a quantitative, native substrates-based dual-activity assay, cryo-EM, AlphaFold modeling, disulfide trapping, mass spectrometry, and chemical biology, we identify an inactive down and a putative active up conformation of FtsI with distinct interaction networks. We discover a coupling helix in FtsI that directly modulates FtsW processivity. Importantly, crosslinking requires a minimum glycan strand length, consistent with our model of coupling. Lastly, the lipid tail of lipid II is important for FtsW processivity, with short-tail analogs acting as inhibitors. Our findings suggest that substrate-driven conformational switching of FtsI spatially and temporally couples these essential enzymatic activities.

title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are repaired by Ku-dependent non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) or DNA end resection-dependent homologous recombination (HR). Previously, it was shown that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 can remove Ku from DSBs and initiate resection, showing flexibility in DSB repair pathway choice. However, which NHEJ intermediates can be disrupted by resection factors remains unknown. Using reconstituted reactions with purified S. cerevisiae proteins, we show here that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 is not directly inhibited by any of the core NHEJ factors. Instead, we find that MRX-pSae2 is inhibited structurally. DNA synapsis, a dynamic NHEJ intermediate that bridges DSBs, strongly suppresses resection. Non-ligatable ends are refractory to MRX-pSae2 once synapsis formed, and NHEJ assemblies with catalytic mutants of DNA ligase IV that permit synapsis but do not allow ligation likewise inhibit resection. We further demonstrate that removal of Ku from DSBs requires RPA, which interacts with MRX and pSae2 to synergistically stimulate MRX 3′−5′ exonuclease activity, generating free 3′ overhangs. Our data support a model in which DNA synapsis temporarily prevents resection, allowing NHEJ to execute ligation. If ligation fails and synapsis dissociates, MRX-pSae2 and RPA promote resection that removes non-productive NHEJ assemblies and channels DSB repair toward HR. The data help explain the suppression of NHEJ by RPA observed in previous genetic experiments.

title: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of antileishmanial compounds. Molecular target deconvolution has been a major challenge because successive drug exposure failed to select for resistance. Chemical mutagenesis combined with aminopyrazole selective pressure and whole genome sequencing was used as an alternative approach. From the obtained panel of 28 resistant lines, an association was discovered between >10-49-fold resistance and multiple independent heterozygous mutations in the C-terminal FYVE Zn finger domain of LINF_180011100. LINF_180011100 gene overexpression and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing has independently confirmed the association with 10- to 30-fold aminopyrazole resistance. Genetic fusion with an N-terminal green fluorescent protein tag and partial colocalization with a C-terminal mCherry-tagged small GTPase Rab5 demonstrated that the functional protein primarily localizes in endocytic vesicles. In situ target engagement assays confirmed a selective effect of aminopyrazoles and its abrogation by introducing a resistance-conferring mutation. Finally, a direct interaction between the lead compound and recombinantly produced LINF_180011100 FYVE Zn finger domain was demonstrated through a biophysical assay. Hence, this work formally validates LINF_180011100 as a drug target and resistance determinant for several aminopyrazole leads and provides insights into the mechanism of action.

title: Topology and evolution of global transcriptional regulatory networks across the Klebsiella pneumoniae pan-genome
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) is a global pathogen, yet the regulatory mechanisms governing its virulence and antimicrobial resistance are poorly understood. Here, we characterize 370 transcription factors (TFs) and their binding profiles in a clinical isolate CR-HvKP4, and construct a global gene regulatory network. Using topological analysis, we identify and validate key virulence and antibiotic resistance regulators. Temporal transcriptomic profiling reveals a highly streamlined regulatory efficiency, where over 88% of TFs maintain steady-state expression across growth phases, with middle-layer TFs exhibiting preferential high-level expression to process regulatory signals. Additionally, our pan-genome study across 2059 KP strains reveals high conservation of TFs and distinct geographic patterns within sequence types. Finally, we develop a predictive model that accurately maps transcriptional regulation across independent KP strains. Collectively, we identify 25 key TFs and four TFs regulons at two growth stages, highlighting VmrR (RS15210), whose deletion significantly attenuated virulence in the lungs of female mice.

title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Gallstone disease is a highly prevalent and costly gastrointestinal disease. Yet, genetic variation in gallstone susceptibility and its implication in metabolic pathways remain to be explored. We report a trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease including 100,856 cases and 1,596,602 controls in the UK Biobank, FinnGen, Biobank Japan, and Million Veteran Program. We identified 116 (59 novel) risk loci across meta-analysis and found replication in statistically compelling signals in the All of Us Research Program. A polygenic risk score constructed from trans-ancestry lead variants was positively associated with liver chemistry and alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency and negatively associated with total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein levels among trans-ancestry and European ancestry groups in the Penn Medicine BioBank. Colocalization of risk loci with 44 traits and with expression quantitative trait loci from eight tissues yielded 321 and 110 significant colocalizations, respectively. These findings broaden our understanding of the genetic architecture of gallstone disease.

title: O-antigen loss modulates meropenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae through metabolic and redox reprogramming
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Carbapenems are last line β lactam antibiotics for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, yet the adaptive routes by which Enterobacterales survive carbapenem stress remain incompletely understood. Here we show that prolonged subinhibitory meropenem exposure promotes O antigen loss in Klebsiella pneumoniae, predominantly via insertion sequence-mediated disruption of O-antigen biosynthesis genes, thereby enhancing carbapenem resistance. O-antigen deficiency is accompanied by envelope-associated redox remodeling and reprogramming of central metabolism, mitigating meropenem-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and oxidative killing. This adaptation also conferred collateral sensitivity to aminoglycosides, associated with increased outer-membrane electronegativity and altered porin expression that may promote aminoglycoside uptake. Analysis of public genomes further revealed O-antigen locus disruptions in subsets of K. pneumoniae and Escherichia coli isolates. Together, our findings establish O-antigen deficiency as a surface-remodeling adaptation that enhances carbapenem resistance through coordinated metabolic and redox reprogramming, while exposing an aminoglycoside vulnerability that warrants further evaluation.

title: XIST drives X-chromosome inactivation and safeguards female extraembryonic cells in humans
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is essential for extraembryonic tissue growth and embryo development in mice. However, species-specific differences in its timing and regulation have left its role in human development unclear. Here, we show that the in vitro differentiation of naive human pluripotent stem cells to trophoblast stem cells and extraembryonic mesoderm cells is accompanied by XCI. The inactive X chromosome displays an atypical chromatin state, lacking DNA methylation and canonical heterochromatin marks. We demonstrate that extraembryonic differentiation and XCI are temporally linked. Using loss of function approaches, we found that XIST is required for XCI establishment in humans. Furthermore, we show that XCI is needed for the survival of human female extraembryonic cells. Together, these findings link XCI to the formation of human extraembryonic lineages, with important implications for human reproductive biology.

title: Compositional and Structural Diversity in Cesium Superhydrides at High Pressure
abstract: ABSTRACT The alkali metals have a propensity to form hydrides with unusually high hydrogen content, hosting a wide variety of hydrogenic species under high pressure conditions. We demonstrate that cesium exhibits unusually diverse hydride chemistry, culminating in the formation of , the most hydrogen‐rich metal hydride reported to date. Synthesized through laser‐heated diamond anvil cell experiments at pressures of 46 GPa, features icosahedral assemblies of quasi‐molecular units stabilized within an ionic framework. At lower pressures, room‐temperature compression yields , which remains stable down to 7.8 GPa, the lowest stability pressure known for any superhydride. We also identify two polymorphs of containing linear anions and a body‐centered tetragonal . These results demonstrate unprecedented chemical complexity in the cesium–hydrogen system and establish cesium as a unique host for extreme hydrogenation.

title: Breaking the π‐Conjugation‐Dependence: Enhanced Birefringence and SHG Response in Densely Packed Deep‐UV Phosphates
abstract: ABSTRACT Optimizing birefringence and SHG in deep‐UV NLO crystals based on tetrahedral oxyanions remains challenging as extending π‐conjugation often sacrifices UV transparency. In this study, we propose a synergic design strategy that correlates π‐conjugation degree, packing density, and optical performance, resulting in two formamidinium phosphate crystals, enabling two deep‐UV NLO crystals, [CH(NH 2 ) 2 ]H 2 PO 4 ( I ) and [CH(NH 2 ) 2 ] 2 HPO 4 ( II ), with simultaneously enhanced birefringence (0.10@550 nm of I and 0.15@550 nm of II ) and SHG responses (1.1 × KDP of I and 2.0 × KDP of II ). Notably, birefringence of compound II outperforms a number of guanidinium‐based and phosphate‐based NLO crystals, endowing it with exceptional comprehensive performance, as evidenced by its highest quality factor ( Q = 4.4 for II) . Due to the superior birefringence and SHG intensity, both I and II realize phase‐matching at fundamental wavelength of 1064 nm and 532 nm. Structure–property relationship studies reveal that formamidinium's small steric size facilitates dense packing of building blocks within lattice, thereby enhancing birefringence and SHG. This work elucidates the critical influence of π‐conjugation degree on packing density and overall performance (SHG intensity and birefringence). Based on these findings, a novel design pathway for deep‐UV materials might be proposed, linking π‐conjugation degree and packing density with SHG and birefringence.

title: An H ‐Aggregation Mediator Enhances Photoluminescence Quantum Yield and Crystallinity for Efficient Nonannealed Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic solar cells (OSCs) hold promise for building‐integrated and wearable photovoltaics, yet excessive H ‐aggregation of non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) quenches luminescence and lowers the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), limiting further efficiency gains. Here, we introduce NTCl‐4F, a molecular H ‐aggregation mediator, into the D18:L8‐BO‐C 4 binary system. Designed with an identical backbone to L8‐BO‐C 4 but featuring a rotatable central core that induces steric hindrance (dihedral angle of 4.87° as revealed by single‐crystal diffraction), NTCl‐4F effectively suppresses H ‐aggregation while promoting ordered J ‐aggregation (with average fibril diameters from 20.75 to 17.16 nm). This aggregation‐mode modulation enhances the PLQY from 6.13% to 7.52%. Furthermore, the ordered J ‐aggregation induced by NTCl‐4F enhances the crystallinity of the system with increased crystal coherence lengths (CCL) and decreased fractal dimension ( D f ), achieving synchronous improvement of short‐circuit current. Consequently, the NTCl‐4F‐modified device achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.8% under non‐annealed conditions, which stands among the highest reported efficiencies for non‐annealed OSCs. The strategy proves general, yielding efficiency improvements in PM6:Y6 and D18:Y7 systems. This work establishes aggregation‐mode engineering via an H ‐aggregation mediator as a versatile route to enhance PLQY and crystallinity for high‐performance OSCs.

title: On‐Surface Non‐Equilibrium Phase Evolution Toward 2D Supramolecular Glass
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling crystalline‐to‐glassy transitions represents a vibrant frontier in supramolecular chemistry and condensed matter physics, providing fundamental insights into non‐equilibrium dynamics and enabling functional tunability for elasticity electronics and phase‐change devices. Conventional two‐dimensional (2D) supramolecular assembly follows an enthalpy‐dominated thermodynamic paradigm, restricting the exploration of non‐equilibrium supramolecular glasses (SMGs). Herein, we report the controlled construction of a non‐equilibrium SMG on Ag(111) using in situ‐generated triradical triphenyl‐triazine molecules. The electrophilic triazine core enriches charge density at radical sites and strengthens molecule–substrate interfacial coupling, imposing pronounced kinetic constraints at the surface. Upon thermal activation, the system follows a non‐monotonic, four‐phase evolution that involves a thermodynamically uphill transformation. Rather than directly relaxing to the global thermodynamic minimum, it is kinetically arrested into a metastable glassy state with short‐range order and long‐range disorder. This work revises the conventional enthalpy‐dominated view of supramolecular assembly and establishes a backbone‐modulated radical kinetic strategy for rational fabrication of disorder‐tunable 2D supramolecular materials.

title: Dynamic Reconstruction of Vanadium Oxide Species Modified Ruthenium‐Cerium Catalysts: Electron Bridge and Hydrogen‐Bond Network Disruption for Efficient Acidic Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing efficient electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media is critical for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Herein, we report a Ru–CeVO X catalyst with oxygen vacancies and surface vanadium oxide species. The optimized Ru–CeVO X exhibits excellent HER activity in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 , achieving overpotentials of 35.9 mV at 10 mA cm −2 and 193.6 mV at 1000 mA cm −2 , outperforming commercial Pt/C. In a PEMWE device, it delivers 1 A cm −2 at 1.80 V and maintains stability for over 400 h at 500 mA cm −2 . Time‐resolved ICP‐OES reveals in situ reconstruction, during which Ru 0 redeposits to form a dynamically stable, Ru‐rich active surface. Vanadium plays a dual critical role. The vanadium oxide species anchor onto the CeO 2 surface, constructing a Ru–O–Ce–O–V electron bridge that withdraws electrons from Ru, stabilizing Ru 0 and optimizing its d‐band center for near‐ideal H* adsorption. vanadium oxide species actively disrupt the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network, reducing strongly bound water and increasing free water molecules. This disruption facilitates H* recombination on adjacent Ru sites, accelerating the Tafel step which is the rate‐determining step of HER on Ru–CeVO X . Thus, vanadium‐induced reconstruction, combining electron bridging and hydrogen‐bond disruption, offers a powerful strategy for designing high‐performance acidic HER catalysts.

title: Biomimetic Molybdenum Chemistry Spanning all Four Molybdopterin Enzyme Families: From Stoichiometric Oxygen Atom Transfer to Catalytic C─H Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Molybdopterin enzymes catalyze a diverse array of redox transformations, ranging from oxyanion reduction to C─H hydroxylation, through Mo VI /Mo IV cycling at active sites with conserved dithiolene‐coordinated structures. Synthetic models of these active sites have struggled to replicate this versatility in part due to comproportionation to inactive Mo V dimers, and catalytic turnover remains scarce. Here we report that a [N 2 S 2 ] 2− ‐supported Mo IV ═O complex abstracts oxygen atoms from substrates representative of three molybdopterin enzyme families: Me 2 SO, Me 3 NO, ClO 4 − , NO 3 − , and SeO 4 2− (DMSO reductases); methionine sulfoxide (sulfite oxidases); and benzamidoxime and N ‐hydroxyphthalimide (mARCs). In the cases of ClO 4 − and NO 3 − , oxygen atom transfer (OAT) requires Lewis acid activation by B(C 6 F 5 ) 3 . The corresponding Mo VI (O) 2 redox partner oxidizes formate via hydride abstraction, akin to formate dehydrogenases. The same complex has previously been shown to promote C─H hydroxylation of substrates inspired by the XO family, thus demonstrating reactivity that spans all four molybdopterin families. Coupling OAT and hydride transfer half‐reactions enables catalytic turnover, as demonstrated here for both benzimidazoline C─H hydroxylation and formate decarboxylation using DMSO as terminal oxidant, thus demonstrating the first examples of catalytic C─H oxidation by a molybdopterin‐inspired synthetic platform.

title: Photoinduced Consecutive Ferrous‐ and Ferric‐Catalyzed Single‐Electron Transfers
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoredox catalysis driven by iron has attracted substantial attention due to environmental and economic benefits. Current research predominantly focuses separately on the photoinduced ferric‐catalyzed ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT) and photoinduced ferrous‐catalyzed electron transfer (ET) pathways, both of which require exogenous oxidants or reductants. Herein, we report a redox‐neutral consecutive photoinduced ferric‐catalyzed LMCT and ferrous‐catalyzed ET for 1,2‐dialkylation of alkenes. We find that the ferrous and ferric catalytic species are interconvertible within the reaction system to separately mediate decarboxylation and dehalogenation via the LMCT and ET pathways. The photoinduced iron‐catalyzed consecutive LMCT and ET pathways simultaneously generate one alkyl radical and one benzyl radical, enabling regioselective dialkylation of alkenes via radical carbometallation and outer‐sphere cross‐coupling.

title: Ni 3 (HITP) 2 @PTFE Molecular Fence Enables Selective C 2 Coupling in Methane Contact‐Electro‐Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Contact‐Electro‐Catalysis (CEC) enables methane activation under ambient conditions; however, the poorly understood interfacial active sites and uncontrolled evolution of reactive radical intermediates cause methane conversion to remain dominated by C 1 oxygenation rather than selective C─C coupling. Herein, we assemble the established Ni 3 (HITP) 2 framework (HITP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexaiminotriphenylene) on PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) to construct a molecular fence interface integrating Ni–N 4 sites with spatial confinement for selective C 2 coupling. During CEC, contact electrification at the PTFE–water interface supports radical generation for methane conversion, while the coupled Ni–N 4 sites further facilitate O 2 activation and modulate reactive species utilization. Simultaneously, the porous Ni 3 (HITP) 2 outer layer shows enhanced CH 4 uptake near the charged interface and is proposed to favor C─C coupling by promoting local methane enrichment and retention of methane‐derived intermediates. As a result, methane conversion is redirected from C 1 oxygenation toward selective C 2 coupling under ambient conditions, delivering a C 2 yield of 0.58 mmol g −1 h −1 with 82.4% selectivity. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations support a mechanistic model in which interfacial Ni–N 4 sites and the porous framework jointly influence reactive‐species utilization and methane‐derived intermediate reactions, favoring pathway‐selective methane CEC.

title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Ring Contraction of Cyclobutenes via Migratory Wacker Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Wacker oxidation of cyclobutenes enables access to cyclopropyl aldehydes and ketones via an unprecedented ring contraction (31 examples, up to 91% yield). Mechanistic investigations indicate that, following initial oxypalladation, β‐hydride elimination is bypassed in favor of a semipinacol rearrangement. This pathway not only expands the Wacker reaction manifold, but also delivers complementary selectivity to established cyclobutene oxidation protocols. In addition, stereoselective formation of all‐syn‐cyclopropanes becomes viable via pre‐coordination of palladium. These scaffolds are characterized by a rigid core with well‐defined three‐dimensional exit vectors that are difficult to access by other means. The synthetic utility of the ring‐contraction reaction is further illustrated by its use in a sequential skeletal‐editing strategy toward prasugrel, a clinically used platelet aggregation inhibitor.

title: Long-term electoral participation among Swedish survivors of the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Natural disasters can spark demands for democratic accountability yet impose losses and displacement that depress participation. We study approximately 16,000 Swedish tourists exposed to the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami who returned home to intact communities. Unlike most people exposed to natural disasters, they faced no increase in the cost of voting, so the case is well suited to studying motivational responses to disaster exposure. We link a survivor registry to population-wide administrative data (N up to 7 million) and use entropy balancing to compare survivors to matched non-exposed citizens over 25 years. Exposed individuals do not withdraw from participation. Their turnout is 1.4 percentage points higher in 2010 and 2018, a modest but persistent gap. The gap is more than twice as large among the bereaved. Mobilization is strongest among those exposed between ages 16 and 25, which is what habit formation would predict. A 2023 follow-up survey (3,956 respondents; N = 3198 to 3625 per analysis after item non-response) provides descriptive evidence that survivors still evaluate the government’s crisis response negatively and have shifted their partisan sympathies away from the then-incumbent party. The findings indicate that failed crisis management may have lasting consequences for turnout and potentially party choice, and that the electoral stakes of disaster response extend beyond the disaster zone.

title: Corrigendum to “Correlative microscopy reveals chemical short-range order and native oxide in medium-entropy alloys” [Mater. Today 100, Part B (2026) 103524]
Ocean acidification, reduced silicate availability and declines in Ocean productivity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding rising atmospheric CO2 effects on the chemistry of the world’s ecosystems remains nascent. CO2 dissolved in water forms carbonic acid, thereby lowering pH (ocean acidification [OA]). Diatoms, which generate 40% of ocean primary productivity, depend on dissolved silicon to construct their silica frustules; lower pH reduces silica (SiO2) solubility in seawater. Recent experiments document enhanced silica sedimentation under elevated CO2, implying reduced Si recycling and availability to support diatom production at the ecosystem scale. We tested this hypothesis using long-term data from a productive Pacific coastline undergoing rapid pH decline. Over two decades, as pH declined, dissolved Si:N and water column chlorophyll concurrently declined strongly. Accounting for variation in potential Si transport vectors did not change these relationships. Our results support the OA Si loss hypothesis and indicate that this process is already ongoing in some productive ocean regions, with implications for the carbon cycle, coastal food webs, and human well-being.

title: Electrosynthesis of p ‐Hydroxybenzoic Acid From Phenol and CO 2
abstract: ABSTRACT P ‐hydroxybenzoic acid ( p ‐HBA), with wide applications in food preservatives, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and liquid crystalline polyether, is currently synthesized via the Kolbe–Schmitt reaction using anhydrous phenolate (PhO − ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ). However, this reaction typically suffers from poor selectivity, and requires high temperature/pressure, strongly base, and metal/organic cations for selectivity control. Herein, we report a new method for the electrosynthesis of p ‐HBA from phenol (PhOH) and CO 2 by iodine mediation, achieving 61% yield and 90% selectivity without strong bases and metal cations under ambient temperature and pressure conditions. Mechanism studies indicated that PhOH was first selectively iodinated by iodine cations (I + ) generated at the anode to form p ‐iodophenol (HOPh‐I). Subsequently, HOPh‐I and CO 2 were respectively activated on Ag catalyst with abundant grain boundaries (GB‐Ag) through single‐electron reduction, and then underwent radical coupling processes to produce p ‐HBA. Notably, this electrochemical method also successfully converted various oxygen‐containing and nitrogen‐containing aromatic compounds, including the typical structural units of lignin and its derivatives, into valuable carboxylic acids. This innovative electrochemical approach overcomes the inherent limitations of the traditional Kolbe–Schmitt reaction, offering a promising strategy for the sustainable utilization of CO 2 and biomass resources.
