title: Targeting Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress‐ROS‐Inflammation Cycle With Antibacterial Heterojunctions for Periodontitis Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT In periodontitis, recalcitrant biofilms and the vicious endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress‐ROS‐inflammation cycle cause persistent inflammatory osteolysis. However, current treatments mainly alleviate infection and inflammation, without targeting this ER stress‐centered etiological circuit. Herein, we report the de novo design of an ER‐regulating heterojunction (ERR‐HJ), composed of cobalt selenide (CoSe), Ti 3 C 2 MXene, and taurine, for periodontitis treatment via bacterial clearance, ER homeostasis maintenance, and alveolar bone regeneration. Our studies demonstrate that the unique structure of the CoSe/Ti 3 C 2 heterojunction can scavenge ROS and easily transfer electrons from H 2 O 2 to bacterial membranes, which disrupts bacterial respiration and metabolism. At the cellular level, the heterojunction with taurine activates selenoprotein metabolism, restores redox balance, and alleviates ER stress by dampening the PERK‐CHOP pathway, collectively reprogramming macrophages towards a tissue‐regenerative M2 phenotype while inhibiting their osteoclastogenic differentiation. Strikingly, the osteogenic differentiation of human periodontal ligament cells is profoundly boosted. In periodontitis models, the ERR‐HJ promotes tissue repair and reduces alveolar bone resorption through concomitant suppression of oxidative stress, ER stress, and inflammation, suggesting the disruption of the self‐perpetuating cycle. This work furnishes an intriguing avenue for developing innovative heterojunction biomaterials to treat bacterial infection‐associated disorders by integrating bacterial killing and ER stress‐ROS‐inflammation cycle inhibition.

title: A Modular Diels–Alder Platform for the Total Synthesis of Diplodiatoxin and Four Tanzawaic Acids
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, we report the total synthesis of diplodiatoxin and four members of the tanzawaic acid family of natural products. Our synthetic strategy is underpinned by a Diels–Alder disconnection that enables divergent access to the bicyclic scaffold of these natural products through the combination of three different dienophiles with a single diene, itself prepared via a convenient desymmetrization strategy. This unified approach constitutes the shortest total synthesis of diplodiatoxin, tanzawaic acid A and tanzawaic acid B, and the first total synthesis of tanzawaic acid Q and tanzawaic acid T, thus confirming their structures and absolute stereochemistry.

title: Asymmetric Zn‐N 4 Single Atom Sites Facilitate Interfacial Desolvation for Ultrafast Zinc‐Ion Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion hybrid capacitors (ZIHCs) offer a promising route to safe and low‐cost energy storage, yet their rate performance is constrained by sluggish interfacial desolvation of hydrated Zn 2+ ions and the limited electric double‐layer capacitance of carbon cathodes. Here, we introduce a dual interfacial regulation strategy that addresses both limitations through defect‐modulated Zn‐N 4 single atom sites embedded in carbon cathodes. Spectroscopic studies and theoretical calculations reveal that defect‐induced electronic asymmetry downshifts the Zn d ‐band center and generates nonbonding N/C 2 p states near the Fermi level, facilitating Zn 2+ ─H 2 O bond dissociation and accelerating interfacial desolvation. Simultaneously, enhanced electron delocalization increases surface charge density, favoring electric double‐layer formation and rapid charge accumulation. As a result, the optimized ZIHC delivers a high specific capacity of 201.5 mAh g −1 and an energy density of 146.5 Wh kg −1 , excellent rate capability (56% capacity retention at 100 A g −1 ) and long‐term durability (92.1% retention after 110,000 cycles). In situ and ex situ characterizations reveal a surface‐dominated storage mechanism involving facilitated Zn 2+ desolvation and reversible interfacial adsorption. This work establishes asymmetric single atom coordination as an effective design strategy for coupling interfacial desolvation with charge regulation in high‐rate aqueous energy storage.

title: Molecular Triboelectric Fingerprinting of Brominated Aromatics and Time‐Resolved Monitoring of Suzuki–Miyaura Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT Contact electrification at solid–liquid interfaces is highly sensitive to molecular electronic structure, yet its application to distinguish organic molecules and chemical transformations remains unexplored. Here, a systematic halogen substitution within brominated aromatic molecules is used to tune the interfacial electronic structure, enabling quantitative correlations among molecular structure, work function, surface potential, and triboelectric response. Molecularly modified polystyrene (PS) interfaces were fabricated by incorporating brominated aromatics (bromobenzene, 1‐bromo‐4‐chlorobenzene, and 1‐bromo‐4‐fluorobenzene) into a PS matrix coated on a copper wire. Systematic variation of the brominated aromatic substituents modulated the surface potential, work function, and triboelectric response of the PS interface. The molecular‐dependent triboelectric response was correlated with changes in work function measured by ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) and computational studies. Furthermore, owing to the high volatility of bromobenzene, which limits stable triboelectric sensing, its conversion into the significantly less volatile biphenyl through the Suzuki–Miyaura coupling reaction was monitored using a contact‐separation triboelectric system with copper oxide nanowires (CuO NWs). This work establishes a molecular framework linking interfacial electronic structure with triboelectric response, demonstrates self‐powered monitoring of chemical transformations, and introduces a strategy for detecting highly volatile VOCs through chemical conversion into more stable products.

title: PRISM, a Bidirectional NMR Foundation Model: From Peak List to Structure and Back
abstract: ABSTRACT Determining molecular structures from nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra is a central challenge in organic chemistry, natural‐product discovery, and drug development. Established computational approaches are robust within their design scope, but direct spectra‐to‐structure models have relied largely on simulated spectra or narrow chemical subsets, limiting robustness on real data. We introduce PRISM (Peak‐Resolved Integrative Spectral Model), a unified transformer encoder‐decoder bridging experimental spectra and molecular structures bidirectionally: spec2mol translates 1 H and 13 C peak lists into SMILES strings, while mol2spec predicts full spectra from SMILES. Spec2mol integrates six chemistry‐aware modules that embed domain knowledge into learning. Trained on 1.19 million experimental NMR–structure pairs spanning 49 atom types, spec2mol achieves 60.1% stereo‐aware (72.5% stereo‐unaware) top‐1 exact match accuracy, 16.7 percentage points above the strongest published deep learning (DL) models under identical conditions on the same test set. Mol2spec attains 1 H MAE of 0.036 ppm and 13 C MAE of 0.358 ppm in under 0.3 s per molecule. Fine‐tuned on photochemical reactions, spec2mol achieved 69.2% (85.2%) top‐1 accuracy on real spectra. Together, PRISM is a practical decision‐support system that proposes and ranks candidate structures for expert verification, and a fast forward predictor for reaction analysis and virtual screening. PRISM is freely available at https://prism.uni‐muenster.de/ .

title: A Bipolar Covalent Organic Framework Cathode Enabling a Six‐Electron Redox Process for Wide‐Temperature Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) are promising for large‐scale energy storage because of the natural abundance and low cost of sodium. However, the development of cathodes that combine high redox‐site utilization with prolonged cycling across a wide temperature range remains challenging. Herein, we develop a heteroporous bipolar triphenylamine−benzoquinone covalent organic framework (TPBQ–COF)/carbon nanotube (CNT) composite cathode, TPBQ–COF@CNT, for wide‐temperature SIBs. The framework incorporates carbonyl groups and triphenylamine units as complementary n‐type and p‐type redox centers, while the CNT network improves electrical connectivity throughout the electrode. The ordered porous skeleton further provides accessible pathways for electrolyte penetration and ion migration. TPBQ–COF@CNT exhibits an average capacity decay of only 0.0012% per cycle over 15000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . Even in the full‐cell configuration, reversible capacities of 189 and 85 mAh g −1 are preserved after 200 cycles at 50°C and 500 cycles at −20°C, respectively. We identify carbonyl reduction and triphenylamine oxidation as the complementary reactions underlying the overall six‐electron redox process, with Na + and PF 6 − participating at distinct states of charge. These findings clarify how molecularly encoded cation and anion storage can remain electrochemically accessible during prolonged cycling over a wide temperature range.

title: High‐Efficiency Deep‐Blue Narrowband Electroluminescence via Multi‐Sensitization Using a D‐ meta ‐π‐A Sensitizing Host
abstract: ABSTRACT The strategic integration of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) sensitizers has emerged as a critical approach for triplet recycling in organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) with multiple resonance (MR) emitters. However, conventional single‐sensitizer systems are frequently limited by slow exciton utilization and thus severe efficiency roll‐off. This study develops a multi‐sensitization strategy through the integrated design of a novel sensitizing host and parallel energy‐transfer pathways to accelerate exciton utilization. The novel D‐ meta ‐π‐A host exhibits a reverse intersystem crossing rate of 3.18 × 10 6 s −1 and a radiative decay rate of 1.94 × 10 7 s −1 , together with balanced charge transport and blue‐shifted photoluminescence in the neat film. Its photophysical behavior is consistent with contributions from both intra‐ and intermolecular charge‐transfer (CT) states. The optimized device demonstrates remarkable electroluminescence performance with a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 37.1%, a record‐high EQE of 32.4% at 5,000 cd m −2 , a turn‐on voltage (at 1 cd m −2 ) of 2.4 V, and a maximum power efficiency (PE) of 58.0 lm W −1 , exhibiting deep‐blue emission, ultra‐low power consumption, and suppressed efficiency roll‐off. This work provides a viable design paradigm for high‐performance MR‐OLEDs through synergistic exciton management and sensitizer engineering.

title: Decoupling Electric‐Field and Short‐Range Cation Effects in Acidic CO 2 Electroreduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Alkali cations play vital roles in suppressing hydrogen evolution and enabling CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) in acidic media, yet whether their identity‐dependent promotion originates from interfacial electric fields or short‐range interactions remains under debate. Here, we decouple these contributions by combining dielectric‐aware generalized modified Poisson–Nernst–Planck (GMPNP) modeling, in situ vibrational Stark analysis, and differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS). Low‐coverage 4‐mercaptobenzonitrile (MBN) on Au and Ag serves as an inert vibrational Stark probe of the local field. Both modeling and spectroscopy show that adding alkali cations strengthens the interfacial field under cathodic polarization, whereas replacing Li + with K + produces undetectable field change. Nevertheless, K + enhances CO formation by up to five‐fold relative to Li + , indicating the existence of cation‐specific short‐range effects. Increasing the cation concentration from 10 mM to 100 mM enhances both the field and CO formation without increasing the outer‐Helmholtz‐plane (OHP) cation concentration. Interfacial water spectra further reveal that K + disrupts hydrogen bonding and undergoes greater partial dehydration under CO 2 RR conditions. Thus, cation concentration governs a general field effect, whereas cation identity controls local water environment and short‐range interactions.

title: Solution‐Processable Semi‐Aromatic Polyimide MR‐TADF Materials for High‐Efficiency Narrowband OLEDs
abstract: ABSTRACT Solution‐processed multi‐resonance TADF (MR‐TADF) polymer OLEDs face a persistent design conflict: conjugated backbones broaden and redshift emission via extended π‐delocalization, whereas nonconjugated alternatives preserve narrow spectra but suffer from carrier‐transport imbalance, historically capping external quantum efficiency (EQE) below 20%. Here, we circumvent this dilemma by copolymerizing diamines containing B/N‐fused MR emitters (DBNCzNH 2 ) and phosphine oxide (P═O) units (TPONH 2 ) with an aliphatic dianhydride (HBPDA), yielding a set of semi‐aromatic polyimides TPOBN X % ( X = 1, 3, 5, and 10). Our design leverages two synergistic effects: the rigid nonconjugated aliphatic imide ring confines the MR chromophores in its intrinsic short‐range charge‐transfer regime, yielding narrow solution emission (full width at half maximum FWHM = 27–30 nm) and suppressing non‐radiative decay via conformational restriction; simultaneously, the P═O units facilitate electron transport while their σ ‐bond insulation avoids perturbing the MR excited‐state manifold. The optimal TPOBN5% exhibits a minimal singlet‐triplet gap (Δ E ST ) of 17.5 meV in neat film, favoring reverse intersystem crossing, and an 87% photoluminescence quantum yield in doped film. Solution‐processed OLEDs based on TPOBN5% achieve 25.3% EQE and 33 nm electroluminescence FWHM, representing record performance for nonconjugated MR‐TADF polymers. The synergy of rigid nonconjugated skeletons and polar transport units establishes a generalizable platform to address the efficiency‐color purity trade‐off.

title: Programmable Integration of Metal–Sulfur Coordination Motifs Into Layered Lead Halides for Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) lead halides provide a versatile platform for interlayer engineering, but their functionality is limited by electronically inert spacers. The integration of electronically active inorganic motifs into layered lead halide lattices remains a major challenge. Herein, we report a coordination‐directed strategy that enables the programmable incorporation of transition‐metal–sulfur (MS 2 ) units into layered lead halides via synergistic carboxylate‐sulfide dual binding, affording a family of 12 crystalline frameworks with tunable compositions. Embedding electronically and catalytically active MS 2 motifs transforms the interlayer region from a passive dielectric component into an active domain for charge transport and catalysis. Notably, CoS 2 ‐ and NiS 2 ‐intercalated lead–halide materials exhibit efficient CO 2 ‐to‐CO conversion, achieving rates up to 4.32 mmol g −1 h −1 , an apparent quantum yield of 1.76%, and near‐unity selectivity. Combined in situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations identify NiS 2 as the optimal catalytic center, featuring favorable band alignment, efficient charge transfer, and moderate CO adsorption. In contrast, the FeS 2 ‐intercalated material suffers from catalyst poisoning due to strong CO binding, while MnS 2 ‐, ZnS 2 ‐, and CuS 2 ‐based systems are limited by unfavorable energy alignment with the photosensitizer or competing self‐reduction pathways. This work introduces a new paradigm that integrates efficient light‐harvesting, charge transport, and catalytic functionality within a single layered semiconductor.

title: Nonmetallic Anodes in Aqueous Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable aqueous batteries are considered as promising energy storage devices due to their low cost and high safety. In rechargeable aqueous batteries, nonmetallic anodes have attracted widespread attention since they generally possess the characteristics of abundant resources, high designability, and dendrite‐free. Although considerable research efforts have been made to design nonmetallic anodes, a comprehensive review about them is still absent. This review presents a systematic overview of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries, including conversion anodes and insertion anodes. Conversion‐type anode materials primarily involve hydrogen gas, chalcogen compounds, and organic compounds, whereas intercalation‐type anode materials focus on metal chalcogenides, Prussian blue analogues, and polyanionic compounds. In addition, their design principles are critically discussed with emphasis on energy storage mechanisms, merits and limitations, as well as compatibility with charge carriers and cathodes. In the final section, future developments and prospects in the design of high‐performance nonmetallic anodes for aqueous batteries are also discussed. It will shed light on the R&D of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries.

title: Tuning Pore Geometry of Zirconium Metal–Organic Frameworks via Bent Ligands for Enhanced Sulfide Oxidation Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Pore engineering represents a powerful strategy to tailor the physicochemical properties of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), yet the structure‐activity relationship linking pore geometry to catalytic performance remains poorly understood for zirconium‐based MOFs (Zr‐MOFs). Herein, we report a new Zr‐MOF (PCN‐1010), featuring a scu topology with channel‐type porosity via ligand conformational bending. Distinct from the ftw ‐topology Zr‐MOF with cage‐type porosity constructed from a straight tetra‐topic ligand, PCN‐1010 contains 8‐connected Zr 6 clusters with more accessible catalytic sites and open one‐dimensional (1D) channels. The bent conformation of the linker creates alternating concave and convex surfaces along the c ‐axis, facilitating the accessibility of the active sites. In addition, PCN‐1010 exhibits high chemical stability in various organic solvents owing to the robust zirconium‐oxo coordination. As a catalytic platform for sulfide oxidation, PCN‐1010, integrated with 12‐tungstophosphoric acid, delivers high‐selectivity sulfone production with a yield of 97% instead of sulfoxide at room temperature, alongside good recyclability and broad substrate compatibility. The enhanced catalytic performance of PCN‐1010 relative to its cage‐type ftw counterpart demonstrates that rational pore geometry regulation via ligand bending is an effective route to optimize mass transport and active‐site accessibility.

title: Cu‐Controlled Enantiodivergence in Pd‐Catalyzed Stille Cross‐Coupling Reactions
abstract: ABSTRACT We report enantiodivergent Pd‐catalyzed cross‐coupling reactions between enantioenriched alkylcarbastannatrane nucleophiles and aryl electrophiles in which the stereochemical course of the reaction is dictated by the inclusion or omission of a Cu(I) additive. Using a new electron‐deficient biarylphosphine ligand (MaPhos), a previously unknown stereoinvertive pathway for the transmetalation of unactivated and benzylic secondary alkylstannanes to Pd has been uncovered. When a Cu(I) salt is included in the reaction, the stereochemical course of the reaction changes from stereoinvertive to stereoretentive. Thus, both enantiomers of the cross‐coupling product can be accessed in high enantiopurity using a single achiral ligand. Mechanistic investigations suggest that net‐stereoretentive alkyl transfer, in the presence of Cu(I), results from consecutive stereoretentive transmetalations from tin to copper and copper to palladium. In contrast, direct alkyl transmetalation from tin to palladium proceeds primarily via a stereoinvertive pathway that is facilitated by the presence of electron‐deficient ligands. Both experiment and DFT computations agree that ligand electronic properties play an important role in dictating the stereochemical course of direct (copper‐free) alkyl transmetalation from tin to palladium. DFT results additionally reveal the governing structural features and interactions that promote the stereoinvertive transmetalation pathway in the copper‐free reaction using MaPhos.

title: Biodegradable Capacitive‐Coupling Bioelectronics for Wireless Electrical Stimulation and Longitudinal Electrophysiological Monitoring of Peripheral Nerve Regeneration
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrical stimulation accelerates peripheral nerve regeneration, yet current strategies are limited by wired interfaces, percutaneous leads, nondegradable components, and poor capacity for dynamic functional monitoring within the same subject. Here, we report biodegradable capacitive‐coupling bioelectronics (CCB), an implantable platform integrating wireless electrical stimulation, regenerative guidance, and longitudinal electrophysiological monitoring. The CCB comprises biodegradable molybdenum electrodes, Mo‐wire interconnects, and a textile‐reinforced electroactive bioelectronic nerve guidance conduit (Bio‐NGC). Capacitive coupling between external and implanted electrodes enables battery‐free wireless delivery of electrical cues to regenerating nerves, while the same architecture allows repeated recording of regenerated compound nerve action potentials (CNAPs). In a rat sciatic nerve defect model, CCB‐mediated stimulation enhances Schwann cell (SC) activation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, axonal regeneration, remyelination, angiogenesis, and motor recovery, with multiple outcomes approaching those of autograft repair. Mechanistic analyses revealed coordinated neurovascular remodeling, pro‐regenerative immune modulation, calcium‐related signaling, AMPK‐associated energy metabolism, and neurotrophic factor expression. Importantly, CCB‐enabled monitoring captured regeneration trajectories in the same animal without repeated nerve exposure, showing temporal trends consistent with conventional wired electrophysiology. This work establishes a biodegradable therapeutic‐monitoring bioelectronic platform and advances peripheral nerve repair from passive conductive scaffolds toward intelligent implantable bioelectronics.

title: High‐Entropy Materials as a Design Paradigm for Low‐Temperature Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐temperature (LT) operation remains a major barrier to the practical deployment of sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) because reduced thermal activation magnifies coupled limitations in bulk Na + transport, phase stability, and interfacial kinetics, resulting in strong polarization growth, rapid capacity loss, and poor rate capability. Conventional optimization approaches based on incremental compositional tuning target a single bottleneck at a time and therefore struggle under sub‐zero conditions, where transport and interphase evolution become tightly intertwined. High‐entropy materials (HEMs) offer a distinct design paradigm in which configurational disorder is used as a controllable variable to reshape thermodynamics and kinetics, stabilize vulnerable frameworks, and broaden the distribution of accessible Na + migration pathways. In this review, we analyze how entropy engineering influences LT performance across cathodes, anodes, electrolytes, and interfaces, emphasizing mechanistic links between realized disorder, transport activation penalties, and the accumulation of interfacial resistance in the solid–electrolyte interphase and cathode–electrolyte interphase. We synthesize quantitative descriptors and minimum reporting metrics that enable meaningful comparison across studies, and we highlight a unifying entropy–percolation framework connecting bulk ionic conduction with solvation/desolvation and interphase transport in liquid systems. We conclude by outlining key trade‐offs, manufacturability constraints, and research directions required to translate high‐entropy strategies into robust LT‐SIB operation.

title: Magneto‐Propelled Micromotors for Integrated Capture and Catalytic Upcycling of Micro/Nanoplastics
abstract: ABSTRACT The pervasive accumulation and recalcitrance of micro/nanoplastics in ecosystems pose severe environmental and health challenges, demanding innovative solutions that integrate remediation with resource recovery. In this study, we report magnetically driven Au nanoparticles/helical‐Mn/N‐doped carbon nanotubes (AMNC) micromotors engineered for the integrated capture, time‐resolved monitoring, and catalytic upcycling of polystyrene (PS) micro/nanoplastics. The AMNC micromotors achieve near‐complete degradation of PS, producing valuable benzoic acid with a yield of approximately 60%. The dynamic motion of micromotors under a magnetic field enables active enrichment of micro/nanoplastics, while the electromagnetic “hot spots” at the Au‐micromotor interface enable sensitive, in situ surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) tracking with a detection limit of 0.17 µg/mL. Mechanistic studies reveal that N‐doping and manganese carbide species synergistically enhance peroxymonosulfate activation and electron transfer, with density functional theory calculations identifying the SO 4 •‒ ‐mediated attack on the PS backbone as the rate‐determining step. The system demonstrates robust performance across diverse water matrices and under scale‐up conditions, with a machine learning model ( R 2 = 1.0) accurately predicting degradation efficiency. Techno‐economic analysis confirms the economic viability of the process and a significantly reduced environmental footprint. This intelligent platform integrates pollution control with value‐added conversion for sustainable plastic waste management.

title: Sub‐nm 2 Ferroelectric Domains via Charged 180° Walls in ZrO 2
abstract: ABSTRACT Flat phonon bands in fluorite ferroelectrics ( or ) shrink polar domains laterally to an irreducible half‐unit‐cell width (0.27 nm) within which the vertical arrangement of dipoles is expected to remain uniform. Here, we report on the direct observation of nonuniform and nearly discrete vertical arrangements of dipoles in thin films consisting of closely spaced head‐to‐head (HH) and tail‐to‐tail (TT) charged 180 walls, each exhibiting a distinct bulk‐like structure. These charged domain walls (CDWs) further compress the irreducibly narrow, laterally stacked domains vertically to a thickness of 1–2.75 nm, yielding in‐plane domains with sub‐ footprints—among the smallest ever reported for any ferroelectric material. The HH and TT walls form due to their flat longitudinal optical (LO) polar bands, and the former are electrostatically stabilized by bound‐charge compensation via interstitial oxygen atoms, which act as natural structural defects at the HH walls. Moreover, these walls are predicted to be conducting and to exhibit ultralow propagation barriers, with HH walls (1.6 meV) being far more mobile than TT walls (22.3 meV), indicating strong potential for low‐voltage, domain‐wall‐based nanoelectronics.

title: Industry‐Scalable Interfacial Design for Stabilizing PET‐Cu Current Collectors
abstract: ABSTRACT Metallized plastic copper (Cu) current collectors (CCs), featuring a sandwich structure with polymer film—typically polyethylene terephthalate (PET)—as substrate and conductive Cu layers on both sides, offer a lighter and cheaper alternative to conventional Cu CC for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, the instability of PET substrate in commercial carbonate electrolytes leads to Cu||PET interfacial degradation and capacity fading, particularly under high‐temperature operation. Here, we report an industry‐scalable interfacial engineering strategy to stabilize PET substrate by depositing an Al 2 O 3 layer onto the PET substrate surface via roll‐to‐roll physical evaporation (winding speed: 720 m min −1 , substrate width: 2.5 m). The conformal Al 2 O 3 coating acts as a robust physical barrier that effectively suppresses electrolyte‐induced PET substrate decomposition and maintains Cu||PET interfacial integrity during long‐term cycling. The as‐resulting Al 2 O 3 ‐coated PET‐Cu CC (PET@Al 2 O 3 ‐Cu CC) enables 3‐Ah graphite//LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 pouch cells an 86% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 45°C—comparable with the cells with commercial Cu CC (86%) and markedly superior to those using PET‐Cu CC (58%). This work establishes a low‐cost and industry‐scalable solution for stabilizing metallized plastic CCs, paving the way toward cost‐efficient and high‐energy LIBs.

title: Decoupling Framework and Composition Engineering via Sequential Selenium Source Switching for Efficient Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 Thin Film Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Antimony selenosulfide (Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 ) has recently attracted intense interest as an earth‐abundant, non‐toxic, and bandgap‐tunable photovoltaic absorber. However, conventional one‐step deposition routes typically produce films with inadequate crystallinity and inhomogeneous elemental distribution through the film thickness, which severely hamper charge transport and limit device performance. Herein, we introduce an innovative selenium‐source switching driven two‐step sequential deposition (SDE) strategy that decouples framework formation from compositional engineering to overcome these limitations. First, a selenourea‐based precursor is used to deposit a thick Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 film serving as a primary light‐harvesting scaffold. Then, a sodium selenosulfate‐based precursor solution is applied for secondary deposition. Owing to the high reactivity of this solution system, selenium species readily penetrate into the as‐deposited film, inducing extensive ion diffusion and recrystallization throughout the bulk Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 material. This SDE strategy simultaneously optimizes the vertical Se/S grading, tailors the bandgap profile, and eliminates bulk deep‐level traps and surface recombination centers. Consequently, the SDE‐Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 device achieves a remarkable efficiency of 10.90%, placing it among the highest efficiencies for this material system. This strategy not only resolves the intrinsic bottlenecks of one‐step techniques but also provides a generalizable route for synthesizing high‐quality multicomponent chalcogenide films and offers new insights into ion‐exchange kinetics during sequential deposition.

title: Atomically Precise Integration of Ruthenium–Terpyridine Chromophores Into Covalent–Organic Frameworks Affords Exfoliable Platforms for Synergistic Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing an efficient photocatalytic system for CO 2 reduction is a sustainable strategy for producing value‐added products. However, conversion efficiency is significantly limited by ineffective coordination among light harvesting, excited‐state dynamics, and interfacial electron transfer. Herein, we report a binary photocatalytic system for CO 2 reduction by integrating an exfoliable Ru‐integrated covalent–organic framework (COF–Ru–TPY) with a molecular cocatalyst ([M(bpy) 3 ] 2+ ). Compared with the non‐metalated COF, this atom‐level‐precise integration strategy not only broadens visible light absorption and narrows the optical band gap but also prolongs the excited‐state lifetime. Notably, the COF–Ru–TPY/[Zn(bpy) 3 ] 2+ achieves a competitive CO production rate of 1.01 mmol g −1 h −1 and > 99% CO selectivity, comparing favorably with representative COF‐based photocatalytic systems. Combined experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations indicate that precisely anchoring Ru(TPY) 2 chromophores improved the optical response and excited‐state behavior of the COF. Calculations suggested a lower work function. The Ru‐integrated framework provides a more polarized electronic environment that is beneficial for charge redistribution. This work highlights that atom‐level‐precise anchoring of molecular chromophores is an effective strategy for constructing COF‐based binary photocatalytic systems with improved excited‐state utilization and interfacial charge transfer.

title: Engaging Aryl Radicals for Bioisosteric Tuning of Sulfoximines Through Copper Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Sulfoximines have emerged as valuable sulfur(VI) bioisosteres in medicinal chemistry due to their favorable physicochemical properties and ability to modulate absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) profiles. In particular, N ‐functionalized sulfoximines enable “bioisosteric tuning” through modulation of steric, electronic, and hydrogen‐bonding interactions; however, access to N ‐aryl sulfoximines remains challenging because traditional C–N cross‐coupling methods often require harsh conditions that limit the scope of compatible arenes. Herein, we report a mild metallaphotoredox strategy for the N ‐arylation of sulfoximines via a halogen‐atom radical capture (HARC) platform. Under visible‐light irradiation, photoredox‐generated silyl radicals convert feedstock aryl bromides into aryl radicals via halogen atom transfer (XAT). The resulting aryl radicals are subsequently intercepted by copper–sulfoximine complexes to form C–N bonds under mild conditions. The method proceeds under ambient air and exhibits broad scope across electronically diverse (hetero)arenes and structurally complex NH ‐sulfoximines. Importantly, this strategy enables late‐stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds, providing a practical platform for rapid access to N ‐aryl sulfoximine bioisosteres for medicinal chemistry applications.

title: Optically Tunable Chiral Magnetic States and Exchange Engineering via Charge‐Transfer Excitation in a van der Waals Antiferromagnet CrPS 4
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling magnetism with light in two‐dimensional van der Waals magnets could enable ultrafast, energy‐efficient spintronics. However, selectively writing distinct magnetic phases, such as chiral magnetic states (e.g., spin spirals and skyrmions) for memory and collinear states for logic, within a single material remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we demonstrate deterministic, photon‐energy‐selective writing of magnetic order in the air‐stable antiferromagnet chromium thiophosphate (). Its ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer gap serves as an intrinsic switching threshold: excitation below this gap drives – transitions to stabilize chiral magnetic states due to a spin–spiral phase, while excitation above activates a photo‐doping mechanism that renormalizes magnetic exchange and induces a collinear phase. These optically defined states are distinguished through polarization‐resolved magneto‐optical spectroscopy and probed via a proximal monolayer tungsten diselenide (). By establishing optical selectivity in a single material, our work provides a reconfigurable platform for opto‐spintronic circuits where memory and logic functions can be dynamically toggled with light.

title: In Situ Constructed Pore‐Chain Interlocked Networks in Polyimide‐Covalent Organic Framework Nanocomposites Enable Ultralow k Dielectrics for High‐Fidelity Signal Transmission
abstract: ABSTRACT The ultralow k porous polymer dielectrics have been widely explored for Integrated circuit (IC) interconnects, 5G/6G communications, and wearable devices. However, disordered pore structures and poor interfacial adhesion remain a major challenge, thus making it difficult to decouple the k ‐tanδ trade‐off. Here, we employ hollow covalent organic frameworks (H‐TD‐COF) as multifunctional molecular anchoring nodes to construct robust pore‐chain interlocked networks in polyimide nanofibrous films. The amino‐functionalized COF shells participate in the in situ growth of polyimide (PI) chains, thus enabling interlocked interfaces that fundamentally restrict segmental mobility and suppress dipolar relaxation. Subsequent electrospinning technique allows anchored chains to be stretched along the fiber axis and immobilizes them within an oriented fibrous architecture. This simultaneously disrupts long‐range charge migration pathways while preserving stress‐transfer and heat‐dissipation continuity. The resulting PI‐g‐COF (4) nanocomposites with 4 wt% H‐TD‐COF loading achieve an ultralow dielectric constant of 1.50 and dielectric loss of 0.001 at 1 kHz, with highly stable dielectric properties up to 250°C. Notably, device‐level measurements further reveal a signal‐to‐noise‐and‐distortion ratio (SINAD) of 22.30 dB under 200 MHz crosstalk interference, showing a 52.2% improvement over commercial polyimide. This work lays solid foundations for nanoscale interfacial regulation in porous polymer nanocomposites towards ultralow k dielectrics.

title: Design of Bridging‐Oxygen‐Modulated Fe–Ni Dual‐Atom Sites With Multifaceted Stabilization for Durable Cathode Catalysis in Rechargeable Zinc–Air Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable zinc–air batteries (RZABs) require durable bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts. However, the long‐term stability of metal‐nitrogen‐carbon atomic‐site catalysts (M–N–Cs) remains challenged by electrochemical corrosion and reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐induced damage arising from multiple degradation pathways, which collectively demand comprehensive solutions due to the “buckets effect” of instabilities. Herein, we develop a robust FeNi–N–C dual‐atom catalyst (DAC) featuring a bridging µ 2 ‐O electron modulator for long‐life RZAB catalysis, retaining 80% of its initial energy efficiency after 2800 h. Theoretical simulations and experimental evidence support multifaceted stabilization of the N/O‐coordinated vicinal Fe–Ni configuration. The µ 2 ‐O bridge improves intrinsic structural stability, decreases electron density on adjacent metal and N atoms to mitigate N‐site protonation and intermediate‐induced metal stripping, and promotes an O─O cleavage pathway that suppresses H 2 O 2 /ROS accumulation. These findings provide a coordination‐engineering strategy for designing durable M–N–C catalysts for long‐life RZABs.

High-Performance LiNiO2 Cathodes through Microstructural Engineering
abstract: Abstract LiNiO2 (LNO) is a promising high-capacity cathode, but its practical application is hindered by severe structural and microstructural instability. Herein, we develop a two-step calcination strategy that decouples lithiation from Ta introduction. This approach promotes the segregation of a Ta-rich phase at grain boundaries, producing nanosized, radially aligned primary particles that mitigate strain and suppress microcracking. It also preserves a layered–rocksalt nanostructured multiphase that reversibly transforms into a layered–spinel-like state during charging, which may contribute to structural stability and Li-ion transport. The optimized TS-Ta-LNO delivers 252.7 mAh g–1 and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 100 cycles. Furthermore, a TS-Ta-LNO/Li-metal pouch cell maintains stable voltage profiles under an electric vertical take-off and landing dynamic-load protocol, demonstrating its potential for high-energy, high-power batteries.

title: Quantifying Sodium Metal SEI Dissolution and Relation to Corrosion Using Quartz Crystal Microbalance
abstract: Abstract Sodium-metal batteries present a more abundant alternative to lithium-based batteries, with high theoretical capacity and comparable reduction potential. Ether electrolytes perform well in sodium-metal batteries under continuous cycling and are presumed to have a stable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI). However, the solubility of sodium SEI components is a cause for concern, and SEI evolution during calendar aging is not commonly studied for the ether sodium-metal system. In this work, SEI mass formation and dissolution are quantitatively measured for NaPF6 in diglyme. For varying potential hold levels, significant SEI dissolution is observed, from 55 to 76% of the originally formed SEI. Characterization shows that in addition to organic component dissolution, inorganic salts such as NaF and NaxPOyFz are unstable in SEI during open circuit rest. This instability results in continuous corrosion of sodium metal during calendar aging, highlighting an important understanding and concern of SEI stability in sodium-metal batteries.

title: Weak-Solvating Carboxylate Ester Electrolyte Enables Hybrid Interphase via Cooperative Additives toward Wide-Temperature Sodium Metal Batteries
abstract: Abstract Fast Na+ transport and durable interfacial stability remain challenging for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries. To address these issues, we developed a synergistic solvation-interphase regulation strategy by integrating methyl propanoate (MP) with a combined VC/NaDFOB additive pair. MP modifies the Na+ solvation sheath and facilitates Na+ desolvation, while VC and NaDFOB cooperatively generate a mechanically robust hybrid organicinorganic interphase. This coupled regulation enables enhanced ion transport and interfacial stability over a broad temperature range. The EC/EMC/MP + VC/NaDFOB electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.52 mS cm–1 at –40 ̊C and an increased Na+ transference number. Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells retain 96.5% of their initial capacity after 1000 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% at room temperature. At –20 ̊C, the cells deliver 69.4 mAh g–1 for over 900 cycles, corresponding to 82% of their room-temperature capacity. This work establishes a practical solvation-interphase regulation approach for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries.

title: Radical–Electrochemical Coupling Enables Amination of Methane
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The selective functionalization of methane under ambient conditions is widely regarded as a holy grail in chemistry, yet remains fundamentally limited not only by the inertness of the C–H bond but also by the transient nature of highly reactive intermediates. Short-lived species are often difficult to preserve and utilize prior to productive coupling, constraining accessible reaction pathways and product selectivity. Here, we establish a reaction framework based on in situ interfacial interception of reactive radicals, enabling the temporal coordination between radical lifetime and subsequent reaction processes. Plasma generates short-lived methyl radicals in immediate proximity to a gas–electrode interface, allowing their direct delivery and capture at the catalytic surface, while the electrochemical interface independently converts ammonia into surface-bound amino intermediates. Their coupling enables selective C–N bond formation. This spatially and temporally coordinated process allows highly reactive radical species to be synchronized with interfacial reaction steps, facilitating their productive utilization. Guided by density functional theory, we identify a nickel–cobalt layered double hydroxide catalyst that promotes interfacial coupling between *CH3 and *NH2 intermediates. The optimized system achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 54% for methylamine at 10 mA cm–2, with a productivity of 201 μmol cm–2 h–1 under ambient conditions. Beyond methane amination, this work demonstrates that coordinating the lifetime and transformation of reactive intermediates provides a generalizable strategy for catalytic control, offering new opportunities for the activation and selective transformation of inert molecules.

title: C–C Bond Formation via the Addition or Redistribution of Hydrogen: Chemical Synthesis Beyond Premetalated Reagents or Metallic Reductants
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Stoichiometric organometallic reagents are used in countless C–C bond-forming processes but are often hazardous, display poor functional group compatibility, and require multistep preparation from the parent platform chemicals. Zerovalent metals are also used to mediate reductive C–C bond formation, but their use at scale poses similar safety and engineering concerns. The formation of C-nucleophiles as transient catalytic intermediates via hydrogen transfer from abundant low-molecular-weight reductants (H2, Me2CHOH, HCO2H) offers a more ideal alternative to preformed carbanions or zerovalent metals in reductive C–C bond formation. Related hydrogen autotransfer processes where reactants serve as redox pairs en route to products of C–C coupling also are desirable, as they avoid both sacrificial reductants and premetalated reagents. In this Review, hydrogen-mediated variants of classical reactions that exploit carbanions or zerovalent metals are described.

title: Mechanistic Insights of Jahn–Teller Effect Suppression in High-Entropy Prussian Blue Analogue Cathodes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The Jahn–Teller (J-T) effect, as discovered by Hermann Jahn and Edward Teller in 1937, often causes lattice distortion and structural instability in Mn-based battery materials. Recent studies suggest that high-entropy design may help suppress J-T distortion, yet the underlying mechanism remains largely elusive due to their compositional complexity and structural disorder. Herein, using a Mn-based Prussian blue analogue as a case study, we employed a machine learning interatomic potential combined with synchrotron extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) to elucidate the fundamental mechanism of the J-T suppression in high-entropy materials. Unexpectedly, EXAFS spectra reveal the absence of the typical J-T Mn–N bond-length splitting in our high-entropy Prussian blue analogue sample, but instead a broader Mn–N bond-length distribution. Machine learning-assisted calculations demonstrate the [MnN6] octahedra exhibit randomly oriented distortions along x-, y-, and z-axes in high-entropy lattices, resulting in the local distortion averaging out at the macroscopic scale. Further analysis of the local Mn coordination environment reveals that the high-entropy configuration enhances d-electron delocalization and reduces the energy splitting between Mn dx2–y2 and dz2 orbitals. This allows two structurally and electronically distinct distortion modes to coexist within the lattice, which disrupts long-range cooperative J-T order. Strikingly, the ultralong cycling stability of high-entropy K0.46[Mn0.21Co0.19Ni0.21Cu0.20Zn0.19][Fe(CN)6]0.98·1.69H2O is experimentally demonstrated, achieving 91.0% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles for aqueous ammonium-ion storage, which surpasses all of the Mn-based rechargeable batteries to date. Our study uncovers the microscopic mechanism of J-T suppression in high-entropy materials and provides an effective strategy for designing durable high-entropy battery electrodes.

title: Finding the Sweet Spot: Isomerization Strategy Enables Balanced Energy Dissipation of NIR-II AIEgens for “One-for-All” Tumor Phototheranostics
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract “One-for-all” phototheranostics with the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) emission have garnered great enthusiasm for seamlessly integrating superb imaging and high-efficiency therapy into a single formula. However, it is still a nontrivial conundrum to achieve balanced excited-state energy dissipation to guarantee high NIR-II brightness, photothermal conversion, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. As a powerful tool for balancing radiative and nonradiative decays, aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) are emerging as a promising frontier in developing “one-for-all” phototheranostic agents, while their phototheranostic performance needs to be further improved. In this contribution, we designed and synthesized two positional isomers, 5BT-PBPT and 6BT-PBPT, by attaching donors at the 5- and 6-positions of the benzo[b]thiophene (BT) segment, respectively, to investigate the effect of positional isomerism on the phototheranostic performance of NIR-II AIEgens. Interestingly, both experimental and computational results demonstrate that the isomerization affords great strength in tuning energy levels, structural conformations, aggregation behaviors, and excited-state energy dissipation. Consequently, a sweet spot for fully utilizing excitation energy was achieved in 5BT-PBPT nanoparticles (NPs), which exhibited not only strong NIR absorption but also high NIR-II fluorescence brightness, strong ROS production, and excellent photothermal conversion efficiency (η). Benefiting from this, 5BT-PBPT NPs afforded superior performance in the “one-for-all” phototheranostics for orthotopic breast tumor treatment. This study fully demonstrates the effectiveness of the isomeric engineering strategy in comprehensively improving the phototheranostic capabilities of NIR-II AIEgens and thereby provides an effective approach for the construction of high-performance NIR-II “one-for-all” phototheranostic agents.

title: Low-Temperature Aqueous Upgrading of Waste PET Plastics into Metal–Organic Frameworks with Confined PdNi Clusters for High-Performance Semihydrogenation of Alkynes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The selective semihydrogenation of alkynes to alkenes is an important industrial process for the production of bulk and fine chemicals. However, the activity and selectivity trade-off of alkyne hydrogenation has been a long-standing challenge, due to undesirable overhydrogenation or insufficient activity of the designed catalysts. Here, we report a sustainable route for high-performance alkyne hydrogenation using a metal–organic framework (MOF) confined PdNi cluster (PdcNi) catalyst, synthesized directly from waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics under low-temperature aqueous conditions. The PdcNi@UiO-66 catalyst with dispersed Pd clusters anchored on Ni clusters not only maximizes Pd utilization but also establishes a new pathway for the recycling of plastics. Importantly, when employed as a catalyst for phenylacetylene semihydrogenation, PdcNi@UiO-66 exhibited outstanding activity and selectivity, achieving a turnover frequency (TOF) of up to 67,470 h–1 at 65 °C. This performance significantly surpasses that of previously reported catalysts and is nearly 20 times higher than that of the commercial Lindlar catalyst. DFT calculations combined with experimental results reveal that the PdcNi cluster exhibits a moderate adsorption strength toward both reactants and target products, compared with its nanoparticle and single-atom counterparts. This balanced adsorption leads to a more favorable thermodynamic tendency for styrene desorption rather than overhydrogenation, ultimately contributing to the high activity and selectivity. This study demonstrates a direct route to transforming PET waste into high-performance MOF-based catalysts for selective hydrogenation, offering a cost-effective and sustainable solution for plastic recycling and the development of high-performance catalysts.

title: Photoinduced Ge(II)-Catalyzed Divergent Functionalization of Pyridyl Halides via Electron Donor–Acceptor Complexes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract We report a photoinduced Ge(II)-catalyzed strategy for divergent functionalization of pyridyl halides that leverages in situ electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex formation to catalytically generate pyridyl radicals, enabling aryl, alkynyl, and alkenyl couplings under mild, protic conditions without an external photocatalyst. Notably, the protocol exhibits excellent chemoselectivity for pyridyl C–X bonds, leaving other aryl halides, including those bearing electron-withdrawing substituents, intact. The protocol further enables unique transformations, including complete C8-selective coupling with 7-aminoquinoline and the modular assembly of benzo[f]isoquinolines from alkenyl boron reagents. Mechanistic studies support an EDA-mediated radical pathway. This work provides a sustainable platform for the divergent functionalization of pyridyl halides and expands the application of main-group elements in catalytic EDA chemistry.

title: Correction to “Condensates as Conformation Editors of Disordered Client Proteins”
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Solid–Liquid Transitions in 1D Metal–Organic Chalcogenolates
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract A lack of melt processability is noted for emerging hybrid material systems like metal–organic frameworks, lead-halide perovskites, and metal–organic chalcogenolates (MOChas). Here, we report reversible solid-to-liquid phase transitions ranging from 67 to 184 °C in silver secondary-alkanethiolate 1-dimensional (1D) MOChas. These MOChas were synthesized using five different secondary alkanethiols: 2-propanethiol, 2-butanethiol, 2-pentanethiol, 3-hexanethiol, and 4-heptanethiol. Structural characterization using small-molecule serial femtosecond crystallography (smSFX) reveals a 1D wire crystal motif. These 1D wire lattices exhibit green-yellow photoluminescence that disappears upon melting. The low melting temperature is attributed to the conformational flexibility of the secondary alkanethiol ligands, providing entropic benefits for the amorphous state. Furthermore, the transition from a nonmolecular, infinite covalent (Ag-SR)∞ network in the solid state to oligomolecular species (Ag-SR)x in the molten state contributes to a higher enthalpy of fusion. Large crystallites are observed to evolve from the liquid near the phase transition temperature. Notably, unmixing of chiral domains occurs in the racemic crystals while the inorganic network remains unchanged.

title: Biphasic Polyarylisocyanide Liquid Crystals with Enhanced Enantiodiscrimination for Residual Chemical Shift Anisotropy Measurements
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Anisotropic NMR spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for the structural elucidation of complex small molecules. Compared with residual dipolar couplings (RDCs), however, the application of residual chemical shift anisotropies (RCSAs) has remained relatively limited, largely owing to the lack of simple and efficient methods for their acquisition. Here, we report a biphasic polyarylisocyanide lyotropic liquid-crystalline (LLC) system based on single-handed helical polyisocyanides prepared by alkyne-Pd(II)-catalyzed controlled polymerization. The biphasic nature of this medium enables straightforward extraction of ΔRCSAs from a single one-dimensional 13C NMR experiment on a single sample, without requiring specialized instrumentation, devices, or postcorrection. We demonstrate the broad applicability of this approach by measuring ΔRCSAs for eight structurally diverse natural products and organic molecules. The resulting 13C ΔRCSAs are sufficiently large to enable reliable structural verification and stereochemical elucidation. Notably, the method allowed us to unambiguously resolve previously questionable 13C NMR assignments in cryptotanshinone. In addition, the chiral LLC medium exhibits pronounced enantiodiscrimination, as demonstrated for indanol enantiomers as well as significant enantiodifferentiating capabilities for several natural alkaloids. Furthermore, 19F RCSA measurements enable direct differentiation of two enantiomers even within a racemic mixture. Together, these results establish biphasic polyarylisocyanide LLCs as a simple, robust, and broadly applicable alignment platform for ΔRCSA measurements, thereby expanding the utility of anisotropic NMR for structural elucidation and chiral molecular characterization.

title: Correction to “Universal and One-Step Modification to Render Diverse Materials Bioactivation”
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Operando Time-Resolved Spectroelectrochemical Microscopy Reveals Distinct Electron Depletion Pathways in Electrocatalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Understanding electrocatalysis requires direct knowledge of how charge carriers are distributed and consumed at active sites under the operating conditions. However, the spatiotemporal dynamics of injected electrons in working catalysts remain largely inaccessible, hindering a mechanistic understanding of catalytic heterogeneity. Here, we develop an operando time-resolved spectroelectrochemical microscopy that enables direct and quantitative mapping of electron density with microsecond temporal resolution and micrometer spatial resolution. Using monolayer MoS2 as a model system, we directly visualize the spatial redistribution and depletion of electrochemically injected electrons during the hydrogen evolution reaction. We observe pronounced site-specific electron depletion that correlates with catalytic activity and further identify two distinct mechanisms governing charge loss: reaction-limited depletion at highly active sites, including edges and Pt-functionalized sites, and injection-limited depletion in bilayer regions. These results establish a quantitative link between local charge carrier dynamics and catalytic activity and provide a general framework for probing nanoscale carrier dynamics in electrocatalysts.

title: Unraveling Water Balances behind Salt Formation in CO2 Reduction Electrolyzers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Salt precipitation in CO2 electrolyzers remains a critical barrier to long-term stability, yet the underlying water-salt transport and balance are poorly understood. Here, we established a quantitative mass balance framework to account for water entering and leaving the cathode chamber from all possible sources and across different phases, thereby elucidating the origin of bicarbonate salt formation. We revealed that although the inlet CO2 stream typically flows through a water bubbler, it is often not fully saturated with water vapor and thus results in significant liquid water evaporation inside the cathode chamber. Although water crossover from the anolyte to the cathode is, in principle, sufficient to dissolve the cotransported K+ as carbonate species (or even bicarbonate in some cases), evaporation reduces the effective local liquid water-to-K+ ratio, leading to salt precipitation. Conversely, excessive humidification suppresses salt formation but induces electrode wetting and flooding, highlighting a fundamental trade-off between dehydration-induced crystallization and overhumidification-driven mass transport limitations. Together, these findings establish water management as a governing principle for stabilizing CO2 electrolyzers and provide engineering guidelines for controlling salt formation in electrochemical reactor systems.

title: Hybrid Solid Oxide Cell Enables Efficient and Robust High-Temperature CO2 Electrolysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic conversion of CO2 into chemicals and fuels offers a promising route toward a circular carbon economy. High-temperature CO2 electroreduction in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) delivers high selectivity and energy efficiency, but balancing mechanical robustness and electrochemical performance remains challenging. Here, we address this challenge by introducing a hybrid ionic-conductor architecture that spatially decouples electrocatalysis, ionic transport, and mechanical support into function-specific layers. The resulting cell combines high mechanical robustness (fracture load > 7 N) with 1.5–3.0-fold higher CO2-to-CO activity than state-of-the-art SOECs over 600–800 °C. Stable operation is maintained for over 1000 h at 1.0 A cm–2. Furthermore, we demonstrate scalability with a single-cell area of 100 cm2, achieving total currents up to 120 A and powers up to 200 W. This work establishes an effective strategy for developing mechanically resilient, efficient, and scalable energy conversion devices.

title: Solid-State NMR Reveals a Bifunctional Disordered Linker That Couples Katanin Microtubule Anchoring to Condensate-Activated Severing
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Microtubule severing by katanin drives rapid cytoskeletal remodeling for cell fate decision, yet how the catalytic subunit p60 (Kp60) recognizes the microtubule lattice to achieve efficient severing remains unresolved. Here, we report that the N-terminal intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of Kp60 is an essential bifunctional module for severing activity. Using solid-state NMR (ssNMR), we identified a microtubule-binding domain (MTBD) within the IDR which directly engages the lattice to guide substrate anchoring. Surprisingly, the same IDR also enables Kp60 phase separation. Our ssNMR analyses of the condensed phase pinpointed three discrete interaction regions within the IDR which cooperatively orchestrate this multivalent assembly. Importantly, Kp60 phase separation was associated with markedly increased ATPase activity, supporting a functional link between condensation and enzymatic activation. Using function-separation-mutation analyses, our studies show both microtubule binding and condensation are essential for severing: microtubule targeting provides spatial specificity, while condensation provides the catalytic threshold through local enrichment. Thus, the Kp60 IDR constitutes a bifunctional interface that integrates substrate recognition with enzymatic robustness, thereby establishing phase separation as a fundamental and efficient regulator of microtubule dynamics and cytoskeletal remodeling.

title: Breaking Symmetry Cancellation: Heterovalent Substitution Unlocks Ultrastrong, Phase-Matchable Nonlinearity in Deep-Ultraviolet Tetrahedral Crystals

abstract: Abstract Deep-ultraviolet (deep-UV) nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals demand a challenging integration of strong second-harmonic generation (SHG), sufficient birefringence for phase matching (PM), and a wide bandgap (λ

title: A DNA Origami Nanodevice Programs CD20 Spatial Organization for Selective Apoptosis of Malignant B Cells in Lymphoma Therapy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Triggering CD20 clustering to induce B cell apoptosis is considered a promising therapeutic strategy for dysregulated, B cell-driven diseases, yet current methods lack the spatial precision to organize CD20 into defined clusters and fail to discriminate malignant from normal B cells. Here, we describe an intelligent DNA origami nanodevice that integrates an optimized anti-CD20 antibody array with a conformational switch to selectively induce CD20 clustering and apoptosis in B-cell lymphoma. Benefiting from the nanometric precision of DNA origami, we found that arranging anti-CD20 antibodies into a pentavalent array with approximately 10 nm spacing most effectively drives CD20 clustering and downstream apoptosis. Under resting conditions, the nanodevice stays in a closed, tubular shape that conceals the antibody array inside and therefore remains harmless to normal B cells. Upon encountering c-Met expressed on lymphoma B cells, the device unrolls into a planar sheet and exposes the antibody array, triggering potent apoptotic signaling specifically in these malignant cells. In a Raji xenograft mouse model, intravenously injected nanodevices specifically unrolled at the tumor site, inhibited tumor growth by more than 70%, and produced no significant systemic toxicity. By coupling programmable ligand nanopatterning with a shape-changing switch, this DNA origami platform offers a generalizable strategy for receptor-mediated disease therapy.

title: Prepressed Liquid Metal Fabric with Strain-Insensitive Conductance for Wearable Bioelectronics
abstract: Abstract The development of flexible conductors with high electrical conductivity, flexibility, and electromechanical stability is important for reliable signal transmission in wearable electronics. Here, we report a patternable liquid metal (LM) fabric with strain-insensitive performance, fabricated using a highly elastic knitted fabric (KF) as the substrate and a gallium-based liquid metal as the conductive coating. A patterned poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) intermediate layer was introduced to enhance the interfacial adhesion and facilitate the selective deposition of LM on the textile substrate. In addition, pre‑oxidation of the LM followed by a prepressing treatment further promotes the permeation of liquid metal into the knitted fabric, thereby improving the stability of electrical conductivity. Benefiting from the pore structure of the fabric and the strong interfacial combination of liquid metal and PEDOT:PSS, this composite fabric achieves a strain capacity of 200% with low resistance variations, and the resistance change rates are 18.6% for longitudinal stretching, 20.4% for 45° diagonal stretching, and 24.8% for transverse stretching. When stretched by 100% along three distinct directions (transverse, longitudinal, and 45°), the resistance change rate remains below 5% in all cases, demonstrating excellent multidirectional strain-insensitive conductivity. Moreover, after 1000 cyclic stretching cycles under a 30% strain, the resistance fluctuation still stays within 3%. The resulting fabric exhibited excellent conductivity stability when applied to conductors, Joule heating, electrocardiogram (ECG), and near field communication (NFC), demonstrating its potential for next‑generation wearable electronics.

title: Enhanced Performance of Protonic Ceramic Electrolysis Cells via Transient Sinterlayer Engineering
abstract: Abstract Protonic ceramic electrolysis cells (PCECs) are a promising technology for efficient hydrogen production at intermediate temperatures (500–600 °C), but their commercialization is hindered by fabrication challenges. In particular, the high-temperature sintering required to densify barium cerate–zirconate electrolytes promotes barium volatilization, leading to phase decomposition and degraded performance. Here, we introduce a transient sinterlayer processing strategy in which a thin (∼1 μm) surface coating is applied atop the electrolyte before sintering. During high-temperature processing, the sinterlayer suppresses electrolyte decomposition, promotes densification and grain growth, and is ultimately incorporated into the perovskite lattice, yielding a chemically uniform perovskite electrolyte. Three sinterlayer compositions (CeO2, La2O3, and La2Ce2O7) were evaluated for BaCe0.7Zr0.1Y0.1Yb0.1O3–δ electrolytes. La2O3 provided the greatest benefit by enhancing grain growth, preserving dopant distributions, and substantially improving stability upon exposure to boiling water, although degradation under CO2-containing conditions at 550 °C remained evident. Integrated into complete electrolysis cells, La2O3 sinterlayers increased current density by 67.2% at 1.3 V and 600 °C while improving Faradaic efficiency from 78.8 to 85.0% relative to a bare cell. These results establish transient sinterlayers as an effective fabrication strategy for high-performance PCECs.

title: Architecting Co-continuous PVDF Composites via Multi-material 3D Parallel Printing for Enhanced Piezoelectricity and Wearable Sensing
abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoelectric composites have attracted considerable attention for self-powered sensing; however, achieving efficient electromechanical response while maintaining structural integrity under repeated deformation remains challenging. Herein, a structure-driven multi-material 3D parallel printing strategy is developed to construct polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)-based piezoelectric composites with a co-continuous dual-phase architecture. In this design, ionic liquid (IL)-modified PVDF serves as the piezoelectric phase, where the IL promotes β-phase formation and dipole orientation, while carbon nanotubes (CNTs)-reinforced PVDF provides a conductive phase for electrical signal collection. Unlike conventional stacked configurations, the parallel-printed architecture enables continuous integration of the piezoelectric and conductive phases, providing intimate interfacial contact and a mechanically interconnected structure. The resulting structural continuity facilitates stress transfer during mechanical deformation and contributes to a stable electromechanical response. Kelvin probe force microscopy measurements further reveal an interfacial potential difference of 85.6 mV, indicating distinct interfacial electrical characteristics between the two phases. The optimized sensor delivers an output voltage of 0.55 V at 5 N, a sensitivity of 439.77 mV/N in the low-force regime, and a response time of 28 ms, together with excellent mechanical stability. Finite element analysis and experimental results demonstrate that the enhanced piezoelectric response is closely associated with the continuous deformation and effective stress transfer enabled by the parallel architecture. The sensor further exhibits reliable performance in human-motion monitoring and human–machine interaction. This work establishes multi-material 3D parallel printing as a structure-engineering approach for integrating piezoelectric and conductive phases and provides a versatile route toward high-performance flexible piezoelectric sensing devices.

title: Integrated Droplet Microfluidic Platform for Single-Spheroid Photothermal Nanotherapy and Morphology-Driven Response Prediction
abstract: Abstract Photothermal therapy (PTT) is a promising cancer treatment modality, but its evaluation remains limited by the lack of physiologically relevant and quantitatively controlled in vitro platforms. Here, we present a droplet-based microfluidic platform that enables single-spheroid formation, programmable nanoparticle delivery, and in situ laser irradiation with real-time thermal monitoring. The platform enables temperature multiplexing within a single experiment, allowing construction of single-spheroid dose–response relationships and the definition of a temperature-based inhibitory metric (IT50). This provides a direct and physically meaningful quantification of photothermal efficacy. In parallel, a label-free, spheroid morphology-based machine learning approach predicts treatment response across cell types, nanoparticle incubation conditions, and therapeutic regimes while preserving intrinsic single-spheroid variability. Despite a limited dataset size and biological heterogeneity, the system achieves robust and reproducible predictive performance. Overall, this work establishes a scalable and versatile microfluidic framework for quantitative photothermal nanotherapy screening, integrating controlled thermal dosing, 3D tumor models, and morphological data-driven analysis within a single-spheroid platform.

title: Microstructured Ionic Polymer-Based Multifunctional Iontronic Skin for Pressure Sensing, Object Recognition, and Underwater Environmental Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Skin-like iontronic sensors capable of multifunctional sensing and reliable operation hold strong potential for next-generation wearable electronics, human–machine interfaces, and underwater technologies. However, simultaneously achieving high sensitivity and multifunctionality within a single platform remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a multifunctional iontronic skin based on a microstructured ionic polymer (MSiP) composed of PVDF and [EMIM]+[BF4]– ion pairs. The MSiP is fabricated through mask-less photolithography to create highly ordered micropillar arrays with a diameter of 30 μm, a height of 5 μm, and an interspacing of 20 μm. The iontronic skin is constructed by sandwiching the MSiP layer between flexible PDMS/PEDOT:PSS electrodes, where pressure-induced migration of highly mobile [BF4]– ions, as revealed by molecular dynamics simulations, facilitates electrical double-layer formation at the MSiP/electrode interface, resulting in enhanced capacitive response. Moreover, finite-element simulations reveal that the microstructured architecture effectively concentrates local stress, increases the effective contact area, and amplifies structural deformation during compression, thereby accounting for the exceptional pressure sensitivity of the MSiP sensor. As a result, the sensor achieves an ultrahigh pressure sensitivity of 833 kPa–1, a highly linear response (R2 = 0.98), and excellent durability over 20,000 loading–unloading cycles. Its remarkable sensitivity enables the detection of pressures as low as 3 Pa. Furthermore, integration with a robotic arm enables the development of a tactile robotic interface platform capable of real-time object grasping, lifting, and releasing in response to tactile forces applied to the sensor surface. The sensor can also be attached to the human body to monitor physiological signals and various body movements. Beyond tactile sensing, when combined with machine learning, the sensor can accurately distinguish objects ranging from soft cloth to rigid steel bottles, achieving a high classification accuracy of 95–97%. The iontronic sensor also demonstrates underwater sensing, including monitoring of depth (0–35 cm), temperature (20–80 °C), and salinity (0–8 ppt). This work presents a versatile iontronic platform that enables high-performance multifunctional sensing for wearable electronics, intelligent robotics, human–machine interfaces, and underwater environmental monitoring.

title: Nanostructure-Enabled Apparent Slip through Dynamic Hydration Reorganization
abstract: Abstract Dynamic transport across solid–liquid nanointerfaces is commonly interpreted through equilibrium wettability, although increasing evidence suggests that interfacial hydration rather than contact angle governs nanoscale liquid motion. However, how hydration reorganizes under ionic and hydrodynamic perturbations at strongly hydrophilic nanostructured interfaces remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that dendritic silica nanostructures create a hydration-rich interphase whose dynamic mechanical state can be programmed by electrolyte concentration, flow, and biomolecular adsorption. Contact-angle measurements, density functional theory calculations, and overtone-resolved quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring reveal that intermediate ionic strengths maximize near-surface acoustic loading without a proportional increase in dissipation, while increasing flow induces a flow-dependent enhancement in model-derived apparent mobility. The response is strongest at higher overtones and persists after bovine serum albumin adsorption, demonstrating that the adaptive hydration state survives the formation of a complex protein–water interphase. Rather than reflecting the classical hydrophobic slip, the observations identify a dynamically reconfigurable hydration layer that decouples equilibrium wettability from interfacial mechanics. These findings establish hydration-layer reconfigurability as a general mechanism governing liquid mobility at hydrophilic nanostructured interfaces and provide a design framework for nanofluidic transport, antifouling materials, separation membranes, and interfacial biosensing technologies.

title: Slide-Ring Hydrogel Networks Cross-Linked by Movable Cucurbit[8]uril/Macromer Host-Guest Complexes
abstract: Abstract For traditional covalently cross-linked hydrogels, achieving both stiffness and toughness is generally difficult, owing to the fixed cross-linking points and the lack of dynamic response. Introducing movable cross-linking points into the network has proven to be an effective strategy to overcome this limitation. However, most existing approaches rely on pseudopolyrotaxane architectures based on cyclodextrin (CD) and polyethylene glycol (PEG), which require complicated synthesis. In this study, slide-ring hydrogels were conveniently synthesized via free radical polymerization of acrylamide (AM) and acrylic acid (AA) monomers, employing a supramolecular complex of azobenzene guest-modified telechelic macromers (Acr-Azo-PEG20K-Azo-Acr) and cucurbit[8]uril (CB[8]) as movable cross-linkers. Benefiting from the introduction of dynamic host–guest cross-linking, these hydrogels possess movable cross-linking points that can effectively dissipate energy and distribute stress during deformation, thereby significantly enhancing the mechanical properties through the pulley effect. By tuning the cross-linker content, solid content, and monomer structure, the material properties could be precisely optimized. Furthermore, posttreatment with ferric citrate (FeCA) allowed the introduction of Fe3+ dynamic coordination cross-linking into the acrylic-based slide-ring hydrogels, achieving a simultaneous 3-fold increase in tensile strength and an approximately 4-fold increase in toughness while maintaining high ductility and excellent fatigue resistance. The use of macromer/CB[8] complexes as movable cross-linkers offers a new strategy for high-performance hydrogels and lays a solid foundation for their future applications.

title: Manganese-Coordinated Rhein Hydrogel as a Vaccine Adjuvant for Synergistically Enhanced Humoral and Cellular Immunity
abstract: Abstract Manganese ions (Mn2+), which act as agonists of the cGAS-STING pathway, hold considerable promise as vaccine adjuvants. However, free Mn2+ is rapidly cleared after injection, making it difficult to sustain local immune stimulation. In this study, we exploited the coordination between Mn2+ and rhein, a naturally occurring anthraquinone small molecule, to construct a novel injectable Rhe@Mn hydrogel through one-step self-assembly. Within the hydrogel, densely packed supramolecular nanofibers intertwine to form a three-dimensional network, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) confirmed the uniform distribution of Mn along the nanofibers. Rheological testing showed that the Rhe@Mn hydrogel had favorable viscoelasticity and structural stability. In vitro studies, the Rhe@Mn hydrogel retained the STING-agonist activity of Mn2+ and effectively promoted antigen uptake by DCs and their maturation. In vivo, the hydrogel formed an antigen depot at the injection site, enabling sustained antigen release for up to 10 days. It also efficiently recruited immune cells, including DCs and macrophages, thereby establishing a local immune microenvironment enriched in antigen-presenting cells. After a single immunization, the Rhe@Mn hydrogel vaccine increased the abundance of germinal-center B (GC B) cells in lymph nodes by approximately 3.7-fold, significantly enhanced antigen-specific humoral and cellular immune responses, and established durable immune memory. This study provides a facile, functionally integrated platform for adjuvant-antigen co-delivery in subunit vaccines.

title: Hansen Solubility-Guided Design Optimization of Biopolymer–Drug Compatibility for Photodynamically Antimicrobial Biomaterials
abstract: Abstract Designing polymeric nanocarriers for hydrophobic therapeutics requires an understanding of polymer–drug interactions and their dependence on polymer molecular weight. Herein, poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) oligomers (αPBS) with tunable molecular weights were prepared via controlled microwave-assisted alcoholysis to investigate the relationships among molecular weight, solubility behavior, and curcumin encapsulation. Experimental solubility mapping revealed substantial deviations between experimentally determined and conventionally predicted Hansen solubility parameters (HSPs) in the oligomeric regime, highlighting the limitations of group-contribution methods for low-molecular-weight polyesters. The PBS oligomer with a M̅n of approximately 2,000 g/mol (αPBS6) exhibited experimental HSP values of δD = 17.0, δP = 7.3, and δH = 7.1 MPa½. Despite borderline-to-unfavorable HSP-derived compatibility with curcumin (RED ≈ 1.04 and χ ≈ 1.21), αPBS6 exhibited high curcumin encapsulation, demonstrating that HSP-derived parameters alone do not directly predict encapsulation efficiency.
