Curcumin-loaded αPBS nanoparticles (Cur@PBS6) had an average diameter of 232 ± 1.5 nm, a high loading capacity (8.54–9.10%), and good colloidal stability. Their loading capacity exceeded those of commercial PBS (6.36%), PBSA (6.64%), and PLA (2.75%) systems, indicating that molecular-weight modification and nanoparticle formation conditions contribute to curcumin incorporation. Spectroscopic analyses suggested reduced curcumin aggregation following encapsulation, which preserved its photoactivity and promoted reactive oxygen species generation under blue-light irradiation. Moreover, Cur@PBS6-incorporated electrospun poly(lactic acid) fibers exhibited photodynamic antibacterial activity under blue-light irradiation (450 nm, 0.3 W/cm2, 60 min), achieving bacterial killing efficiencies of 94.2% against Escherichia coli and 98.1% against Staphylococcus aureus. These findings demonstrate that experimentally determined HSPs provide a complementary framework for evaluating molecular-weight-dependent polymer–drug interactions, while nanocarrier performance is collectively governed by molecular weight, crystallinity, formulation condition, and other physicochemical factors.

title: Cross-Dimensional Percolation and Metastructure-Assisted Highly Efficient Electromagnetic Interference Shielding Films
abstract: Abstract Increasing electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues make shielding materials urgent in need. However, designing a thin/lightweight material with high shielding effectiveness (SE over 100 dB) by facile and scalable technologies with high production accuracy is still challenging. Herein, excellent shielding composite films are successfully prepared through sequential scalable positive pressure filtration, accurate inkjet printing, and facile transferring. From mass ratio optimization of 1D silver nanowires to 2D MXene, a skeleton with maximum inner free space and fast electron and phonon transport channels through cross-dimensional percolation is produced for internal multiple reflection absorption. To further increase EMI SE, graphene-based mesh metamaterials are theoretically calculated and accurately printed with controlled conductivity for impedance matching as the top layer. Facile inkjet printing succeeds in balancing print accuracy and conductivity control by advanced ink formulation. Finally, under multiple attenuation mechanisms verified through complex permittivity analysis in both frequency domain and real space (conductive loss, dipole polarization, and various interfacial polarizations), EMI SE of 102.31 dB in X-band is achieved. Integrating different attenuation technologies in a single material system of multidimensions inspires further designing shielding materials with increasingly strict requirements like multiband compatibility with special frequency enhancement.

title: Amino-Terminated Ti3C2T x MXene Prepared via Ammonia Treatment Boosts Efficiency and Stability of Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract Defect-mediated non-radiative recombination and progressive material degradation impose fundamental limits on the power conversion efficiency (PCE) and operational durability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). To address this issue, we synthesized amino-terminated Ti3C2Tx MXene (denoted as A-MXene) nanosheets through LiF/HCl etching and subsequent ammonia post-treatment and incorporated them into PSCs. Characterization results reveal that ammonia treatment modifies the surface/interlayer chemistry of Ti3C2Tx and introduces amino-related nitrogen species, accompanied by increased interlayer spacing, reduced lateral flake dimensions, and enhanced dispersibility. In PSCs, A-MXene regulates both Pb- and I-related chemical environments, improves perovskite crystallization, suppresses non-radiative recombination, and promotes interfacial hole extraction. Consequently, the A-MXene-modified device delivers a PCE of 23.49%. Moreover, the encapsulated device retains 94.9% of its initial PCE after 720 h of uninterrupted 1-sun illumination at 85 °C in a N2 atmosphere. These findings establish ammonia-treated MXene as a versatile additive capable of concurrently governing defect chemistry and charge transport, thereby enabling high-efficiency, stable PSCs.

title: A High-Brightness, Low-Energy-Spread Au Needle Point Electron Source Nanocold-Cathode Adapted to Low-Power Photoelectric Coexcitation
abstract: Abstract To address the requirements of vacuum electronic and optoelectronic device applications for next-generation low-power-consumption, high-brightness, low-energy-spread, and tunable electron sources, the pursuit of high-efficiency metal nanocold-cathodes with plasmon-enhanced properties in specific waveband emerges as one of potent solutions. In this study, by screening and comparing the cathode materials and structures, we propose a high-brightness, low-energy-spread Au needle nanocold-cathode point electron source adapted to low-intensity photoelectric coexcitation. The experimental results demonstrate sensitivity to excitation light and outstanding electron emission performance of this point electron source: under the coexcitation of an electrostatic field below ∼1.25 V μm–1 and a supercontinuum-spectrum laser with average intensity of ∼24 W cm–2, the source achieved an emission current of 130 nA, improving by one order of magnitude when compared to the field emission current (∼13 nA) under pure electrostatic field excitation. As the laser excitation intensity increased, its effective work function decreased from 5.1 to 2.7 eV, resulting in a significant reduction of the excitation threshold for electron emission. Benefiting from the plasmon-enhanced light-harvesting effect, the cathode exhibits high sensitivity and selectivity to the wavelength and polarization of the incident light. In the 532–675 nm plasmon resonance band, the emission current exceeds 225 nA at an average excitation intensity of only 7.05 W cm–2, ∼17 times the pure electrostatic field emission current. Meanwhile, the plasmon relaxation preferentially populates high-energy electrons and suppresses the energy spread broadening induced by the space charge effect, thereby achieving a high reduced brightness of 6.89 × 109 A m–2 sr–1 V–1 and a low-energy spread of approximately 0.5 eV. This low-power photoelectric coexcitation scheme greatly relaxes the requirements on the excitation source, providing a route for the miniaturization and integration of vacuum optoelectronic point electron sources.

title: Toward Robust InP Laser Lift-Off: Energy-Dependent Absorption Shift and Self-Absorption under Single-Pulse 1064 nm Irradiation
abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous integration of InP on silicon is essential for the next generation of electronic systems by enabling high-performance photonics and radio frequency devices. Near-infrared Laser Lift-Off (LLO) is a promising route to enable the cost-effective transfer of InP-based device layers onto Si platforms. However, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. To clarify these laser-material interactions, we investigate an InP/InGaAs heterostructure under single-pulse 1064 nm irradiation. Through microstructural characterization and coupled optical-thermal simulations, we reveal that the LLO process deviates fundamentally from the conventional sacrificial layer decomposition model. Instead, we identify an energy-dependent transition driven by highly localized transient melting and dynamic optical property changes. At moderate energies, rapid atomic intermixing and phosphorus depletion occur within a short-lived liquid phase, followed by epitaxial recrystallization that preserves macroscopic structural integrity. At higher energies, thermally induced bandgap shrinkage in the nominally transparent InP strongly enhances direct 1064 nm absorption. This initiates a positive feedback loop of thermal runaway, shifting the dominant energy absorption from the InGaAs sacrificial layer toward the InP layer and causing catastrophic ablation. These findings suggest that the onset of InP self-absorption imposes a critical high-energy constraint on the LLO process, rather than the sacrificial-layer decomposition threshold alone, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding and optimizing InP layer transfer.

title: Growth Kinetics of Gallium Selenide on Graphene: Bridging Atomistic and Mesoscale Processes
abstract: Abstract Achieving uniform, wafer-scale thin layers and heterostructures remains a major challenge in the synthesis of two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors, which requires precise control of growth parameters and atomic-level insight into surface interactions. We combine density functional theory (DFT) and kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulations to investigate the early stages of 2D gallium selenide (GaSe) growth on graphene and determine how GaSe domain morphology, growth rate, and nucleation density depend on the atomic fluxes and substrate temperature. The presence of Ga on the substrate is key to promoting GaSe nucleation, while a sufficiently high Se flux is required to enable 2D GaSe growth and suppress accumulation of Ga clusters. The DFT-informed KMC simulations also reveal a trade-off between the growth rate and morphology, showing that increasing the flux of Ga relative to Se promotes faster growth of GaSe and increases the surface roughness. In contrast, high substrate temperatures promote edge healing and favor the formation of compact triangular domains. These results identify a narrow window of experimental conditions for 2D GaSe growth on graphene.

title: Type-III Porous Liquid ZIF-8/Perfluorodecalin for O2 Delivery and CO2 Removal: Stability, Sorption, and Transport Monitored by In Situ EPR Spectroscopy
abstract: Abstract Perfluorodecalin (C10F18) is a well-known gas carrier for chemical and biomedical applications. Being an inert and stable liquid, it is capable of dissolving and releasing large volumes of O2 and CO2. In this work, we propose a route for enhancing its functional properties furthermore by designing a type-III porous liquid (PL) composed of C10F18 and metal–organic framework ZIF-8. Using spin probes encapsulated in ZIF-8, we employ in situ electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy to investigate the stability of this PL and the adsorption, transport, and desorption of O2 and CO2 in practical conditions. The prototypical flow system with EPR detection was designed to demonstrate the controllable sorption cycles of ZIF-8/C10F18 PL. The exceptional stability and appealing functional properties of this PL pave the way for its future chemical and biomedical applications.

title: Biodegradable Starch/Gelatin/PAM Hydrogel Electrolyte for Wide-Temperature Flexible Zinc-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract The booming development of flexible wearable electronics requires safe, deformable, and sustainable aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Liquid electrolytes suffer leakage, zinc corrosion, and dendrite growth, while the recently reported hydrogel electrolytes fail to balance biodegradability and mechanical stretchability. Herein, we developed a fully biodegradable biomass dual-network hydrogel electrolyte fabricated via free-radical copolymerization of starch, gelatin, and acrylamide (AM) with ZnSO4 salts. Benefiting from abundant hydrogen-bond networks formed by renewable biomass skeletons, the tailored hydrogel effectively immobilizes free water to construct a water-poor interfacial microenvironment, simultaneously suppressing dendrite proliferation and electrolyte leakage. The hydrogel delivers an outstanding low-temperature tolerance and favorable ionic conductivity of 23.76 mS cm–1 (–20 °C) and contributes to accelerating redox reaction kinetics and improving the reversibility of the Zn plating/stripping process. Therefore, the assembled Zn||sodium vanadate battery delivers a high capacity of 350 mAh g–1 at 1.0 A g–1 with 100% Coulombic efficiency and 83% capacity retention over 700 cycles. Impressively, within a broad temperature window of 0–55 °C, the pouch cell could work under repeated bending states, and the hydrogel is fundamentally degraded within 20 days in natural soil. It provides a facile strategy for flexible and sustainable AZIBs with high performance.

title: Synergistic Effects of Thermally Engineered Defect-Rich Structures in Renewable Nanocarbons for Enhanced Electrochemical Performance
abstract: Abstract The electrochemical performance of conventional hard carbons remains constrained by their limited surface activity and insufficient interlayer spacing for efficient sodium storage. Here, we report a microstructurally engineered carbon derived from waste passenger tyres, exhibiting tunable defect density, interlayer spacing, and pore distribution through controlled carbonization between 700 and 1500 °C. The thermally driven reconstruction of sp2/sp3 domains induces a hierarchical framework featuring short-range ordered graphene nanodomains embedded within disordered carbon matrices, generating abundant closed and open pores that synergistically facilitate ion transport and adsorption. The optimized carbon produced at 1300 °C delivers a first-cycle reversible capacity of approximately 282.1 mAhg–1, retains approximately 278.5 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles at 10 mA g–1, and exhibits sustained high-current cycling stability over 500 cycles. Detailed micromechanistic analysis reveals that the enhanced sodium storage originates from the coupling of enlarged interlayer spacing (≈0.38–0.40 nm) and optimized Raman-active disorder with the internal pore architecture, enabling coexisting diffusion-controlled intercalation and surface-induced capacitive processes. This work establishes a framework for defect-controlled microstructural engineering of tyre-derived carbons, providing mechanistic insight into the pore–defect–graphite interplay and offering a sustainable pathway for converting end-of-life rubber waste into high-performance anode materials for next-generation sodium-ion batteries.

title: Bubble-Guided Self-Healing Superhydrophobic Surfaces with Dual-Mode In Situ Visual Monitoring
abstract: Abstract Superhydrophobic surfaces exhibit great application potential ranging from sophisticated droplet manipulation to aerospace and other fields, owing to their unique properties such as liquid repellent, anti-corrosion, anti-icing, drag reduction, and so on. However, maintaining the stability of the solid–liquid interface remains a major challenge: the instability of the three-phase line caused by the collapse of the air layer during dynamic transport and the degradation of surface function caused by the retention of micro–nano contaminants seriously undermine its durability. In nature, rice leaves possess oriented microgroove architectures for unidirectional droplet transport, while submerged photosynthetic plants continuously generate bubbles to sustain intact solid–air–liquid (SAL) composite layers. Inspired by these merits, we propose a directional confinement–transport strategy, in which the microcolumn structure achieves dynamic compensation of the interfacial air layer through precise submillimeter bubble manipulation and establishes a cooperative stabilization of “structural confinement–air self-replenishment”. The surface demonstrates exceptional self-cleaning and no loss transport behaviors, vastly expanding its applicability in extreme environments. In addition, we construct a monitoring system based on interfacial chemical reactions, which enables in situ visual monitoring of the surface wetting state and can restore its superhydrophobicity on demand. In essence, this approach not only benefits the development of the superhydrophobic field, but also provides valuable theoretical foundations and practical guidance for constructing multifunctional stable interfaces, thereby propelling the field toward practical applications.

title: A Geometrically Tunable Cardiovascular Shunt for the Individualized Care of Neonates with Congenital Heart Defects
abstract: Abstract Congenital heart defects (CHDs), particularly single-ventricle anomalies such as hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), require early surgical intervention using fixed-diameter vascular shunts. However, current shunts are incapable of adapting to the physiological changes of infant growth, often leading to hemodynamic imbalance and elevated mortality risk. Here, we report a geometrically tunable cardiovascular shunt lined with a photoresponsive hydrogel based on methacrylated dextran (DexMA) and dithiothreitol (DTT). This dual-stage crosslinked hydrogel system enables minimally invasive modulation of the inner lumen diameter in response to external blue light. We optimized the hydrogel composition to achieve both mechanical robustness (Young’s modulus ≈ 8.5 kPa) and light-induced deswelling, allowing for lumen expansion up to 39% with high stability over one month. In vitro studies confirmed excellent cytocompatibility, hemocompatibility, and minimal immune activation. Prototype annular shunts demonstrated precise, programmable diameter increases (15–18%) corresponding to computational models of infant growth. This dynamic, photoresponsive platform is a critical advance toward implantable materials for personalized cardiovascular interventions and a significant step toward growth-accommodating pediatric medical devices.

title: RES NPs/GelMA Sustained-Release Cryogel Modulates Macrophage Arachidonic Acid Metabolism and Angiogenic Microenvironment Promoting Diabetic Wound Healing
abstract: Abstract Refractory chronic diabetic wounds severely impair quality of life. Their delayed healing is mainly driven by impaired angiogenesis and persistent inflammation caused by infection and excessive ROS. Resveratrol (RES) has anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic effects, but its clinical use is limited by poor solubility and low bioavailability. Here, we developed a dual-mechanism sustained-release system for RES to promote diabetic wound healing. RES was converted into nanoparticles (RES NPs) to improve cellular uptake and bioavailability, then encapsulated in GelMA cryogel microspheres (CMS) for injectable, sustained release. This system downregulated NF-κB signaling, reduced ROS, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines and COX2, thereby inhibiting arachidonic acid metabolism and promoting macrophage polarization from M1 to M2. Meanwhile, AMPK activation restored endothelial cell function, enhanced angiogenesis, and supported new vessel formation. Overall, this strategy accelerated high-quality wound repair in diabetic conditions.

title: Anharmonic Shear Vibration of Electrostatic Layers Leads to Low Thermal Conductivity in Bi2O2Se
abstract: Abstract Bi2O2Se is among the best n-type oxide thermoelectric materials with low lattice thermal conductivity and shows a robust ferroelectric state at room temperature in reduced dimensions. Herein, we have combined experimental and theoretical studies to comprehend this elusive congruence of low lattice thermal conductivity (κlat) and an incipient ferroelectric state. We have experimentally measured the κlat of Bi2O2Se in the 10–300 K temperature range, which showed that temperature–dependent κlat deviates from the usual T–1 dependence. Density functional theory-based calculation of phonon dispersion reveals that the low κlat in Bi2O2Se primarily originates from the anharmonic lattice vibration and the presence of low-frequency optical phonons, which strongly interact with the longitudinal acoustic phonons and suppress their dispersion along Γ-A and Γ-X directions in the Brillouin zone. Our study reveals that the lowest frequency optical phonons at ∼25.7 and ∼66.5 cm–1 involve a shear interlayer vibration that can promote distortion in the Bi–O bond length and displacement of Se atoms. We propose that these vibrational modes can dynamically break the centrosymmetric configuration in the reduced dimension, leading to the experimentally observed ferroelectricity in ultrathin nanosheets or flakes of Bi2O2Se as reported in the literature. We have corroborated the presence of these low-frequency phonons using low-temperature heat capacity measurement and temperature–dependent Raman spectroscopy.

title: Preconstructed Electrolyte Interphase Enables Stable Commercial V2O5 Cathodes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) show great potential for large-scale energy storage on account of their exceptional safety, low cost, and environmental friendliness. As a representative cathode for AZIBs, commercial vanadium pentoxide (c-V2O5) still suffers from critical bottlenecks including severe vanadium dissolution, sluggish Zn2+ diffusion, and intensive interfacial side reactions in aqueous electrolytes. Herein, a novel electrochemical pretreatment strategy is developed to in-situ construct a uniform, compact ∼3 nm amorphous electrolyte interfacial layer (EIL) with an organic–inorganic composite structure on the surface of c-V2O5 in an organic lithium-ion battery system, which breaks through the limitations of unstable and inhomogeneous interfacial layers formed in conventional aqueous systems. The EIL exerts multifunctional effects by suppressing vanadium dissolution, accelerating ion diffusion, and inhibiting side reactions, endowing the modified electrode with a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 98.3%, outstanding cycling stability (180 mAh g–1 after 5000 cycles at a current density of 1 A g–1), and enhanced rate capability. This work could provide guidance for optimizing cathode materials of AZIBs through rational electrolyte interface engineering in the future.

title: Tailoring Viscoelasticity by Carbon Filler Dimensionality toward High-Impact-Resistant Polydiborosiloxane Composites
abstract: Abstract The development of lightweight and flexible materials with high-impact-resistant performance remains a critical challenge under dynamic loading conditions, including precision instruments, electronics, and military defense systems. Herein, carbon fillers with distinct dimensionality are incorporated into polydiborosiloxane (PDBS) to construct composites with tunable viscoelastic behavior and excellent impact resistance. Increasing filler dimensionality not only retains the specific shear-stiffening viscoelastic behavior of PDBS but also significantly enhances the energy-dissipation capability and impact-resistant performance of the composites. Notably, the composite with large-size graphene achieves a high impact-force attenuation rate of 92.2% under low strain-rate impact while maintaining a strength of 48.8 MPa and a toughness of 24.2 MJ/m3 under high strain-rate impact. This work highlights the critical role of filler dimensionality in tailoring the viscoelasticity toward high-impact-resistant composite materials, thereby offering potential for efficient protection under dynamic loading conditions.

title: Defect and Ion-Migration Regulation in MAPbI3 Memristors via ZIF-67 Modification toward Stable Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Computing
abstract: Abstract High-performance resistive random-access memory (RRAM) based on organic–inorganic hybrid perovskites remains limited by intrinsic vacancy defects and uncontrolled ion migration, which usually induce random conductive filaments (CFs) formation and poor device stability. Herein, a defect-engineering strategy is proposed by using a cobalt-based zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF-67) as a multifunctional additive to synergistically regulate the MAPbI3 film through Co ion incorporation and ligand-assisted defect passivation. Structural, morphological, optical/electrical, and conduction analyses reveal that the introduction of ZIF-67 improves film quality by enlarging grains and reducing grain boundaries, while regulating Pb-vacancy-related defect states and introducing a stronger Co–I bond. These effects suppress disordered vacancy migration and promote stable CFs formation during resistive switching (RS). Consequently, the Cu/ZIF67-MAPbI3/p-Si device exhibits enhanced RS performance, including a high resistance ratio (>103), low operating power consumption (≈1.01 mW), endurance over 2300 cycles, and improved switching uniformity with reduced coefficients of variation for both high-resistance state and low-resistance state. Benefiting from its continuously tunable conductance, the device successfully emulates synaptic plasticity behaviors, including paired-pulse facilitation (PPF), spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), and long-term potentiation/depression (LTP/LTD). Moreover, an experimentally calibrated multilayer perceptron achieves Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST) handwritten digit recognition with an accuracy of 97.54% and a last loss of 3.35%, demonstrating the potential of ZIF67-MAPbI3-based RRAM device for artificial synapses and neuromorphic computing.

title: Mechanoimmuno‐Engineered Dendritic Cell Membrane Nanodiscs Presenting Diverse Antigens for Potent Antibacterial Vaccination
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional antibacterial vaccines often fail to elicit robust immunity against multifaceted virulence factors, including bacterial surface antigens and secreted toxins, particularly lacking the strong T‐cell responses essential for effective infection prevention. To overcome this limitation, we engineered dendritic cell (DC) membrane‐derived nanodiscs (aDCNDs) with stiffness‐tuned topology as a mechanoimmunological antibacterial nanovaccine. aDCNDs uniquely co‐present multi‐antigens from bacterial membranes and secreted toxins alongside upregulated immune‐stimulatory molecules, eliciting potent adaptive immunity that simultaneously targets Pseudomonas aeruginosa cells and neutralizes cytotoxic exotoxins for dual protection. Their precisely controlled sub‐50 nm size enables superior lymph node accumulation versus larger nanovesicles. Importantly, aDCNDs engage T cell mechanotransduction to promote TAZ nuclear translocation, augmenting T cell activation and the secretion of IFN‐γ, IL‐17A, and IL‐4, an effect not observed with conventional soft nanovesicles. The increased stiffness of aDCNDs represents an important and likely contributor to this mechano‐stimulatory effect. In lethal murine models of septicemia and pneumonia, aDCNDs vaccination achieved profound reductions in bacterial burdens (up to 99.99%) and markedly improved survival without systemic toxicity. This work establishes the aDCND platform as a safe and effective antibacterial strategy, highlighting mechano‐immunology as a critical design principle for next‐generation antibacterial vaccines.

title: Interfacial Hydrogen Spillover in Partially Alloyed PdNi Electrocatalysts for Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen spillover can decouple elementary steps in the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet conventional bimetallic catalysts often suffer from discontinuous interfaces that block spillover pathways. Herein, an interfacial hydrogen spillover mechanism is engineered in a Pd–PdNi–Ni catalyst via a partial interface alloying strategy for pH‐universal hydrogen evolution. The graded PdNi interface serves as a recombination sink integrating two synergistic pathways: primary spillover, in which strongly adsorbed H* generated on Ni spontaneously migrates across the interface, and secondary spillover, in which H* produced on Pd also diffuses to the same interfacial sites. The dual spillover is driven by a favorable hydrogen intermediate gradient resulting from Ni‐to‐Pd electron transfer and an optimized d‐band center. The optimal catalyst delivers ultralow overpotentials of 60 mV (alkaline) and 37 mV (acidic) at 10 mA cm −2 , with robust durability, and the corresponding anion exchange membrane electrolyzer exhibits 1.73 V at 0.5 A cm −2 and 452 h stability in simulated seawater. Operando Raman spectroscopy detects Pd–H and Ni–H vibrations, providing direct evidence for hydrogen migration from both domains to the interface, and theoretical calculations confirm the electronic origin and spillover pathways. This work demonstrates a rational design for high‐performance HER catalysts by harnessing dual hydrogen spillover.

title: Magnetic Resonance Reveals Radical Stability in Native Biofilms and Its Role in Bacterial Resistance
abstract: ABSTRACT Bacterial cells embedded in biofilms exhibit enhanced antimicrobial resistance compared with planktonic cells, contributing to persistent infections and failure of conventional antibiotic treatments. This resistance is influenced by the extracellular matrix (ECM), a heterogeneous network of polysaccharides, proteins, and lipids surrounding embedded cells. However, how the ECM regulates the accessibility of redox‐active small molecules remains poorly understood. Here, we combine electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), solid‐state NMR (ssNMR), and dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) ssNMR to determine how native Pseudomonas fluorescens Pf0‐1 colony biofilms differentially reduce nitroxide radicals across morphologies. EPR reveals that radical reduction depends on biofilm morphology, hydration, and ECM composition. Wild‐type biofilms exhibit slower nitroxide reduction than planktonic cells, while isolated ECM and dehydrated biofilms show negligible reduction, highlighting the importance of cellular accessibility. ssNMR identifies preferential spatial proximity of nitroxides to ECM polysaccharides and lipids, while DNP ssNMR reveals increasing polysaccharide content across biofilm morphologies that correlates with slower reduction kinetics. These findings support a model of protection in which the ECM provides the barrier to nitroxide access, and cellular reduction is the final step. Our integrated magnetic resonance approach provides molecular insight into how biofilm composition and structure determine the fate of therapeutically relevant redox‐active small molecules.

title: Fluxional Monomers Remodel Crystallinity at Low Loadings in Diketopyrrolopyrrole Co‐Thienothiophene Conjugated Polymers
abstract: ABSTRACT Conjugated polymers (CPs) are a class of semiconducting materials in which electrical conductivity and mechanical extensibility can coincide. Despite advances in synthesis and processing, these key properties are typically negatively correlated and derive from the semicrystalline microstructure of the polymer film. Here, we introduce a new strategy to improve the microstructure and mechanical properties of CPs through the introduction of bullvalene‐based fluxional comonomers, in which bonds rearrange constantly at ambient temperatures. By comparing bullvalene‐containing poly(diketopyrrolopyrrole‐thienothiophene) (p(DPP‐TT)) with static controls, we show that fluxional backbones resist thermal annealing induced crystallization, creating smaller crystallites even at low comonomer loadings (5 mol%). While comonomers produce minimal mechanical differences in low‐molecular weight CPs, when the network is reinforced through crosslinking, bullvalene strongly enhances stretchability, yielding a crack onset strain more than twice that of the controls. Additional experiments indicate that crosslinking enables the network to realign micro crystallites under stress to delay crack onset, but only when large crystallites are absent, as in fluxional CPs. Despite the incorporation of non‐conjugated comonomers, electrical mobility remains similar to controls at all levels of strain. This work demonstrates that fluxional components can outperform static analogues as structural modifiers in diketopyrrolopyrrole co‐thienothiophene CPs, leading to significant macroscopic effects.

title: Extending the Stretchability Limit of Elastomers Through Mechanical Bond Motion
abstract: ABSTRACT Elastomers with superior mechanical properties are imperative for next generation technologies spanning soft robotics, implantable bioelectronics, and adaptive aerospace systems. However, in conventional chemically crosslinked elastomers, increasing crosslinking density usually enhances modulus while reducing the attainable deformation before fracture, leading to a persistent stiffness–extensibility trade‐off. Here, we report polymer networks incorporating a single type of [2]rotaxane crosslinker that combines hidden length activation and stress redistribution through mechanical bond motion, enabling greater extensibility at comparable stiffness. Increasing the rotaxane crosslinker content raises Young's modulus from 0.08 to 1.83 MPa while decreasing fracture strain from 10.24 to 2.70. The resulting networks exhibit an empirical stiffness–extensibility relationship of , compared with the classical scaling . This relationship corresponds to a smaller proportional loss of extensibility for the same proportional increase in modulus. The fracture energy reaches 5.57 kJ/m 2 , compared with 1.01 kJ/m 2 for control networks, demonstrating enhanced fracture resistance. Similar stretchability enhancements are observed in networks prepared from other acrylate monomers, supporting the applicability of this design across different acrylate matrices. This work provides a molecular strategy for designing stiff, stretchable, and damage tolerant elastomers.

title: Proton‐Induced Perthionitrite‐Mediated Zinc Thiolate Persulfidation
abstract: ABSTRACT The perthionitrite anion, SSNO − , has been proposed as a S 0 source for persulfidation of biological thiol and thiolate compounds. Here, SSNO − reacts with an iminopyridine‐supported zinc thiolate complex to form a perthiolate‐supported zinc perthionitrite complex, acting as both a ligand to zinc and as a sulfur source for persulfidation of the thiolate moiety. A related zinc thionitrite complex was also prepared, enabling comparison of zinc thionitrite and zinc thiolate persulfidation. In these compounds, the zinc‐bound SNO − ligand is selectively persulfidated over the zinc‐bound thiolate moiety upon addition of S 8 , cleanly forming SSNO − rather than the perthiolate. This work therefore demonstrates that direct S 0 transfer from SSNO − to thiolate anions is thermodynamically unfavorable and must instead be mediated by preceding SSNO − decomposition.

title: Surfactant‐Mediated “ Oil‐in‐Water ” Electrolyte Design via Sonochemical Assembly: Low‐Dielectric Interfacial Regulation for Ultrastable Aqueous Zinc Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐metal batteries are plagued by severe performance degradation originating from the Zn anode's instability. Although electrolyte engineering has been widely established as a primary strategy to address this challenge, the utility of numerous promising species is intrinsically limited by their poor aqueous solubility. Herein, a surfactant‐mediated “ oil‐in‐water ” (denoted as SMOW) electrolyte design is proposed to unlock the potential of hydrophobic species. A long‐term stable micellar electrolyte is developed via sonochemically engineered self‐assembly, in which hydrophobic species are encapsulated within the surfactant micelles. Driven by interfacial electrostatic repulsion, these micelles release the hydrophobic species on the zinc anode surface. The enriched interfacial layer acts as an effective low‐dielectric shield, intrinsically accelerating Zn 2+ desolvation while physically isolating the Zn anode from reactive water molecules. Owing to the synergistic effect between the hydrophobic species and the surfactant, highly compact and dendrite‐free Zn deposition with suppressed parasitic side reactions is realized, enabling an ultralong cycling lifespan of over 3900 h for the Zn anode at 10 mA cm −2 . Furthermore, the assembled Zn||I 2 full cells deliver cycling for over 10000 cycles at 5 A g −1 with negligible capacity fading. This work provides a universal paradigm to break through the design constraints of aqueous electrolytes.

title: From Atoms to Reactors: A Critical Review of a Decade of Machine Learning in Heterogeneous Catalysis (2017–2026)
abstract: ABSTRACT This critical review traces the evolution of machine learning (ML) across the full value chain of heterogeneous catalysis over 2017–2026, from catalyst discovery to reactor and process design, and across the principal reaction families (CO 2 reduction, water splitting, nitrogen chemistry, zeolite‐catalyzed transformations). Each stage is evaluated against four criteria — data foundation, method maturity, experimental validation and deployment readiness — through a structured capability scorecard. Digitalization has advanced from the top of the length scale downward: prediction of adsorption energies and atomistic potential‐energy surfaces is now mature, with errors of tens of meV relative to the reference DFT calculations and accelerations of three orders of magnitude over DFT, yet experimentally validated catalyst improvements remain rare. The most significant advance is the closed‐loop autonomous laboratory coupling Bayesian optimization, automated synthesis and high‐throughput testing. Large language models have begun to add a reasoning and orchestration layer, while kinetics, reactor and process design remain the least digitalized stages. We argue that the field's next decade of impact will be decided not by more accurate atomic‐scale prediction but by carrying ML into experimental validation and the reactor‐and‐process scale, where catalysis is hardest to industrialize and where data‐driven methods are weakest.

title: Dual‐Electrode Catalytic Engineering for Sustainable C─C Bond Construction via Paired Electrochemical α‐Alkylation of Nitriles
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient paired electrochemical synthesis requires precise synchronization between anodic intermediate generation and cathodic consumption. However, uncontrolled adsorption and mismatched reaction kinetics often result in intermediate accumulation and competing side reactions. Here, we address this challenge through interfacial regulation of both anodic and cathodic catalysts, enabling a synchronized electrocatalytic platform for α‐alkylation of nitriles using alcohols as sustainable alkyl sources. An Fe‐doped NiO anode and Pb/C cathode are rationally integrated to regulate alcohol oxidation, carbon–carbon coupling, and selective C═C hydrogenation. Fe incorporation tailors the electronic structure and adsorption behavior of Ni sites, accelerating alcohol activation while mitigating nitrile‐induced inhibition, whereas Pb/C selectively promotes alkene hydrogenation without affecting nitrile functionalities. The optimized paired system achieves 91.68% yield and >99% conversion for 2,3‐diphenylpropionitrile at 20 mA cm −2 , enabling continuous and efficient synthesis across a broad range of aromatic and aliphatic alcohols with excellent functional‐group tolerance and robust operational stability. This work provides a general catalyst design principle for paired electrochemical synthesis by coordinating interfacial reaction kinetics and intermediate flux between two electrodes.

title: Disorder Beats Order: Carbon Microstructure Steers Radical Versus Cationic Pathways in Kolbe Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon electrodes are ubiquitous in organic electrochemistry, yet the structural origin of their selectivity in radical‐mediated reactions remains poorly understood. Here, we show that carbon microstructure is a primary determinant of product selectivity in Kolbe electrolysis, a prototypical electrochemical C─C coupling reaction central to fuel, fine chemical, and pharmaceutical production. We investigated eight carbon electrodes in two complementary libraries: five commercial carbons spanning diverse macroarchitectures, and carbon nanofibers with controlled graphitization. Both reveal a consistent structure–selectivity trend for various carboxylic acids and a mixed‐acid feed. Counterintuitively, the most disordered electrodes, despite the highest charge‐transfer resistance, give about an order of magnitude more Kolbe dimer than highly graphitized ones, which give little or none. Disordered, sp 3 ‐rich surfaces bearing oxygen functionalities strongly favor both Kolbe coupling (alkane) and Hofer–Moest products (alcohol/aldehyde), whereas graphitized, sp 2 ‐rich surfaces favor further oxidation to carbocations, yielding mainly alkenes and esters. Density functional theory calculations suggest that oxygen‐functionalized sites bind the alkyl radical about three times more strongly than pristine graphene, consistent with longer‐lived surface‐bound radicals that can couple. These findings help rationalize the widely used but poorly understood performance of reticulated vitreous carbon in organic electrosynthesis and offer guiding principles for rational carbon electrode design.

title: Suppressing Ostwald Ripening Enables Programmable Growth of Radially Hierarchical MOF Superstructures Toward Multichannel Optical Waveguiding
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐organic frameworks (MOF) homostructures or heterostructures with domain‐controlled emissive colors have demonstrated significant potential for high‐throughput sensing, anti‐counterfeiting, and information encryption. However, the precise construction of heterostructures with radially branched units remains challenging, primarily because the Ostwald ripening effect during crystal growth tends to drive one‐dimensional elongation. Here, we propose a programmable nucleation‐controlled strategy to spatially construct radially hierarchical MOF superstructures. During crystal growth, suppression of the Ostwald ripening effect triggers stable nucleation events in the system. Subsequently, the relatively high surface energy at the tips of 1D microrods promotes the secondary nucleation on the terminal facets, thereby leading to the formation of radially hierarchical superstructures. The acquired radial architectures with small angular deviations enable efficient multichannel optical signal output. The suppressing‐Ostwald‐ripening‐driven programmable growth paradigm provides a new route for the synthesis of multichannel waveguiding heterostructures and shows broad application prospects in advanced optoelectronic devices, multi‐channel information transmission, and encryption technologies.

title: Non‐Fluorinated Electrolytes Enable Long‐Cycling Micron‐Sized Silicon Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Microsized silicon (µm‐Si) anodes offer lower cost and higher tap density than their nanosized counterparts, however, their practical application remains challenging. A LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is widely considered essential for µm‐Si stable operation. However, potential environmental hazards of fluorides challenge the conventional use of lithium salts and additives for constructing LiF‐rich SEIs. Here, we present a non‐fluorinated electrolyte combining inorganic lithium salts (LiI/LiBr) with reduction‐resistant monoether solvents (tetrahydrofuran and hexyl methyl ether) forms a LiF‐free SEI that effectively addresses the rapid capacity fading of µm‐Si anodes. Unlike conventional mosaic‐structured SEI composed of oligomers and inorganic components (LiF and Li 2 O), our electrolyte forms high‐molecular‐weight polymers with binder‐like functionality at the silicon surface, preserving µm‐Si particle integrity and maintaining electrical connectivity even after pulverization. As a result, the µm‐Si electrode (D 50 = 4.65 µm) with an areal capacity of 3.15 mAh cm −2 achieves a Coulombic efficiency exceeding 99.95% and retains 92.12% of its initial capacity after 300 cycles at 0.3°C and 25°C. Furthermore, Li 3.75 Si||SPAN full cells achieve a capacity retention of over 79.43% after 150 cycles. This work provides an unconventional SEI design strategy for µm‐Si anodes.

title: Dynamic Supramolecular Probe With Chloride‐Guided Assembly and DNA‐Mediated Intracellular Reorganization for Tumor Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Subcellularly targeted molecules usually act through static localization, whereas systems that undergo environment‐triggered state transitions and functional reprogramming remain underexplored. Here, we develop alkyl‐chain‐tunable Ly‐Cn molecules whose intracellular behavior is governed by chloride‐dependent assembly and DNA‐mediated supramolecular reorganization. Responsiveness varies nonmonotonically with chain length, with Ly‐12 achieving an optimal balance. At physiologically relevant chloride concentrations, Ly‐12 undergoes a threshold‐like aggregation transition into supramolecular nanoparticles that are subsequently reorganized and disassembled by DNA. This dual‐responsive process drives initial accumulation in lysosome‐associated compartments, followed by lysosome‐to‐nucleus redistribution and DNA‐mediated nuclear trapping. Ly‐12 thereby acts beyond passive nuclear targeting: it initiates lysosomal perturbation that propagates into oxidative stress, endoplasmic‐reticulum stress, and DNA damage, while white‐light irradiation amplifies this cascade. Transcriptomic analysis corroborates the progressive stress response. In HeLa xenografts, intratumoral Ly‐12 produces marked antitumor efficacy that is further enhanced by white‐light irradiation, without evident systemic toxicity. These findings establish an environment‐responsive supramolecular strategy that converts ion‐regulated assembly and organelle redistribution into light‐amplified therapeutic activity.

title: Charge‐State‐Controlled Surface Modifiers for High‐Voltage and Stable Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT For wide‐bandgap mixed‐halide perovskites, quasi‐two‐dimensional (quasi‐2D) surface reconstruction using bulky‐cation spacers is widely employed to passivate surface defects and disrupt halide migration pathways. Nevertheless, under operational stress, conventional ammonium‐based spacers can undergo deprotonation, destabilizing the low‐dimensional surface layer and weakening its function. Herein, we report an organic‐spacer charge‐state control strategy for the surface modification of Cs 0.2 FA 0.8 PbI 1.8 Br 1.2 wide‐bandgap perovskites. This strategy involves combining octylammonium (OA) with N ‐methylsulfanilic acid (NMSA) to form NMSAO, a charge‐neutralized ammonium–sulfonate modifier state. This configuration induces an associated Ruddlesden–Popper‐like quasi‐2D phase at the perovskite surface that suppresses trap‐mediated recombination, facilitates interfacial charge extraction, and disrupts halide‐ion migration pathways. As a result, the NMSAO‐treated perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.83% and an open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 1.326 V, compared with 17.30% and 1.197 V for the untreated control PSCs. Furthermore, the NMSAO‐treated PSCs retain 93.59% of their initial PCE after 500 h of continuous illumination under ISOS‐L‐1 conditions and more than 93% after 500 h of thermal aging at 85°C. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of a charge‐neutralized organic spacer for quasi‐2D surface reconstruction in wide‐bandgap mixed‐halide PSCs, improving both photovoltaic performance and operational stability.

title: Operando Electro‐Rheology: Unraveling Decoupled Ion Transport‐Mechanical‐Morphological Properties in Nanostructured Block Copolymer Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Block copolymer electrolytes exhibit a complex interplay between self‐assembled morphology, ion transport, and mechanical properties under galvanostatic battery cycling. Here, we propose a novel operando methodology combining concurrent rheology and electrochemical measurements upon dc polarization for a lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI) doped polystyrene‐ block ‐poly (ethylene oxide) diblock copolymer electrolyte. Time‐resolved measurements of the viscoelastic and electrochemical responses to the galvanostatic stimulus permit to uncover the effective response of the block copolymer electrolyte, tracking ion transport‐mechanical‐morphological properties simultaneously. Corroborated by scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging, we observe the block copolymer transitioning from unperturbed, increasingly aligned lamellae to reorganized self‐assembled nanostructures as the applied current density approaches the limiting current and, beyond its onset, the nanomorphology evolves toward gyroid and hexagonal phases. The diffusion coefficients decrease as current density increases, which is attributed to concentration polarization phenomena. Lastly, this methodology identifies a direct coupling between interfacial electrochemical processes and mechanical properties, highlighting the intimate interplay between interfacial phenomena and rubbery plateau modulus upon current densities.

title: Atomically Dispersed Fe–Mo Catalytic Pairs Enable Two‐Electron Li 2 C 2 O 4 Pathway for Reversible Li–CO 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐carbon dioxide (Li–CO 2 ) batteries present a promising strategy for coupling high‐energy storage with CO 2 utilization, yet their development is impeded by sluggish kinetics and severe polarization associated with insulating discharge products. Achieving selective and reversible two‐electron conversion toward Li 2 C 2 O 4 remains a critical challenge for improving energy efficiency and cycling stability. Herein, we report electronically asymmetric dual‐atom Fe–N–Mo catalytic pairs anchored on a highly conjugated N‐doped carbon (NC) framework, forming Fe 1 ‐Mo 1 integrated catalytic pairs (Fe 1 ‐Mo 1 /ICPs) to promote a reversible two‐electron Li 2 C 2 O 4 conversion pathway. The πconjugated highly conjugated N‐doped carbon framework stabilizes atomically dispersed Fe and Mo sites while enhancing inter‐site electronic coupling. Within the proposed heteronuclear Fe–N–Mo configuration, intrinsic electronic asymmetry generates electrophilic Fe and nucleophilic Mo sites, enabling dynamic charge redistribution and complementary catalytic behavior. Such a donor‐acceptor bridge effectively regulates intermediate adsorption/desorption and suppresses competing reaction pathways, thereby favoring the selective and reversible formation of Li 2 C 2 O 4 . Operando spectroscopic analysis confirms the preferential reversible Li 2 C 2 O 4 evolution during cycle, while density functional theory calculations reveal substantially reduced energy barriers for key reaction intermediates. Benefiting from the unique electronic environment and synergistic effects of asymmetric dual‐atom sites, the FeMoCN catalyst delivers outstanding electrochemical performance.

title: Grain‐Boundary‐Facilitated Palladium Hydride Formation Enables Humidity‐Tolerant Catalytic Hydrogen Sensing
abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable hydrogen sensing under high absolute humidity remains a significant challenge owing to the competitive adsorption of water molecules on the sensing material surface. Here, we report a humidity‐tolerant catalytic H 2 sensor based on a grain‐boundary‐rich palladium nanostructure (Pd GB ) that operates without any external heating. The Pd GB sensor functions reliably at 22°C–80°C and 0%–90% relative humidity, achieving a lower limit of detection (LLOD) of 100 ppm even at 80°C and 90% relative humidity (261 g m −3 absolute humidity, corresponding to a > 3000‐fold higher molar concentration of water vapor relative to the LLOD of H 2 ), while satisfying ISO 26142 requirements for gas sensing. A machine‐learning regression model integrated into a sensor prototype enables robust, quantitative determination of H 2 concentration across a wide range of temperature and humidity conditions. Mechanistic investigations combining in situ XRD, temperature‐programmed desorption, molecular dynamics simulations, and density functional theory calculations reveal that the exceptional humidity tolerance originates from the Pd grain boundaries, which accelerate PdH x formation for weakening H 2 O adsorption and suppress humidity‐induced interference. These findings reveal a previously unexplored synergistic mechanism and establish a general materials‐design strategy for next‐generation humidity‐tolerant catalytic gas sensors.

title: Harnessing Rare Earth Elements in Proteins and Functional Materials for Advanced Optical, Magnetic, and Mechanical Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Rare earth‐proteins and their functional materials integrate unique physical properties of rare earth ions (RE 3+ ) with structural programmability of proteins, attracting increasing attention in a wide range of applications. Coordination with RE 3+ can enhance the rigidity and stability of certain proteins, even induce secondary structure transitions, and confer distinct physical properties onto functional materials. The programmability of amino acid sequences regulates coordination chemistry between proteins and RE 3+ , enabling the modulation of their optical and magnetic properties. Moreover, RE 3+ incorporation turns protein structures and aggregation state, leading to enhanced mechanical properties and adhesion strength. However, the development of such materials still faces significant challenges due to lack of molecular mechanism analysis and systematic rational design strategies. This review highlights the chemical structural analysis, rational design and synthesis strategies of rare earth‐protein and their functional materials. In addition, their applications in optics, magnetics, and mechanics are summarized. Finally, their current challenges and future perspectives are discussed.

title: Beyond State of Charge: Electrochemical States and Trajectory Design in Organic Mixed Conductors
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) couple electronic redox, ion transport, solvation, structural reorganization, and mechanics, enabling diverse electrochemical functions but making their internal states poorly represented by scalar descriptors such as voltage, charge, conductivity, or nominal doping level. This Review establishes a state‐centered framework that treats electrochemical operation as the writing, observation, reconstruction, and design of multidimensional, history‐dependent state trajectories. A problem‐specific minimal sufficient state basis is introduced to distinguish essential from redundant coordinates, while waveform history and spatial heterogeneity define when lumped descriptions remain valid. Optical, electrical, ion‐specific, gravimetric, structural, mechanical, and temporal readouts are analyzed as selective projections whose complementarity determines state observability and hidden‐state reconstruction. Within this framework, congruence, kinetic ordering, decoupling, observational degeneracy, and mapping drift become experimentally testable relationships rather than isolated phenomena. Electrochromics, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs), electrochemical memories, actuators, reconfigurable systems, and energy‐storage and conversion devices are then recast as technologies that select different trajectories through a shared electrochemical‐state landscape. The framework ultimately connects molecular structure, electrolyte, morphology, device architecture, and driving protocol to the inverse design of observable, controllable, reversible, and durable electrochemical trajectories.

title: Machine‐Learning‐Potential‐Driven Volcano Relationship in Grain Boundary Amorphicity and Ionic Transport of Antiperovskite Solid Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Ionic transport in solid‐state electrolytes is governed by interfacial disorder and local chemical environments, yet their microscopic design principles remain challenging because large‐scale interfacial kinetics are simulated using molecular dynamics (MD), where predictive design requires quantum‐level accuracy. Here, we use an actively learned machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) to bridge this scale‐accuracy gap in halide‐tunable antiperovskite solid electrolytes. By varying the local Cl − /Br − ratio and quantifying interfacial amorphicity and ion flux, we identify an MLIP‐driven volcano relationship between structural disorder and ionic transport. Cl‐enriched grain boundaries remain overly ordered, whereas Br − enrichment induces excessive disorder that disrupts migration. Intermediate halide compositions maximize ionic transport through moderately amorphous environments. Guided by this relationship, we design an anion‐engineered grain boundary through selective halide tuning. These results establish controlled anion segregation as a strategy for reducing interfacial resistance and highlight MLIP‐enhanced MD as a predictive framework for transport and disorder engineering in solid‐state materials.

title: Amorphization Unlocks Active Sites in Organic Small Molecules for Ah‐Level Aqueous Ammonium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The performance of most organic rechargeable batteries is strongly hindered by insufficient active site exposure arising from strong molecular stacking. To address this issue, an amorphization strategy is implemented to disrupt strong intermolecular π–π stacking in the small molecule 2,3,7,8‐tetraamino‐5,10‐dihydrophenazine‐1,4,6,9‐tetraone (TDT), thereby improving electrolyte accessibility and activating buried redox sites. Amorphous TDT exhibits a high specific surface area of 738 m 2 g −1 , delivers 242.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 , and retains 87.1% of its initial capacity after 817 cycles over 2900 h. In situ ATR‐FTIR and EQCM‐D measurements reveal that NH 4 + is preferentially adsorbed and stored through coordination and deprotonation, while interfacial NH 4 + accumulation induces localized hydrolysis to generate H 3 O + for subsequent proton storage. The TDT||CuFe‐PBA full cell retains 100% of its initial capacity over 100 000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . Moreover, the first Ah‐level AAIB pouch cell delivers 1.037 Ah at an average voltage of 1.14 V, demonstrating the practical promise of amorphous organic small molecule for durable, high capacity AAIBs.

title: A Novel pH‐Activatable Nanozyme for Treating Breast Cancer Bone Metastasis by Regulating Cancer Cell Metabolic Reprogramming and the Tumor Microenvironment
abstract: ABSTRACT Multi‐omics analyses implicate enhanced oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) in breast cancer bone metastasis (BCBM). To target this metabolic vulnerability, we develop SPMMPA, a bone‐targeted nanozyme comprising a Prussian blue core, a disulfide‐bridged mesoporous silica interlayer, and a manganese oxide shell, functionalized with polyethylenimine, alendronate, and the Ser‐Asp‐Ser‐Ser‐Asp peptide. Its acid‐enhanced catalytic activity promotes reactive oxygen species production and glutathione depletion, accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction, reduced OXPHOS and adenosine triphosphate production, and downregulation of peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor gamma coactivator 1‐alpha. Alendronate and silicon release contribute to reduced osteoclast activity and preservation of bone structure. Near‐infrared irradiation further enhances treatment efficacy through photothermal heating below 48°C. In mouse models of BCBM, SPMMPA suppresses tumor growth and alleviates osteolysis, without overt toxicity in the assays performed. These findings support a pH‐responsive catalytic strategy that couples disruption of tumor energy metabolism with protection of bone homeostasis.

title: Multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor for real-time blood monitoring
abstract: Accurate and real-time monitoring of blood electrolyte composition, particularly sodium (Na + ) and potassium (K + ), is crucial for guiding intraoperative and postoperative decisions, as these ions regulate critical bodily functions such as cardiac rhythm and fluid balance. Current blood analysis relies on ex vivo blood sampling, which introduces substantial time delays and can be susceptible to inaccuracies caused by temperature fluctuations. To address these challenges, we report here a multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor (MIFS) capable of monitoring Na + and K + ions in real time directly in the bloodstream. MIFS integrates three parallel liquid metal channels with a multilayer surface-electrode architecture, which synergistically enhances sensitivity, minimizes sensing drift, ensures mechanical flexibility, and offers outstanding biocompatibility for vascular implantation. In vivo testing in rabbit models and validation in human blood samples demonstrate MIFS’s superior sensing accuracy, real-time, and stable sensing in agreement with conventional ex vivo measurements. This work paves the way for real-time blood monitoring in clinical practice.

title: Spider-inspired bidirectional robotic joints driven by electrohydraulic multiaxial strain
abstract: Compared with conventional motors and servos, soft-actuated angular-motion devices are superior in environmental adaptability and human-robot interaction, yet they can only achieve active bidirectional angular motion by integrating antagonistic actuators or restriction modules. The integration of such components introduces deformation antagonism, compromises structural simplicity, and increases control complexity. Herein, we propose a spider-inspired centimeter-scale soft bidirectional robotic joint driven by a pair of synchronously controlled electrohydraulic actuators (EHAs). Specifically, the EHAs generate multiaxial strain, enabling the joint to bidirectionally rotate depending on its physical state, without introducing additional functional components or asynchronous controllers. Furthermore, the joint demonstrates (i) high-speed (forward: 2851° per second, reverse: 1934° per second) and wide-stroke (up to 156.8°) rotational performance, (ii) multimodal motion (e.g., self-unfolding, self-folding, and reciprocating swinging), (iii) continuous response (up to 40 hertz), and (iv) payload-bearing capability. Last, three joint-integrated devices validate its feasibility as a multifunctional, high-dynamic, and single-channel-controlled actuation component in diverse robotic applications. This work establishes a viable design framework for minimalist yet versatile bioinspired robots.

title: Bioinspired ventral-groove fibers for volume-programmable pneumatic actuation
abstract: Pneumatic actuation plays a central role in soft robotics, with conventional systems relying on pressure-driven chamber deformation and closed-loop feedback for precise control. Here, we introduce bioinspired ventral-groove filamentary fibers that reframe pneumatic actuation from pressure-dominated chambers to volume-programmable fiber architectures, enabling previously unexplored robotic capabilities. Coupling microgroove unfolding with elastic expansion, these molecularly programmed fibers achieve reversible 400× area expansion at ultralow pressure (∼0.8 kPa) and scale from ∼100 μm to centimeter-scale diameters and tens of meters in length, supporting micro- to macro-scale robotic systems. We demonstrate responsive textile actuation through an everyday flotation garment with 20-m fibers seamlessly integrated into clothing. We also show a gripping approach with three capabilities: disturbance-robust high-precision grasping, conformal handling of fragile nerve-like filaments and delicate incense-ash cones, and open-loop operation that reduces reliance on sensory feedback. By establishing a volume-programmable actuation paradigm, this work paves the way for low-pressure pneumatic technologies in soft robotics and responsive textiles.

title: Polycomb factor PHF19 affects AML initiation, patient prognosis, and survival
abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is marked by unchecked expansion of undifferentiated myeloid cells. Although oncogenic fusions such as MLL-AF9 can initiate disease, the early steps of leukemogenesis and the role of cell-intrinsic regulators remain unclear. We previously showed that the Polycomb-associated factor Phf19 is required for hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) maintenance and state control in mice and that its loss (Phf19 KO ) impairs HSC function. To define Phf19’s role in transformation, we expressed MLL-AF9 in Phf19 KO hematopoietic cells and performed integrated multiomic analyses. Phf19 deletion promoted acquisition of stemlike features and reduced responsiveness to differentiation-inducing AML therapies. Molecular and functional consequences of Phf19 loss paralleled those observed in the datasets of patients with AML. From these data, we derived a prognostic signature—PHFScore—which reveals previously unrecognized AML survival-correlating genes that robustly stratify patients across distinct cellular origins and leukemogenic stages, underscoring Phf19’s key role in AML biology and prognosis.

title: Scalable architecture for measurement-induced squeezed light interferometers
abstract: Scalable interferometers lie at the heart of photonic quantum technologies, but their expansion has been fundamentally limited by optical losses that grow with circuit depth. Here, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a measurement-induced architecture for multimode squeezed-light interferometers that overcomes this barrier. By shifting complexity from deep optical networks to programmable homodyne measurements, we realize effective transformations within a shallow, low-loss platform. We validate the principle with a six-mode device and extend it to a 400-mode interferometer, marking a leap in scale beyond conventional designs. Crucially, this strategy not only enables scalable squeezed light interferometry but also provides a powerful route to the generation of large-scale entangled states—a key requirement for quantum computing, simulation, and communication. Our results establish measurement-induced circuits as a practical pathway toward noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) applications and future demonstrations of quantum advantage.

title: Structural basis for start codon selection by eIF5-mimic proteins
abstract: Start codon selection extensively regulates the cellular proteome and is implicated in cancer and other diseases. The eIF5-mimic proteins (5MPs: 5MP1/BZW2 and 5MP2/BZW2) restrict non-AUG start codon usage and thereby reprogram proteoform expression from mRNAs with alternative start sites, such as the oncogenic c-Myc. Here, using in extracto cryo–electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biochemical assays, we report how 5MP represses translation dependent on the sequence context at start codons. Cryo-EM structures of 48 S preinitiation complexes (PICs) reveal 5MP1 bound at the A site of the small ribosomal subunit. 5MPs act as initiation factors that stabilize an open PIC conformation, promoting mRNA scanning and inhibiting initiation at suboptimal start codons. We propose to designate 5MP as eIF1S (eukaryotic initiation factor 1 scanning). These findings reveal the structural basis for proteome modulation by 5MPs and may help correct dysregulated translation in disease.

title: A methylation-dependent reader couples arginine methylation to S6K2 signaling in vivo
abstract: Arginine methylation regulates diverse cellular processes, yet how methyl-arginine reader proteins couple this modification to kinase signaling in vivo remains poorly defined. Here, we identify staphylococcal nuclease and Tudor domain containing 1 (SND1) as a pancreas-enriched effector that links symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) recognition to S6 kinase 2 (S6K2) activation. Disruption of SDMA-mediated binding by a point mutation in the SND1 Tudor domain markedly diminishes ribosomal protein S6 (S6) phosphorylation in the pancreas. Mechanistically, SND1 engages SDMA-modified arginines within the carboxyl-terminal glycine-arginine–rich (GAR) motif of S6K2 and promotes S6K2-dependent S6 phosphorylation. Mice harboring lysine substitutions at these GAR arginines ( S6k2 RK) phenocopy Snd1 Tudor-mutant ( Snd1 knock-in) animals, exhibiting impaired pancreatic S6 phosphorylation. Transcriptomic analyses reveal extensive overlap in dysregulated pathways between Snd1 and S6k2 mutant pancreata, supporting a shared signaling cascade. Together, these findings establish a methylation-dependent reader-kinase axis that links protein arginine methyltransferase 5–catalyzed arginine methylation to tissue-specific control of ribosome signaling and cellular stress adaptation.

title: Primary tumor–derived lactate primes prostate cancer cells for a dormant fate
abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. Here, we identify lactic acid (LA), a highly abundant environmental metabolite at the primary site in prostate cancer (PCa), as a key inducer of dormant state. LA-uploading PCa cells undergo a proliferation delay, associated with stemness, therapy tolerance, and invasiveness through the nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 1 (COUP-TF1/NR2F1) activation. These traits rely on LA-driven accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), which serve as reservoirs of lipid-derived acetyl moieties essential for histone acetylation. Notably, the epigenetic reader BRD4 is essential for COUP-TF1 expression and for establishing and maintaining dormancy. In metastatic sites, where LA levels are low, dormant features are lost, allowing DCCs to support metastatic growth. Last, targeting LA-mediated LD formation or BRD4 activation prevents dormancy entry, reducing PCa cell adaptability and increasing vulnerability to antiproliferative therapies.

title: NRF2 coordinates cystine import and glutathione use to sustain ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance in cancer
abstract: Cancer cells must balance detoxification of reactive metabolic by-products while preserving redox homeostasis, but how this trade-off is managed remains unclear. The Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1)–nuclear factor–erythroid 2–related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway, a key regulator of antioxidant defenses, is frequently hyperactivated in cancer. Formaldehyde, a genotoxic one-carbon by-product, is typically detoxified via glutathione (GSH), which is also essential for suppressing ferroptotic cell death. Here, we show that NRF2 promotes formaldehyde tolerance through up-regulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, enabling a protective mechanism that is largely independent of GSH, which remains necessary for ferroptosis resistance. In NRF2-active cells, formaldehyde reacts with cysteine to form a thiazolidine conjugate, and the combination of formaldehyde stress and SLC7A11 inhibition activates the integrated stress response, suppresses global protein synthesis, and markedly compromises cell viability. Together, these findings reveal that NRF2 coordinates ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance, exposing a cancer vulnerability through combined inhibition of cystine uptake and GSH synthesis.

title: Learning by moving: Physical motion accelerates category learning
abstract: Categorization is crucial for survival, helping animals forage, navigate, and avoid predators—all tasks involving movement. Yet, dominant theories of category learning treat it as a purely cognitive or perceptual process. Here, we challenge this view by demonstrating that physical movement can enhance category learning—but selectively. Using immersive virtual reality, we found that performing large actions, such as swinging a lightsaber, substantially improved learning of categories requiring integration of multiple cues (e.g., distinguishing aggressive from noncancerous lesions), while having minimal impact on categories involving independent evaluation of features (e.g., sorting by color and shape). This selective enhancement reveals a previously unrecognized motor contribution to categorization and may explain why prior studies missed it, opening avenues for optimizing training in critical categorization tasks.

title: A noncanonical meiotic cohesin complex associates with specific MCM complexes to promote cohesion establishment and homolog bias
abstract: A meiosis-specific cohesin complex is essential for the segregation of homologous chromosomes and sister chromatids during meiosis, yet its composition and mechanism in Drosophila remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate that SOLO directly interacts with SUNN, SSEP, and SMC1 and that these interactions are conserved between Drosophila melanogaster and Zeugodacus cucurbitae , a Tephritidae species within Diptera. SOLO associates with SMC1 via specific conserved residues within its highly conserved carboxyl-terminal domain. Furthermore, SOLO directly interacts with the MCM4 and MCM6 subunits of the MCM complex and with MMS22L to establish cohesion; consequently, postreplicative expression of SOLO results in a complete function loss. SOLO also interacts with the MEI-217 and MEI-218 subunits of the meiosis-specific minichromosome maintenance complex to promote homolog bias during meiosis. We propose that in Diptera, an evolutionarily diverged meiotic cohesin complex, composed of SOLO, SUNN, SSEP, SMC1, and SMC3, interacts with various complexes to fulfill its diverse meiotic functions.

title: SMCHD1 loss rewires MYOD1 enhancer nexuses and chromatin accessibility landscapes in muscle cells
abstract: SMCHD1 is a chromatin architectural protein linked to heterochromatin repression. Loss of function mutations of SMCHD1 cause facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy type 2 (FSHD2) through activation of the DUX4 transcription factor gene. However, it is unknown how SMCHD1 may regulate transcription independently of DUX4. Here, we show that SMCHD1 safeguards enhancer organization within the three-dimensional (3D) genome in human myoblasts. Loss of SMCHD1 leads to widespread gains in chromatin accessibility, aberrant transcription, and selective remodeling of myogenic transcription factor MYOD1 occupancy. Integrative analyses of histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, Hi-C looping, and enhancer-gene modeling reveal that SMCHD1 loss rewires the landscape of clustered enhancers and promotes the emergence of new networks of enhancer elements, termed MYOD1 enhancer nexuses. These structures are marked by increased enhancer connectivity, increased local 3D chromatin interactions, and coordinated activation of genes likely relevant for FSHD pathology. Our findings identify SMCHD1 as a key architectural constraint that suppresses hyperactive enhancer networks, thereby preserving transcriptional homeostasis in myoblasts.

title: Early Gravettian genomic data from Western Europe reveal population movements before the LGM
abstract: Anatomically modern humans first settled in Europe at least 45,000 years ago, yet limited genomic data from 45 to 20 thousand years (ka) constrain reconstructions of Upper Palaeolithic population dynamics. Before the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM; ∼26.5 to 19 ka), Gravettian groups (∼34 to 25 ka) were widespread across Europe and genetically diverse, including the Fournol and Věstonice lineages. Here, we present genome-wide data from three Gravettian individuals: two from the Franco-Cantabrian region (Chufín, Spain, and Isturitz, France) and one from Italy (Ostuni1b). Our analyses reveal previously undetected gene flow between eastern and western early Gravettian populations in southwestern Europe, challenging models of regional genetic continuity from the Aurignacian to the Solutrean (∼24 to 19 ka). To investigate population history during the LGM, a period for which human skeletal remains are extremely rare, we analyzed sedimentary ancient DNA from Solutrean Layer 122 at El Mirón Cave (Cantabria, Spain; ∼22,000 calibrated years before the present), recovering ∼14,000 human single-nucleotide polymorphisms. These data support persistence of Fournol-related ancestry in southwestern Europe throughout the LGM.

title: Gradient-interlayer–based flexible pressure sensors for high-performance robotic perception
abstract: Tactile perception systems based on flexible pressure sensors are indispensable for humanoid robots to perform dexterous manipulation, compliant interaction, and operation in visually challenging environments. Although strategies relying on surface or spatial microstructure engineering have improved sensor performance, the long-standing trade-off among sensitivity, sensing range, and linearity continues to hinder their practical deployment. Inspired by the gradient distribution of mechanoreceptors in human fingertip skin, we report a gradient-interlayer–based flexible iontronic pressure sensor (GriFIPS) in which a single direct-ink-written elastomeric mesh-like interlayer, with a centrifugal increase in aperture size, is placed between the soft electrode and an ionic hydrogel layer. Operating upstream of the functional layer, the mesh enables progressive, stage-wise contact under increasing load and decouples macroscopic contact-area evolution from the microscopic interfacial response. The sensor simultaneously achieves a sensitivity of 175.9 kPa −1 , a linear sensing range up to 360 kPa with a coefficient of determination of 0.997, a low detection limit of about 2.1 Pa, and a response time of about 25 ms, while remaining stable over 6000 loading cycles and 2000 cycles of 50% tensile strain. Building on this single-channel device, we further extend the architecture into a 3-axis gradient-interlayer–based flexible iontronic force sensor (3-axis GriFIFS) capable of resolving triaxial forces and surface textures. When integrated onto a dexterous robotic hand and combined with a temporal convolutional network, the sensors support tactile object recognition, fabric texture discrimination, human–robot interaction, and tactile-guided assembly, offering a generalizable route to tactile sensing for embodied intelligence.

title: PhagoID: Quantitative in situ proximity labeling defines the proteomes of bead- and microbe-containing phagosome lumina across species, maturation, and immune activation
abstract: The phagosome is an immune organelle that integrates signals from diverse cargos to drive pathogen killing, tissue homeostasis, and antigen presentation. How this compartment coordinates such diverse functions remains incompletely understood. A comprehensive view of phagosomal composition across cell states and perturbations could accelerate insight into its regulation. Here, we establish PhagoID, a modular proximity labeling approach that enables in situ proteomic profiling of the phagosome lumen in living cells. Applying PhagoID to murine and human macrophages, we define conserved and species-specific phagosomal proteomes that include both canonical lysosomal components and unexpected contributors from nuclear, mitochondrial, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) compartments. Integrating these proteomes with 25 genome-scale CRISPR screens of phagosomal phenotypes, we identify a network of lumenal proteins that regulate cargo uptake, acidification, antigen presentation, and microbial control highlighting previously unrecognized phagosomal effectors. We next adapt PhagoID to profile the microbe-containing phagosome and compare the sterile bead-containing phagosome to the Escherichia coli –containing phagosome, demonstrating a modest E. coli signature of phagosome remodeling. Comparative analyses further reveal that loss of LAMP1 enhances recruitment of ER-derived proteins to the phagosome, whereas loss of TFEB minimally perturbs the lumenal proteome despite its role in lysosomal biogenesis. Last, cytokine stimulation remodels the phagosome lumen to enrich for proteins involved in antigen presentation and antimicrobial activity in response to type I and II interferons. These data demonstrate that PhagoID delivers a high-confidence, quantitative, and integrative map of the phagosome lumen, revealing previously unidentified axes of organellar communication and regulatory control in innate immunity.
